title: Tesla Smashes Delivery Record with 308,600 Cars in Final Quarter
summary: Tesla announced record deliveries of 308,600 vehicles in the fourth quarter, exceeding analyst expectations and bringing its total 2021 sales to over 936,000, an 87% increase from 2020. This performance contributed to Tesla's market valuation exceeding $1 trillion, despite a global semiconductor shortage. The company plans to expand production with new factories in Austin and Berlin in 2022.

title: Apple becomes first $3 trillion company
summary: Apple Inc. became the first company globally to reach a $3 trillion market capitalization on January 3, 2022, showcasing strong investor confidence. The tech giant's shares hit a record $182.88 during mid-day trading before slightly dropping. This milestone follows Apple reaching $2 trillion in August 2020, driven by sustained demand for its products and services like iPhones, MacBooks, Apple TV, and Apple Music.

title: Tesla adds $144 billion to market value after record deliveries
summary: Tesla's shares surged 14% and its market value increased by $144 billion after the company announced record-breaking global deliveries of 308,600 vehicles in the fourth quarter, significantly surpassing analyst estimates. This "trophy-case" performance, as dubbed by an analyst, highlights robust demand and Tesla's ability to navigate the global semiconductor shortage, setting a strong pace for 2022. The electric car maker's annual deliveries in 2021 soared to over 936,000, an 87% increase from the previous year.

title: Tesla surmounts supply chain woes with blockbuster Q4 deliveries
summary: Tesla reported record quarterly deliveries of 308,600 vehicles in Q4, significantly surpassing Wall Street estimates and demonstrating its ability to navigate global chip shortages by ramping up production in China. The company's annual deliveries rose by 87% to 936,172 vehicles in 2021, driven by strong demand and strategic management of supply chain issues, including in-house chip design and software reprogramming. Despite challenges with new factory production and ongoing chip shortages, analysts expect continued growth for Tesla in 2022.

title: Apple becomes first company to hit $3 trillion market value, then slips
summary: Apple Inc. briefly touched a $3 trillion stock market valuation on January 3, 2022, becoming the first company to reach this milestone, fueled by investor confidence in its product pipeline and expansion into new markets like automated cars and virtual reality. Although its market capitalization slipped just below $3 trillion by day's end, the achievement highlights the company's strong fundamentals and consumer loyalty for its iPhones, MacBooks, and services. The stock has seen significant growth since the first iPhone launch in 2007, and under CEO Tim Cook, Apple has successfully diversified its revenue streams beyond the iPhone.

title: Setting Sights on Third-Gen Semiconductor Auto Power Modules! Diodes and Sentec Establish Joint Venture “DiodSent” - EnergyTrend
summary: Diodes and Sentec have formed a joint venture called “DiodSent” to develop third-generation semiconductor automotive power modules for hybrid and electric vehicles. The venture aims to combine Diodes' chip R&D with Sentec's thermal management expertise to enhance EV power modules. DiodSent plans to establish production lines in Shanghai and Taiwan, with an initial capacity of 100,000 modules, expanding to 500,000 within three years, targeting European and Chinese mini-vehicle markets and eventually international manufacturers like Porsche and Tesla.

title: Toyota Overtakes GM as Bestselling Auto Maker in U.S.
summary: Toyota Motor Corp. has for the first time surpassed General Motors Co. in annual U.S. sales, becoming the top-selling car company in 2021. This shift is primarily attributed to the global computer-chip shortage, which impacted car manufacturers unevenly. Toyota's U.S. sales reached 2.3 million vehicles, an increase of about 10% from 2020, outselling GM by approximately 114,000 units.

title: Explainer: How Tesla weathered global supply chain issues that knocked rivals
summary: Tesla managed to largely circumvent global supply chain disruptions that severely impacted other automakers by designing more components and software in-house, allowing for quicker adaptation to part shortages. The company demonstrated agility in substituting alternative chips and adjusting vehicle features, unlike its rivals who are more reliant on external suppliers and traditional manufacturing conservatism. Tesla's strategy of maintaining production forecasts and direct ties with chip suppliers also contributed to its ability to secure necessary parts.

title: Qualcomm inks car chip deals with Volvo, Honda and Renault
summary: Qualcomm announced deals to supply chips to automakers Volvo Group, Honda Motor Co Ltd, and Renault SA, accelerating its push into the automotive sector. The company will provide its "Snapdragon Cockpit" chips for digital dashboards and infotainment systems, aiming to help car manufacturers transform vehicles into rolling computers capable of over-the-air updates and generating recurring revenue. Qualcomm also unveiled a new chip and system, "Snapdragon Ride Vision System," for computer vision and safety features, utilizing technology from its recent acquisition of Arriver.

title: Volvo, Honda, Renault Sign Chip Deals with Qualcomm
summary: Qualcomm has secured deals with Volvo Group, Honda Motor, and Renault to supply chips for their upcoming vehicles, expanding its presence in the automotive industry. These partnerships will see Qualcomm's Snapdragon Cockpit chips and associated technologies used for infotainment systems, digital dashboards, and potentially autonomous driving, allowing automakers to offer advanced features and generate revenue through over-the-air updates. This move aims to transform traditional automakers into platform innovators, similar to Tesla's business model.

title: EXCLUSIVE Walmart arm did not deliberately remove Xinjiang goods, China exec tells analysts
summary: A Sam's Club executive in China denied that the Walmart-owned warehouse club deliberately removed products sourced from Xinjiang from its app, calling it "a misunderstanding." The representative stated that Chinese consumers couldn't find Xinjiang products because the app does not support searches based on place names. This comes amid controversy over alleged forced labor in Xinjiang, which has led to some Sam's Club members canceling their memberships in China.

title: U.S. Ford Motor Company Sales Down 17 Percent In December 2021
summary: Ford Motor Company reported a 17 percent decrease in U.S. sales for December 2021, totaling 173,740 units, affecting both the Ford and Lincoln brands. Despite the overall decline, Ford finished the year as America's best-selling automaker in Q4 and saw significant growth in electrified vehicle sales, up 121 percent from the previous year. New models like the Mustang Mach-E, Bronco, Bronco Sport, and Maverick contributed to 14.2 percent of Ford brand retail sales, turning quickly on dealer lots.

title: VISION-S Exhibiting at CES 2022, Entering a New Phase
summary: Sony announced at CES 2022 that its VISION-S initiative, which aims to evolve mobility, is entering a new phase. The company unveiled an SUV-type prototype vehicle (VISION-S 02) alongside its existing sedan prototype and detailed advancements in safety, adaptability, and entertainment features. Furthermore, Sony plans to establish a new operating company, Sony Mobility Inc., in spring 2022 to explore entry into the EV market.

title: Amazon makes deal with Stellantis for electric delivery vehicles
summary: Amazon has partnered with Stellantis for software collaboration and become the first customer for a new Ram electric delivery vehicle. This deal builds on an existing relationship where Stellantis has supplied Amazon with tens of thousands of delivery vehicles since 2018. The move highlights Amazon's ongoing investment in electric vehicle technology and its collaborations within the automotive industry.

title: VINFAST ANNOUNCES ITS ALL ELECTRIC STRATEGY AND FULL ELECTRIC VEHICLE LINEUP AT CES 2022
summary: VinFast announced its comprehensive all-electric strategy and full electric vehicle lineup at CES 2022, revealing plans to cease internal combustion engine (ICE) car production by late 2022 and transition entirely to EVs. The company launched five electric SUV models (VF 5, VF 6, VF 7, VF 8, VF 9) across segments A-E and opened reservations for the VF 8 and VF 9 with a special gratitude program for early customers. VinFast also introduced an innovative battery lease program and will apply blockchain technology for orders, reinforcing its commitment to sustainable mobility.

title: Nikola Motors drops its $2 billion lawsuit against Tesla
summary: Nikola Corp. has dropped its $2 billion patent infringement lawsuit against Tesla Inc., with both companies agreeing to withdraw all claims and counter-claims. Nikola had accused Tesla of copying several patented designs, while Trevor Milton, Nikola's founder, faces a criminal indictment on fraud charges following accusations by the SEC of deceiving investors.

title: China's Top Virtual Influencers on Social Media
summary: This article highlights the growing trend of virtual influencers, or Virtual KOLs, in China, a market that grew by 70% since 2017 to reach $960 million in 2021. It profiles five prominent Chinese virtual KOLs: Luo Tianyi, Ayayi, Angie, Ling, and the Honor of Kings Virtual Idol Group, showcasing their diverse characteristics, social media strategies, and collaborations with major brands. The piece emphasizes how Chinese virtual influencers leverage various social media platforms to connect with a large audience, particularly Gen Z and millennials, offering unique storytelling and commercial opportunities that could inspire the Western market.

title: Why Shares of ARK Innovation ETF, Affirm, Upstart, and SoFi Struggled This Week
summary: Shares of ARK Innovation ETF, Affirm, Upstart, and SoFi experienced significant declines this week due to hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve's December minutes. The Fed indicated potential interest rate hikes as early as March and a plan to shrink its balance sheet, which typically negatively impacts high-growth tech and fintech stocks. Rising bond yields, a consequence of these policies, make it harder to justify the high valuations these companies had achieved.

title: Machine Customers Will Decide Who Gets Their Trillion-Dollar Business. Is It You?
summary: The article explores the rise of "machine customers" and their potential to drive a trillion-dollar business opportunity. It outlines how these nonhuman entities, ranging from bound to autonomous customers, make purchasing decisions differently from humans by being transparent, processing vast amounts of data, and prioritizing efficiency over emotional loyalty. Businesses must adapt their corporate strategy, sales, marketing, and data analytics to cater to this evolving market.

title: VinFast unveils electric SUV trio in Las Vegas
summary: VinFast has unveiled three new electric crossovers: the VF5, VF6, and VF7, at CES in Las Vegas, aiming for global electric car market penetration. These new models, alongside the rebranded VF8 (formerly VF e35) and VF9 (formerly VF e36), feature common styling with LED driving lights and distinct body shapes. VinFast is adopting a unique pricing strategy in the US for the VF8 and VF9, which includes a battery leasing model, a 10-year/200,000km warranty, and competitive pricing against Tesla models.

title: John Deere Announces Farmer-Free Autonomous Tractor
summary: John Deere has announced a fully autonomous version of its 8R tractor, marking a significant step in the company's move towards artificial intelligence in agriculture. The tractor, unveiled at CES 2022, features advanced camera systems and neural net AI for obstacle detection and soil quality readings, operating similarly to self-driving cars but adapted for the simpler task of row-cropping. While this technology promises increased efficiency, it also raises concerns among activists regarding data ownership and farmers' control over information collected from their land.

title: Disruptive Growth Will Require Patience, but Potential Rewards Lurk
summary: This article discusses disruptive growth strategies, particularly focusing on the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), which faced a downturn in 2021 and early 2022 due to anticipated Federal Reserve rate tightening. Despite recent struggles, the article argues that the long-term thesis for disruptive technologies, addressing the fourth industrial revolution, remains intact. It highlights five major themes identified by RBC as future disruptors and notes ARKK's exposure to many of these areas through its holdings like Tesla (TSLA) and Shopify (SHOP).

title: GM To Use Qualcomm' Snapdragon Ride Platform For Advanced Driver Assistance Technology
summary: General Motors (GM) will incorporate Qualcomm's Snapdragon Ride Platform for its next-generation Ultra Cruise hands-free driver-assist system, making it the first to utilize this advanced technology. The system, featuring a powerful 5-nanometer SoC and AI accelerator, will be available in 2023 on Cadillac LYRIQ and CELESTIQ models. This move significantly enhances GM's autonomous driving capabilities.

title: Visteon Showcases Wireless Battery Management System
summary: Visteon Corp. showcased its smart wireless battery management system (BMS) for electric vehicles at CES 2022. This system replaces wired connections with secure communication technology, reducing assembly time, overall vehicle weight, and offering scalability across different vehicle segments. Visteon's CEO, Sachin Lawande, highlights how this innovation streamlines EV manufacturing and enhances the ownership experience.

title: Beam solar-powered off-grid EV chargers deployed worldwide
summary: Beam Global has successfully deployed solar-powered off-grid EV chargers in over 100 municipalities across the U.S. and internationally. These chargers are unique because they don't require construction or electrical work for installation, making them highly portable and useful in various locations, including after natural disasters. The company's innovative solution addresses the challenge of EV charging infrastructure by providing a flexible and rapidly deployable option.

title: Hesai Technology showcased new automotive-grade hybrid solid-state Lidar AT128
summary: Hesai Technology showcased its new automotive-grade hybrid solid-state lidar AT128 at CES 2022. This long-range sensor is designed for L3+ ADAS applications in mass production vehicles, featuring image-level resolution, superior ranging capability, and automotive-grade reliability, with mass production slated for 2022. Hesai also unveiled the QT128, a short-range lidar aimed at L4 applications, entering mass production in Q1 2023.

title: Cathie Wood's Ark portfolio is headed for a shipwreck — and plunging tech stocks aren't even the worst of it
summary: This article argues that Cathie Wood's ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) is overvalued and headed for significant losses, despite Wood's claims of deep value. The author contends that ARK's portfolio is heavily concentrated in high-risk growth stocks, many of which are unprofitable, and that the fund's investment strategy is antithetical to traditional value investing. The analysis calculates that "ARK Inc." (ARK Innovation as a single company) is generating annual losses and is unlikely to meet Wood's projected 40% annual returns, especially as competition erodes the profitability of key holdings like Coinbase.

title: Blink Charging Launches Seven Next-Generation EV Charging Products
summary: Blink Charging Co. unveiled seven new EV charging products and two new apps at CES, marking an unprecedented achievement for the company. These next-generation solutions cater to various sectors including home, fleet, multifamily, and retail, enhancing the EV charging ecosystem. The new offerings, including the MQ 200, HQ 200, Vision IQ 200, 50kW DC Fast Charger, Blink Mobile App, and Blink Fleet portal, aim to provide a more seamless, efficient, and affordable charging experience for consumers and fleets.

title: Here’s Why the UPRO and TQQQ Stock Prices Fell 50.1% Premarket Despite Calm Markets
summary: The ProShares UltraPro S&P500 (UPRO) and ProShares UltraPro QQQ (TQQQ) ETFs both fell about 50% in premarket trading. This significant drop was due to previously announced forward stock splits by ProShares, intended to make the shares more affordable to a wider range of investors, not due to market instability. The splits ensure the total value of investors' holdings remains unchanged, similar to traditional stock splits seen with companies like Apple and Tesla.

title: LG Energy Solution's IPO attracts around $80 bln bids from international investors - sources
summary: South Korean battery maker LG Energy Solution (LGES) has attracted approximately $80 billion in bids from international institutional investors for its $10.7 billion initial public offering (IPO), making it the largest ever in South Korea. The demand significantly oversubscribed the institutional offer, with sources indicating strong interest without price sensitivity. Once listed, LGES, a subsidiary of LG Chem and supplier to EV makers like Tesla and General Motors, is expected to become South Korea's third-largest listed company.

title: What's New With Electric Vehicles for 2022?
summary: The electric vehicle market is rapidly expanding for the 2022 model year, with new EVs from numerous automakers, including many SUV options to address consumer preferences. This article details a variety of new electric models coming to market, from luxury sedans and performance vehicles to trucks and family-friendly SUVs, highlighting their key features, range estimates, and starting prices. It also briefly looks ahead to anticipated EV releases for the 2023 model year.

title: As Stellantis turns 1, automaker faces two paths
summary: As Stellantis marks its first anniversary, experts predict two potential futures for the automaker: becoming a strong EV player like Ford or facing challenges similar to GM decades ago. Despite a strategic focus on electrification through partnerships and investments, the company has yet to launch a fully electric vehicle in North America and struggles with underutilized plants and profitability in China. CEO Carlos Tavares' leadership is seen as a key factor in navigating these challenges and transforming Stellantis into a sustainable tech mobility company.

title: Tesla Megapacks storage facility will provide backup power while reducing reliance on fossil fuels in Houston
summary: Tesla has unveiled a new Megapack battery storage facility in Angleton, Texas, designed to provide backup power and lessen dependence on fossil fuels. The project, consisting of 81 Megapacks, aims to mitigate the effects of power grid disruptions, similar to the near-collapse in February 2021. It could power approximately 20,000 homes on a hot summer day.

title: China to End EV Subsidies After 30% Cut in 2022
summary: China plans to completely withdraw subsidies for new energy vehicles (NEVs) by the end of 2022, following a 30% reduction in 2022. This policy shift, announced by four central ministries, is a continuation of a strategy to phase out direct subsidies that were initially introduced in 2009 to boost EV adoption and support local manufacturers. Despite concerns that reduced subsidies and chip shortages might increase EV prices and slow the market, increasing consumer appetite for EVs is expected to offset these effects, with China maintaining its target for NEVs to account for at least 20% of all automobile sales by 2025.

title: Do Electric Vehicles Have Transmissions?
summary: Electric vehicles generally do not have conventional multi-speed transmissions; most use a single speed because electric motors produce full power immediately and over a wide rev range. While single-speed EVs still have gears to transfer power, notable exceptions like the Porsche Taycan utilize two-speed transmissions, often for enhanced performance or efficiency at high speeds. This advancement, first seen in high-end models, may eventually become more common in less expensive EVs.

title: As India waffles on terms for Tesla, several states woo Musk
summary: Several Indian states are inviting Tesla to set up manufacturing facilities in their provinces, following Elon Musk's comments about ongoing challenges with the national government. These states, governed by parties opposed to Prime Minister Modi's administration, are offering incentives like infrastructure and streamlined approval processes. The overtures highlight the ongoing impasse between Tesla and the Indian government over local manufacturing and import duties.

title: Biden's green agenda requires batteries, but building them is dirty business
summary: President Joe Biden's green energy agenda, crucial for combating global warming and competing with China, heavily relies on lithium for batteries. However, securing this essential metal faces significant hurdles due to environmental concerns and local opposition to proposed mining projects across the U.S. While necessary for the transition away from fossil fuels, lithium mining is a "dirty business" with substantial environmental costs, leading to conflicts between federal ambitions, economic opportunities, and community resistance.

title: Electra Battery Materials (ELBM) - European Expansion a Possibility
summary: Electra Battery Materials (ELBM) is focused on building North America's only fully integrated, localized, and environmentally sustainable battery materials park, aiming to commission a cobalt plant in 2022 and expand into recycling, nickel processing, and precursor production. The company has secured funding, signed a significant tolling contract with Glencore, and plans to replicate its expansion strategy into Europe, focusing on cobalt and potentially standalone recycling plants. ELBM is also actively seeking OEM contracts and partnerships with PCAM manufacturers to strengthen its position in the EV supply chain.

title: About
summary: QuantumScape is dedicated to revolutionizing energy storage with its solid-state battery technology, aiming to power a decarbonized future, starting with transportation. Founded in 2010, the company has developed a patented solid ceramic electrolyte separator that enables fast-charging, long-lasting, and safer batteries by utilizing a lithium-metal anode. This breakthrough technology is designed to simplify manufacturing, increase energy density, and provide enhanced safety compared to conventional lithium-ion batteries.

title: Lucid Group’s (LCID) Lock-up Expiration Fears Prove To Be a Nothingburger as the Stock Opens in the Positive Territory
summary: Fears surrounding a potential sell-off of Lucid Group (LCID) shares following the expiration of a lock-up period for major investors proved unfounded, as the stock opened in positive territory. The article suggests this is due to the Saudi PIF's long-term investment strategy and Saudi Arabia's broader economic transformation plans, which heavily involve Lucid Group. Despite a calm opening, the options market still indicates some hedging flows and a slim possibility of selling pressure later.

title: TrueCar (TRUE) Founder's New Venture Will Get You a Tesla (TSLA) in 10 Minutes
summary: Scott Painter, founder of TrueCar Inc., has launched a new subscription service called "Autonomy" that offers Tesla Model 3 sedans for a flat monthly fee. This service aims to provide a new option for drivers who want to experience a Tesla without the commitment of ownership. Autonomy has already acquired approximately 100 Tesla vehicles for its program, which begins in California.

title: Accelerating EV Charging Installations
summary: Southern California Edison (SCE) is significantly increasing its electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, planning to install 8,000 new charging ports annually over the next few years. This initiative is part of an effort to address the availability barrier of EV charging stations, as highlighted by Edison International President and CEO Pedro Pizarro at the National EV Charging Summit. SCE's Charge Ready programs aim to support widespread EV adoption by providing charging options in various locations, including underserved communities, and for both light-duty and heavy-duty vehicles.

title: Electric Vehicle Market In India To Get A New Player Soon, FedEx Arm Starts Trials In Bangalore
summary: FedEx Express has announced the commencement of electric vehicle (EV) trials in India, starting in Bengaluru, as part of its global goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040. The trial will assess the vehicle technology's operational effectiveness, with plans to extend to Delhi if successful. This initiative aims to support e-commerce growth while significantly reducing fuel consumption and emissions in last-mile delivery.

title: Electric Vehicles and Getting Beyond Tesla
summary: This article discusses the growth opportunities in electric vehicles and the new transportation technology ecosystem, along with investment strategies. It highlights the role of the KraneShares Electric Vehicles and Future Mobility ETF (NYSE: KARS) in capturing this potential, projecting significant growth in EV sales and investment by 2040. The piece invites financial advisors to a webcast for more insights.

title: Behind GM, Ford’s aggressive new electric vehicle strategy is old-time financing: Cash
summary: General Motors and Ford are investing a combined $65 billion in electric vehicles, using their operating cash flow rather than borrowing to finance this transformation. This conservative financial strategy, supported by record auto industry profits, high car prices, and significant cost-cutting, reduces risk for the companies and has boosted their stock prices. This approach contrasts sharply with Tesla's strategy of repeatedly raising capital from stock and bond markets in its early years.

title: Warren Buffett has nearly caught up with Cathie Wood after the tech-stock guru vastly outperformed him in 2020
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway has nearly caught up to Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF in terms of performance since the start of 2020, narrowing the gap from over 200 percentage points to just 5. While Wood's fund soared during the initial pandemic tech boom, it has since fallen due to investors pulling out of growth stocks in anticipation of interest-rate hikes. This shift highlights the differing investment strategies of Buffett's value-oriented approach and Wood's focus on disruptive growth companies.

title: CES 2022 Recap: Tech Becoming More Accessible and Interoperable
summary: CES 2022 showcased significant advancements making technology more accessible and interoperable. Key trends included enhanced immersion in the metaverse with new AR/VR products, traditional auto OEMs committing to mass-market electric vehicles, and the emergence of a unified Internet of Things ecosystem through initiatives like Matter. The event highlighted a shift towards practical, everyday applications for emerging technologies, signaling potential disruptions in various sectors.

title: Elevated by institutional demand, crypto mining firms slide into public markets
summary: Major cryptocurrency mining firms are increasingly going public, driven by institutional demand and strong profitability. These listings, often via SPACs, provide investors with exposure to Bitcoin's growth without direct trading. Critics, however, raise concerns about sustainability and regulatory scrutiny, especially regarding the industry's high energy consumption.

title: GM to spend $6.6 billion on EV plant investments in bid to dethrone Tesla in electric car sales by 2025
summary: General Motors announced a significant investment of $6.6 billion in Michigan to boost electric pickup truck production and build a new EV battery plant. This move is part of GM's broader plan to invest $35 billion in EVs by 2025, aiming to produce 1 million electric vehicles in North America and overtake Tesla as the top U.S.-based EV seller by mid-decade. The investment is expected to create 4,000 new jobs and secure 1,000 existing ones, with Michigan becoming a key hub for EV innovation and manufacturing.

title: POSCO Kicks off Construction on an Automotive Steel Sheet Plant in China
summary: POSCO has started construction on a new automotive steel sheet plant in Tangshan, China, in a joint venture with HBIS Group. The plant, named Hagang Pohang, aims to have an annual production capacity of 900,000 tons and is expected to be completed by the end of 2023. This strategic move strengthens the supply chain for automotive steel in China, a market with significant growing demand.

title: In the Automotive Future, China Means Everything. Get Used To It.
summary: This article discusses the influential role of China in the global automotive industry's future, particularly concerning electric and autonomous vehicles. Driven by a "Tesla effect" and substantial government support, China's domestic EV market is booming, with sales of new electric vehicles more than doubling in 2021. The article highlights how Chinese companies are not only catching up in EV technology but also rapidly advancing in autonomous driving and even flying car development, positioning China to be a dominant force in the automotive landscape.

title: Tesla posts record earnings, sees supply chain issues ahead
summary: Tesla reported record quarterly revenue, surpassing Wall Street estimates, but anticipates ongoing supply chain challenges throughout 2022. Despite these hurdles, the company managed to deliver a record number of vehicles and started production at its new Austin, Texas factory. The electric vehicle maker acknowledges rising competition as more companies enter the EV market.

title: Tesla beats on earnings and revenue, says supply chain issues were 'main limiting factor'
summary: Tesla reported stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter results, with earnings of $2.52 per share and revenue of $17.72 billion, surpassing analyst expectations. Despite beating estimates, shares initially fell due to warnings that supply chain issues, particularly chip shortages, are likely to persist through 2022. CEO Elon Musk stated the company would not introduce new vehicle models in 2022, instead focusing on scaling production at new factories and advancing autonomous vehicle technology.

title: General Motors plans 8,000 new tech hires to power EV goals
summary: General Motors announced plans to hire over 8,000 new technical staff in 2022 to accelerate its development of electric vehicles and software-driven services. This move follows a $7 billion investment in Michigan for EV production and marks an intensified competition with rivals like Ford and Tesla in the North American EV market. GM also intends to expand its digital commerce with the launch of CarBravo, an online used vehicle market.

title: Wall Street gains evaporate, S&P 500 ends lower on Fed tightening timeline
summary: The S&P 500 ended lower after the U.S. Federal Reserve indicated it would soon raise interest rates to combat persistent inflation. All three major U.S. stock indexes swung wildly, with the Dow and S&P 500 closing in negative territory, while Nasdaq saw a nominal gain. The market reacted strongly to Fed Chair Jerome Powell's comments about inflation and supply problems being more severe and long-lasting than anticipated.

title: Tesla posts record profit, won’t produce new models in 2022
summary: Tesla reported record fourth-quarter and full-year earnings despite a global chip shortage, with $5.5 billion in profit in 2021. However, CEO Elon Musk announced that the company would not be rolling out any new models in 2022 due to the chip shortage, further delaying vehicles like the Cybertruck. Tesla's "Full Self-Driving" software is now being tested by nearly 60,000 vehicle owners, and Musk expects it to be safer than human driving this year.

title: Tesla won't roll out new models in 2022 because of chip shortages
summary: Tesla will not roll out any new models in 2022, including the delayed Cybertruck, due to the global chip shortage, according to CEO Elon Musk. Despite this, Tesla reported record fourth-quarter and full-year earnings, with $5.5 billion in profit for 2021 as vehicle deliveries soared. The company plans to focus on existing models and explore new factory locations, while its "Full Self-Driving" software is now being tested by nearly 60,000 users.

title: Jim Cramer says the SARK ETF is trying to benefit from the struggles of high-growth stocks
summary: Jim Cramer highlighted the Tuttle Capital Short Innovation ETF (SARK), which aims to profit from the decline of previously high-flying growth stocks, particularly those found in Cathie Wood's ARK Innovation ETF. SARK was up 38.23% year to date as of the article's publication, while the Nasdaq Composite was down 14.65%. Cramer suggests investors build core portfolios of profitable companies and consider SARK to hedge against continued struggles in growth stocks.

title: Cathie Wood's ARK buys the dip in Tesla shares after months of selling
summary: Cathie Wood's ARK Invest purchased 33,482 Tesla shares worth nearly $28 million following a significant slump in the electric-car maker's stock. This move comes after months of ARK paring back its Tesla holdings. Despite the recent dip, Tesla remains ARK Innovation's top holding, though its weight in the ETF has decreased.

title: General Motors Wants to Hire 8,000 Highly Skilled Workers, Technologists
summary: General Motors announced plans to hire 8,000 highly skilled workers, including software developers and computer scientists, in 2022 to boost its technological capabilities and compete with companies like Tesla. While GM aims to innovate, it faces challenges in attracting top talent due to lower compensation compared to tech giants and Tesla, possibly relying on benefits and perks instead. The automotive industry is increasingly investing in advanced car technologies, making the acquisition of skilled technologists crucial for future success.

title: Nio Is on a Battery Swap Station Building Spree
summary: Nio is aggressively expanding its battery swap station network, surpassing 800 stations in China and opening its first in Norway, with a goal of 1,300 by year-end. This strategy, previously dismissed by other automakers, focuses on a battery-as-a-service model, now gaining support from battery supplier CATL. CATL's entry into the battery swap market with a standardized, compatible battery could revitalize the technology, offering EV owners more flexibility in battery ownership and charging.

title: Tesla agrees to disable self-driving feature that runs stop signs
summary: Tesla has agreed to disable a "rolling stop" feature in its Full Self-Driving system after discussions with the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). The over-the-air software fix affects over 53,000 vehicles across several models from 2016-2022. Tesla claims no accidents have been reported due to this feature, which allowed vehicles to slowly pass through all-way stop intersections under specific conditions.

title: Cramer says he likes most of the Ark Innovation ETF's top holdings after growth stock meltdown
summary: Jim Cramer expressed his approval for many of the top holdings in Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF, believing that the recent declines in growth stocks have made them attractive buying opportunities. He advised investors to average into positions, buying more if prices continue to fall. Cramer specifically shared his outlook on five of the ETF's largest holdings, including Tesla, Teladoc, Zoom Video, Roku, and Coinbase Global.

title: Tesla recalls nearly 54,000 vehicles that may disobey stop signs
summary: Tesla is recalling 53,822 U.S. vehicles equipped with its Full Self-Driving (Beta) software due to a "rolling stop" functionality that may allow vehicles to pass through all-way stop intersections without coming to a complete stop, posing a safety risk. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) stated the recall covers various Model S, Model X, Model 3, and Model Y vehicles from 2016-2022. Tesla will issue an over-the-air software update to disable this feature, despite CEO Elon Musk claiming there were no safety issues with it.

title: Robots marched on in 2021, with record orders by North American firms
summary: In 2021, North American companies invested over $2 billion in nearly 40,000 robots, setting a new record for robot orders. The deployment of robots expanded beyond the automotive sector into various industries, including metals, food, consumer goods, and e-commerce, driven by labor shortages and increased demand. A new breed of "cobots" is also emerging, designed to work collaboratively with humans on assembly lines, addressing the need for automation in industries previously resistant to it.

title: TMUS Stock: 9 Reasons Why T-Mobile Investors Are Dialing Up Gains Today
summary: T-Mobile US (TMUS) stock is experiencing a significant surge after the telecommunications company released its fourth-quarter 2021 earnings report. Despite a slight revenue miss, diluted earnings per share surpassed Wall Street expectations, and a strong 2022 outlook, including projections for 5 million to 5.5 million postpaid net customer additions and significant merger synergies, contributed to investor optimism. The positive report has led to heavy trading activity, with TMUS stock up over 10% as of Thursday afternoon.

title: As Lincoln marks 100 years at Ford, challenges, opportunities loom in brand's 2nd century
summary: Ford's luxury brand, Lincoln, is celebrating 100 years and looking towards an electrified future, despite struggles to maintain market share in the U.S. against foreign luxury brands and Tesla. While domestic sales have declined, the brand has seen significant growth in China and aims for a fully electrified lineup by 2030, leveraging its heritage and strength in the SUV segment. Leaders are optimistic about future growth, focusing on digital connectivity and "effortless experiences" for customers.

title: Former Tesla worker sues company alleging abuse ‘reminiscent of the Jim Crow Era’
summary: A former Tesla manufacturing plant worker, Kaylen Barker, has filed a lawsuit in California, alleging that the company tolerates "rampant acts of racism" within its factories. Barker's suit claims she experienced escalating racist encounters and was subjected to racial slurs and physical abuse, which Tesla allegedly ignored until a coworker threw a hot tool at her. This case follows previous allegations of a racially hostile workplace at Tesla, including a significant damages award to former employee Owen Diaz.

title: General Motors (GM) Option Traders See Downside
summary: Despite General Motors (GM) reporting stronger-than-expected Q4 earnings and announcing significant investments in electric and autonomous vehicles, option traders are indicating a bearish outlook. While investors initially bid up the shares, recent option activity shows a shift from bullish to bearish sentiment, with traders selling upside calls and buying downside puts. This suggests an expectation of further near-term downside for GM stock, influenced by factors like supply chain constraints and a chip shortage.

title: Hertz hires a former Goldman Sachs finance chief as its C.E.O.
summary: Hertz has appointed Stephen M. Scherr, former chief financial officer at Goldman Sachs, as its new chief executive. Scherr, who spent nearly three decades at Goldman Sachs, will assume his role on February 28, taking over a company that recently emerged from bankruptcy. His appointment comes as Hertz plans to expand its fleet with 100,000 Teslas and aims for a formidable position in the future of mobility and fleet management.

title: Hertz names ex-Goldman finance chief Stephen Scherr as CEO
summary: Hertz Global Holdings has appointed Stephen Scherr, former Goldman Sachs CFO, as its new chief executive officer, effective end of February. Scherr replaces interim CEO Mark Fields and joins Hertz during a pivotal time as the company electrifies its fleet, including a significant deal to acquire 100,000 Tesla vehicles. This leadership change and strategic direction follow Hertz's emergence from bankruptcy and a strong rebound in demand.

title: Tesla says the SEC delivered another subpoena in ongoing conflict over Musk tweets
summary: Tesla revealed that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission issued a new subpoena to the company in November 2021. The SEC is investigating whether Elon Musk and Tesla have complied with their 2019 settlement agreement, especially concerning Musk's public tweets about the company. This ongoing scrutiny follows a Twitter "poll" by Musk in which he asked if he should sell 10% of his shares.

title: Tesla Q4 2021 Report Shows Major Year-to-Year Increases, Stable Growth in Solar
summary: Tesla reported substantial year-to-year growth in its solar business for Q4 2021, with 345 megawatts deployed in 2021, a 68% increase from 2020. Despite this, supply chain issues, particularly concerning chip manufacturing, are expected to hinder future growth in both vehicle and energy sectors. The company also faces new competition in solar roofing and controversial legislation regarding solar incentives in California.

title: Tesla charges up matching contribution for 401(k) plan
summary: Tesla has increased the matching contribution for its 401(k) plan. This move was announced by Rob Kozlowski on February 7, 2022. The article provides only the headline and author information, without further details on the specific changes to the 401(k) plan.

title: Tesla (TSLA) Reports Almost $2B Worth of Bitcoin Holdings in 2021
summary: Tesla reported holding almost $2 billion worth of Bitcoin on its balance sheet at the end of 2021, representing a 33% gain from its initial $1.5 billion investment. Despite this, the company faced $101 million in impairment charges throughout 2021 due to Bitcoin's price volatility, particularly as crypto markets experienced a downturn towards the end of the year and into 2022. Tesla remains bullish on digital assets, viewing them as both an investment and a liquid alternative to cash, and plans to adjust its holdings based on market conditions.

title: The biggest chip merger ever is dead. Here's why Nvidia dropped its bid for Arm and what's next.
summary: Nvidia's $40 billion planned acquisition of Arm has been called off due to significant concerns and opposition from its announcement. As a result, SoftBank now intends to take Arm public through an IPO. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that the company will continue to license architecture from Arm despite the deal's collapse.

title: Ferrari takes Qualcomm on board to tackle digitalisation
summary: Qualcomm Technologies and Ferrari N.V. have formed a strategic technology collaboration to advance Ferrari’s digital transformation. Qualcomm will serve as the systems solutions provider for future Ferrari road cars, leveraging its Snapdragon Digital Chassis for telematics, digital cockpit, and ADAS capabilities. Additionally, Qualcomm Technologies will become a premium partner for the Scuderia Ferrari Formula One team and the Ferrari eSports team, with the Snapdragon logo featured on the new F1 race cars.

title: We should never have sold Arm in the first place, says ALEX BRUMMER
summary: Alex Brummer argues that the 2016 sale of British chip designer Arm Holdings to Japan's Softbank for £23 billion was a "serious betrayal" of British technology. He criticizes former Prime Minister Theresa May's government and Cabinet Secretary Jeremy Heywood for facilitating the deal, which he views as short-sighted given Softbank founder Masayoshi Son's intent to use Arm as a bargaining chip rather than for long-term investment. Brummer suggests that following the collapse of Nvidia's £50 billion bid for Arm, the British government has an opportunity to correct past mistakes and bring Arm back to the UK as a public company.

title: Ford poaches former Tesla engineering director Alan Clarke
summary: Ford has recruited Alan Clarke, a former engineering director at Tesla, to join its team. This move highlights the competitive landscape between traditional automakers and electric vehicle pioneers in attracting top talent for future automotive innovations. The article, published in February 2022, emphasizes a strategic hire by Ford to bolster its engineering capabilities.

title: $ARKK, Shopify & Tesla’s PE – What’s Trending on YCharts?
summary: This article highlights the most popular stocks, funds, and economic data pages on YCharts in January 2022, based on pageview data. Key trends included interest in Tesla's PE ratio, Shopify's significant drawdown, and the ARK Innovation ETF's declining performance. It details the most viewed company and fund pages, as well as economic data trends like the S&P 500's P/E ratio.

title: KoBold Metals Raises $192.5 Million to Use AI to Find Battery Minerals
summary: KoBold Metals, a startup supported by Bill Gates and specializing in using AI to locate metals for electric vehicles, has secured $192.5 million in Series B funding. This round saw investments from Apollo Projects, Bond Capital, mining giant BHP Group Ltd., and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, aiming to bolster the supply chain for critical battery minerals. The company's technology is vital for sourcing elements like neodymium, dominated by China, as the U.S. and its allies seek to build their own supply chains.

title: Top Tesla engineer hired by Ford after 12 years with EV industry leader
summary: Ford Motor Co. has hired Alan Clarke, a top engineer who spent 12 years at Tesla, to join its advanced electric vehicle development department. Clarke will report to Doug Field, another former Tesla engineer who now leads Ford's advanced technology and embedded systems. This move is part of Ford's strategy to aggressively compete with Tesla in the electric vehicle market, bringing in new talent with extensive EV development experience.

title: Tesla's Bitcoin Investment Hits Nearly $2 Billion—Here's How That Compares To Billionaire Novogratz's Galaxy, Dorsey's Square And More
summary: Tesla's Bitcoin holdings reached nearly $2 billion by the end of December, despite a $101 million depreciation last year due to volatility. The company holds about 43,200 Bitcoins, making it a significant corporate holder, though still behind MicroStrategy. Tesla maintains that it believes in the long-term potential of digital assets but faces scrutiny regarding Bitcoin's volatility and accounting rules.

title: California sues Tesla for alleged discrimination, racial slurs at plant
summary: California regulators have sued Tesla Inc., alleging widespread racial discrimination and racial slurs targeting Black employees at its Fremont factory. The lawsuit, filed by the California Department of Fair Employment and Housing, claims Tesla ignored years of complaints, leading to a racially segregated environment where Black workers were subjected to derogatory terms and harassment. Tesla preemptively denied the allegations, calling the lawsuit "unfair and counterproductive," while the state seeks back pay, reinstatements, and punitive damages for affected employees.

title: Snow Lake Lithium is developing the world's first all-electric lithium mine to support EV industry in North America
summary: Snow Lake Resources Ltd. is developing the world's first all-electric lithium mine in Manitoba, Canada, aiming to supply the North American EV industry with sustainably sourced, carbon-neutral lithium. The company seeks a joint venture partner to process the raw lithium into EV batteries and intends to cut dependency on foreign supply chains. The project emphasizes environmentally friendly mining practices, utilizing hydroelectricity and electric mining equipment.

title: Tesla recalls over 500,000 U.S. vehicles to fix pedestrian warning sounds
summary: Tesla is recalling 578,607 vehicles in the U.S. due to concerns that its "Boombox" feature, which allows sounds to be played through an external speaker, could obscure essential pedestrian warning sounds. This recall, initiated after scrutiny from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), will be addressed through an over-the-air software update disabling Boombox functionality in Drive, Neutral, and Reverse modes. This is one of several recent recalls by Tesla involving software issues, highlighting increased regulatory attention on the company's features.

title: Tesla Stock vs. Alphabet Stock: Which Is the Better Buy Today?
summary: Morningstar compares Tesla (TSLA) and Alphabet (GOOGL) stock using proprietary metrics to determine which is the better investment. Alphabet is found to be undervalued and has a wider economic moat and lower uncertainty compared to Tesla, which is currently overvalued. Based on their ratings, Morningstar identifies Alphabet as the overall better buy today.

title: Federal prosecutors say a former HP worker scammed the company out of $4.8M and used it to buy a Tesla
summary: Federal prosecutors have accused Shelbee Szeto, a former HP employee, of scamming the company out of $4.8 million. Szeto allegedly routed corporate money to her personal bank account and used it to purchase luxury items including a Tesla, jewelry, and handbags. The complaint was filed on Friday, February 11, 2022.

title: Rivian stock surges after George Soros' fund disclosed $2 billion investment
summary: Rivian stock saw a significant surge after news broke that George Soros' fund had disclosed a roughly $2 billion investment in the electric vehicle manufacturer. The investment, revealed via a December 2021 report, contributed to a 12% jump in Rivian shares, although the exact timing and purchase price of the shares remain unknown. This positive sentiment was further bolstered by Amazon's previous investment and contractual agreement with Rivian for 100,000 electric vehicles.

title: South Korea probes Tesla on suspicion of exaggerating mileage
summary: South Korea's antitrust regulator is investigating Tesla Inc. over allegations that the company exaggerated the mileage specifications of its batteries. The Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) reportedly told Tesla that it misrepresented the mileage of some models, including the Model 3, particularly in cold weather. The KFTC plans to determine sanctions against the automaker.

title: Jaguar Land Rover, Nvidia ally in vehicle software arms race
summary: Luxury automaker Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has partnered with Nvidia to develop advanced computer brains and software for its vehicles launching from 2025 onwards. This collaboration aims to accelerate JLR's in-vehicle software development, enabling features like autonomous driving and parking, and providing more digital functions to drivers. The deal is a significant win for Nvidia in expanding its automotive industry presence and helps JLR compete with rivals like Tesla in digital technology.

title: NHTSA opens safety probe into 416,000 Teslas for 'phantom braking'
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has launched a safety probe into approximately 416,000 Tesla vehicles due to issues with "phantom braking." This investigation focuses on reports of unexpected braking incidents in certain Tesla models. The issue raises concerns regarding driver safety and the reliability of Tesla's advanced driver-assistance systems.

title: Elon Musk, Tesla attack SEC for 'unrelenting' harassment
summary: Tesla Inc. and Elon Musk have accused the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) of engaging in "unrelenting" harassment and an "endless" investigation. They claim this is to punish Musk for his outspoken criticism of the government and to potentially "chill his exercise of First Amendment rights." The accusation was made in a letter to a U.S. District Judge, asking for a "course correction" regarding the SEC's scrutiny, which includes a recent subpoena concerning compliance with a 2018 settlement related to Musk's tweets.

title: Tesla Falls in Consumer Reports Ranking After Design Changes
summary: Tesla Inc. dropped significantly in Consumer Reports' annual auto brand rankings, falling to 23rd out of 32 brands. This decline is attributed to poorly received design changes, such as revamps to the steering wheel and turn signal, and ongoing reliability issues. The Model 3 also lost its "top pick" status in the electric vehicle category to Ford's Mustang Mach-E.

title: Cathie Wood went on TV to defend her ARK funds’ bad performance. It didn’t go as planned
summary: Cathie Wood appeared on CNBC's Halftime Report to defend the poor performance of her ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), which was down 30% year to date. She asserted that the fund's holdings were "way undervalued" and that recent losses were temporary, despite the ARKK ETF declining significantly from its peak. The interview drew attention for its timing, a Zoom call interruption, and Wood's dismissal of the inverse SARK ETF.

title: China’s Baidu Launches Self-Driving Taxis in Densely Populated Shenzhen
summary: Baidu has launched its self-driving taxi service, Apollo Go, in Shenzhen, marking its first deployment in a densely populated Chinese urban area. The service uses 50 pick-up and drop-off stations and allows users to hail vehicles via a smartphone app. While human drivers are currently present for safety, Baidu plans significant expansion, aiming for 65 cities by 2025 and 100 by 2030, putting China at the forefront of autonomous vehicle development.

title: Sustainable Funds Landscape - Highlights and Observations
summary: The article highlights the continued growth and strong performance of sustainable funds in 2021, with nearly $70 billion in new investments and returns generally outpacing conventional funds. It emphasizes the need for greater transparency in sustainable investing, urging funds to clearly describe their approaches and impact beyond financial returns, an issue becoming more critical given the increasing investor interest. The author also delves into different types of sustainable funds and the importance of understanding their diverse strategies.

title: Best Electric Vehicle of 2022
summary: Cars.com has named the Tesla Model Y as its Best Electric Vehicle of 2022, citing its consumer-friendliness, roomy SUV features, impressive range, and reliable Supercharger network. The Ford Mustang Mach-E and Volvo XC40 Recharge Twin were also nominated. The Model Y is recognized for its significant role in accelerating EV adoption and Tesla's consistent product evolution through over-the-air updates.

title: Update: Envirotech Vehicles Picks Osceola for First US Facility
summary: Envirotech Vehicles, a zero-emission electric vehicle manufacturer, has chosen Osceola, Arkansas, for its first U.S. manufacturing facility. This $80 million investment is expected to create over 800 jobs and will initially focus on outfitting imported vehicles before transitioning to full manufacturing. Arkansas is becoming a hub for advanced, sustainable manufacturing, attracting companies like Envirotech Vehicles and Canoo due to its favorable business climate and access to transportation.

title: Cathie Wood’s ARK bet $400 million on 6 stocks this month, and it’s a disaster
summary: Cathie Wood's ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) invested approximately $400 million in six stocks in February, only to see these investments decline by 19% in just 15 trading days. The strategy involved "catching falling knives"—daring new bets and doubling down on previously favored stocks that had already fallen significantly. This approach has led to further losses for ARKK, underscoring the risks of investing in highly volatile, often unprofitable companies even after steep discounts.

title: DoD Awards $35 Million to MP Materials to Build U.S. Heavy Rare Earth Separation Capacity
summary: The Department of Defense has awarded MP Materials Corp. a $35 million contract to construct a heavy rare earth element (HREE) separation facility at its Mountain Pass, California site. This initiative aims to establish domestic HREE processing capabilities, supporting U.S. defense and commercial applications and strengthening America's supply chains. The project seeks to reduce reliance on international markets for these critical materials, which are essential for various technologies including electric vehicles and wind turbines.

title: Tesla: We’ll open our charging network for federal cash
summary: Tesla has proposed opening its Supercharger network to other electric vehicles in exchange for federal funding from the Biden administration's $7.5 billion infrastructure plan. While this move could significantly boost the nation's EV charging infrastructure, Tesla is also requesting federal money for existing Tesla-only stalls alongside new universal chargers, a condition analysts believe is unlikely to be accepted. The decision presents a tricky balance for Tesla between maintaining exclusive access for its customers and capitalizing on federal incentives to expand its charging business.

title: U.S. safety agency probes 1.7 million Hondas after braking complaints
summary: U.S. safety regulators are investigating 1.7 million Honda vehicles, including the 2018-2019 Accord and 2017-2019 CR-V models, due to numerous complaints of inadvertent braking. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has received 278 complaints, with six alleging minor injuries from collisions, and Honda has pledged full cooperation. This probe follows a similar investigation into 416,000 Tesla vehicles for unexpected brake activation.

title: SEC probes Elon Musk and his brother Kimbal over stock sales
summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Elon Musk and his brother Kimbal for potential securities law violations related to stock sales in Tesla late last year. The inquiry focuses on transactions made just before Elon Musk polled his Twitter followers about selling a 10% stake in Tesla, with Kimbal Musk selling 88,500 shares worth about $109 million a day prior to the poll. This investigation adds to existing tensions between Musk and the SEC, stemming from a 2018 settlement over his tweeting habits.

title: Here’s How Investors Are Positioned in the Options Market Ahead of Lucid Group’s Q4 2021 Earnings
summary: Ahead of Lucid Group's Q4 2021 earnings announcement on February 28, 2022, there is significant options market activity, particularly with put options attracting outsized inflows. While the overall Put/Call ratio has normalized somewhat, there was robust put-buying activity for the March 18, 2022, expiration, especially at the $30 strike price, indicating some investors are betting on the stock falling below $30. The company is expected to report substantial revenue for Q4 2021 based on Lucid Air Dream Edition deliveries and will also provide financial guidance for 2022, with delivery targets being a key focus for investor confidence despite a minor recall issue.

title: Consumers Energy to install 200 electric vehicle chargers by the end of 2023
summary: Consumers Energy plans to install 200 new electric vehicle charging stations across Michigan by the end of 2023, including 100 fast chargers, as part of its goal to power 1 million EVs by 2030. This initiative aims to expand charging options, particularly in rural areas, to facilitate longer EV travel and accelerate EV adoption in the state. The project complements broader efforts by Michigan lawmakers and companies like General Motors to invest in EV infrastructure and development.

title: Panasonic to begin mass producing new Tesla battery by end-March 2024
summary: Panasonic announced it will start mass production of a new, larger lithium-ion battery for Tesla by the end of March 2024 at a plant in Japan. This 4680 format battery is about five times bigger than current models, which is expected to lower production costs for Tesla and improve vehicle range. Panasonic plans to build two new production lines at its Wakayama factory for this purpose, with an estimated investment of 80 billion yen.

title: Steve Ivsan Joins Xos As Head of Program Management
summary: Xos, a manufacturer of battery-electric vehicles and powertrains, announced that Steve Ivsan has joined the company as Head of Program Management. Mr. Ivsan will be responsible for defining the product plan and roadmap, designing systems for efficiency, and managing programs, reporting to the COO. With nearly three decades of automotive experience, including roles at Tesla and Rivian, Ivsan brings extensive expertise to Xos during its growth phase.

title: What It Cost to Outfit 6 Homes With EV Chargers
summary: Cars.com outfitted six homes with 240-volt home EV chargers to understand the process and costs involved, finding an average installation price of $3,817, including the charger. The installations varied greatly in complexity and expense, from simple side-of-house mounts to elaborate projects requiring trenching, service upgrades, and even navigating homeowners' associations. The article details the specific costs and challenges for each of the six scenarios, highlighting that factors like home electrical service capacity, charger location, and the permitting process significantly impact the final price and time to completion.

title: Lucid Air production cut deflates company's valuation by billions
summary: Lucid Motors experienced a significant stock drop after announcing a reduction in its EV production by up to 40%. This news has led to a decrease of more than a third in the company's valuation so far this year, impacting its market standing.

title: EXCLUSIVE Ford set to announce plans to run EV, ICE as separate businesses -sources
summary: Ford Motor Co. plans to announce a reorganization to run its electric vehicle (EV) and internal-combustion engine (ICE) units as separate businesses. This strategic move aims to accelerate EV growth and potentially allow for separate financial reporting down the line, although CEO Jim Farley has stated there are currently no plans for a full spinoff. The company seeks to improve profit margins in both divisions by cutting costs in ICE and investing more in EV development.

title: Focus: Big U.S. auto dealers bet billions against the death of the dealership
summary: U.S. auto dealerships are experiencing a record-setting acquisition spree, with transactions totaling $8 billion last year, triple the amount in 2020. This trend indicates a consolidation of ownership among car dealers, despite predictions that online sales would render traditional dealerships obsolete. Large public and private retail chains are buying out smaller, family-controlled operations, leveraging economies of scale to invest in technology and adapt to evolving consumer behaviors, while maintaining a stable number of physical dealership locations nationwide.

title: Is ARK Innovation a Growth Fund or a Value Fund?
summary: Cathie Wood describes her ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) as a "deep value fund" due to recent stock declines, but Morningstar's analysis, based on its Style Box metrics, still classifies ARKK as a growth fund. While many of ARKK's holdings are currently trading below Morningstar's fair value estimates, their underlying growth profiles mean they do not fit the criteria for value stocks according to Morningstar's methodology. Despite significant price contractions, ARKK's portfolio retains a strong growth orientation.

title: Ford reveals radical plan to restructure automaker into three business units
summary: Ford is restructuring its operations into three distinct business units: Ford Blue for traditional internal combustion engines, Ford Model e for electric vehicles and connectivity, and its existing commercial arm. This strategic move aims to enhance the automaker's competitiveness against industry leaders like Tesla in the electric vehicle market. CEO Jim Farley stated that the change is designed to make the 118-year-old company more agile and focused.

title: Ford announces it will split electric and gas vehicle manufacturing into different business units
summary: Ford Motor Company announced plans to separate its electric vehicle business into a distinct unit called Ford Model e, while its traditional internal combustion engine vehicles will operate under Ford Blue. This strategic move aims to attract investments, fund the transition to electric vehicles with profits from gas-powered cars, and recruit new talent, despite calls from some investors for a full spin-off of the EV business. The company intends to invest $5 billion in its electric vehicles this year, doubling last year's investment, to capitalize on the perception of being a technology company.

title: Wipro PARI riding the industrial automation wave
summary: Wipro PARI, a manufacturing automation company, is experiencing significant growth due to the automation of assembly lines for electric vehicles (EVs) globally, executing over 20 projects. The company, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Wipro Infrastructure Engineering since 2021, is expanding its presence in the US and Europe, focusing on the burgeoning EV market and aiming to be a top 10 discrete automation solutions provider worldwide. Wipro PARI's clientele includes major global auto manufacturers, and 75% of its revenues come from export markets.

title: General Motors Announces Jeffrey Morrison to Lead Global Purchasing and Supply Chain
summary: General Motors has appointed Jeffrey (Jeff) Morrison as vice president, Global Purchasing and Supply Chain, effective April 1. Morrison, who has over 25 years of experience in the automotive industry and previously led GM's global electrified vehicle hardware development, replaces Shilpan Amin. This appointment is strategic for GM as it focuses on strengthening its electric vehicle supply chain and fostering improved relationships with suppliers.

title: Musk challenges UAW to seek organizing vote at Tesla's California plant
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has publicly challenged the United Auto Workers (UAW) to organize a union vote at the company's California plant, stating Tesla would not interfere. This challenge comes after President Biden's State of the Union address, which highlighted unionized automakers but omitted Tesla, and amid discussions of potential federal subsidies for union-made EVs that could disadvantage Tesla. Experts suggest Musk's invitation is a strategic move to highlight his belief that Tesla's employees are well-compensated and won't unionize, potentially also benefiting the company's international operations in regions with stronger union support.

title: Grupo México de Larrea y Telesites de Slim impulsan cierre ganador de la BMV
summary: The Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV) closed with gains, driven by companies like Grupo México and Telesites, as oil prices receded. In contrast, Wall Street indices ended lower, and oil prices also fell due to investor concerns about inflation, Federal Reserve policy, and the impact of the Russia-Ukraine conflict on commodity markets. The article also details the performance of various companies on both the BMV and Wall Street, as well as the impact on global markets and bond yields.

title: Emerson Expands In Round Rock, CyberLandr Moves To Austin
summary: Emerson is investing $9 million and creating at least 50 new jobs in Round Rock, Texas, to expand its operations. Meanwhile, Stream It, Inc. has moved its CyberLandr research and development facility to Austin, Texas, to further develop its innovative RV/camper designed for Tesla's Cybertruck, having already raised over $540,000 in crowdfunding and $110 million in preorders. Both companies are contributing to economic growth and job creation in the Central Texas region.

title: Ford's plan to cut $3B in waste will funnel money from gas vehicles to fund electric, tech
summary: Ford Motor Co. announced a major reorganization, splitting its operations into "Ford Model e" for electric vehicles and "Ford Blue" for gas-powered vehicles. CEO Jim Farley revealed plans to cut $3 billion from the gas vehicle division over the next two to three years and reallocate it to electric vehicle development and technology. While executives aim for greater efficiency and innovation, the move has sparked anxiety among employees regarding potential job impacts.

title: Ford finally makes use of denying Tesla its ‘Model E'
summary: Ford has named its new EV unit "Model e," a name it previously prevented Tesla from using eight years ago. This move allows Ford to finally utilize the moniker it legally secured, prompting Tesla to change its desired "Model E" to "Model 3" for one of its vehicles. The article also includes several featured stories covering diverse topics such as Trump's tariffs, dealership buy-sells, and Jeffrey Epstein's interest in Carlos Ghosn's arrest.

title: E.C.D. Builds the Classic Defender of Your Fantasies
summary: E.C.D. Automotive Design, formerly East Coast Defenders, has grown into a significant bespoke vehicle business, restoring and customizing Land Rovers, including a new Tesla-powered electric drivetrain option. The company emphasizes quality, efficiency, and extensive customer customization, producing high-end Defenders that blend classic charm with modern amenities. Despite the high price tag, E.C.D. offers an exclusive and well-executed driving experience that new SUVs cannot replicate.

title: Tesla fights shareholder push to ditch carbon-rich crypto
summary: Tesla is seeking SEC approval to avoid a shareholder vote on a proposal to liquidate its cryptocurrency holdings due to environmental and volatility concerns. The proposal, filed by an Icelandic investor, criticizes the energy consumption of bitcoin mining and its reliance on fossil fuels, calling it a setback for Tesla's sustainability mission. Tesla argues the resolution is unnecessary and overly prescriptive, citing CEO Elon Musk's efforts to reduce crypto's carbon footprint and referring to crypto investments as a hedge against inflation.

title: General Motors, PG&E pilot vehicle-to-home technology
summary: General Motors and Pacific Gas and Electric Company are launching a pilot program to test vehicle-to-home (V2H) technology, allowing EV owners to use their cars as backup power during outages. The program will involve bidirectional charging technology and aims to make power outages "invisible" by utilizing mobile EV batteries. This initiative addresses the need for energy storage as more automakers adopt electrification and utility providers face challenges like preventing wildfires with power shut-offs.

title: Tesla's Musk seeks to end SEC muzzle on tweets, could face uphill battle
summary: Elon Musk has asked a federal judge to terminate his 2018 agreement with the SEC that requires some of his tweets to be pre-vetted by a lawyer. His lawyers claim the SEC's actions have become harassment and infringe on his right to free speech. Legal experts suggest Musk faces an uphill battle as courts generally uphold consent decrees and grant considerable leeway to the SEC in enforcing subpoenas.

title: Amazon announces 20-for-1 stock split, $10 bln share buyback
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has announced a 20-for-1 stock split and authorized a $10 billion share buyback plan, causing its shares to rise by 7% in extended trading. This marks Amazon's first stock split since 1999, aimed at making shares more accessible to investors and increasing flexibility for employees managing equity. Trading with the new share price will commence on June 6.

title: Novonix Borrows $1M For Burnside Facility
summary: Novonix Battery Testing Solutions, which originated from research at Dalhousie University, has secured a $1 million loan from the Atlantic Canada Opportunities Agency (ACOA). This funding will enable the company to purchase specialized equipment for its production facility in Burnside Industrial Park, intended to pilot a new method for cathode material production. Novonix CEO Chris Burns highlighted that the contribution will accelerate their efforts to demonstrate the scalability of their cathode synthesis technology.

title: Why Hasn’t Cathie Wood’s ARK Fund Invested in Quantum Computing or Quantum Technologies?
summary: This article questions why Cathie Wood's ARK Fund, known for investing in disruptive innovations, has not invested in quantum computing or quantum technologies, despite the industry fitting ARK's investment criteria. It explores potential reasons such as the nascent and highly theoretical nature of the quantum industry, and lack of clear commercial viability from ARK's perspective. The author concludes that based on publicly available criteria, the quantum industry appears to be a suitable investment for ARK.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Approves 20-for-1 Stock Split, $10B Buyback
summary: Amazon's board of directors approved a 20-for-1 stock split and a $10 billion share buyback. This marks Amazon's first stock split since 1999 and is intended to make shares more accessible to a broader range of investors and employees. Other major tech companies like Apple, Tesla, and Alphabet have also undertaken stock splits recently.

title: ANZ Petroleum Brings 7-Eleven Store Format to New England
summary: ANZ Petroleum has brought 7-Eleven's newest store format to New England with a 5,230-square-foot store in Danbury, Conn. The location includes a drive-thru, Laredo Taco Company QSR, indoor seating, and six fuel dispensers. The project was the result of ANZ Petroleum acquiring the site in 2019 following a terminated Cumberland Farms contract, with assistance from Petroleum Equity Group.

title: BNY Mellon taps next CEO
summary: BNY Mellon has announced its next CEO. The article title "BNY Mellon taps next CEO" and mentions Thomas P. “Todd” Gibbons and Robin Vince, indicating a leadership change at the company.

title: Amazon announces 20-for-1 stock split
summary: Amazon announced a 20-for-1 stock split, following similar moves by other major tech companies like Alphabet, Apple, and Tesla. The article explains that a stock split divides existing shares into multiple, smaller-priced shares without changing the overall value of an investor's holdings or the company's market capitalization. Stock splits are often done to increase a stock's liquidity and make it more accessible to a wider range of investors, though in an era of fractional shares, some of the practical impact is diminished.

title: Amazon surges as stock split, buyback excite investors
summary: Amazon's stock surged over 5% after the company announced a 20-for-1 stock split and a $10 billion share buyback, aiming to attract more investors and boost confidence. This move follows a period of lackluster performance for the e-commerce giant, despite its substantial growth since its IPO. The stock split, the first since 1999, and the buyback are seen as psychological boosts and a signal that management views the stock as undervalued.

title: CERAWEEK PG&E partners with Ford Motor on bidirectional EV charging
summary: California utility PG&E Corp is partnering with Ford Motor Co to bring bidirectional charging electric vehicles (EVs) to its customers, allowing EVs like the Ford F-150 Lightning to power homes for several days. This pilot program aims to test how these vehicles can support grid reliability by providing backup power. Ford CEO Jim Farley stated that the company plans to make most of its EVs bidirectional, distinguishing its approach from Tesla's due to its energy business.
