Despite the pressing demand for critical minerals like copper, lithium, and nickel, the industry struggles to attract investment, streamline government approvals, and overcome its negative public image. Experts emphasize the urgent need for a shift in perception and policy to prevent raw material shortages that could hinder the energy transition.

title: Tesla recalls cars for overheating issue—of screens, not battery packs
summary: Tesla is recalling 129,960 vehicles, including 2021-2022 Model S and Model X, and 2022 Model 3 and Model Y, due to an overheating infotainment CPU during fast charging. This issue can cause screen lag or restarts, and is considered a safety concern because of the rearview camera feed. Tesla plans to address this with an over-the-air software update.

title: U.S. judge says Musk recklessly tweeted that 'funding secured' for taking Tesla private
summary: A U.S. judge has ruled that Elon Musk's 2018 tweets claiming "funding secured" to take Tesla private were inaccurate and reckless, as there was no concrete financing from Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund at the time. This pre-trial decision marks a significant win for investors suing Musk for allegedly inflating Tesla's stock prices with false statements. The ruling determines Musk knowingly made false statements, leaving the determination of damages to shareholders for an upcoming jury trial.

title: Netflix and TikTok Cultures Reveal the Dark Side of Innovation
summary: This article explores the demanding work cultures at highly innovative companies like Netflix and TikTok, highlighting the "dark side of innovation." It discusses how the relentless pursuit of growth and excellence leads to long hours, poor work-life balance, and employee burnout, despite the prestige and career opportunities offered. The article contrasts the inspiring public image of innovation with the personal costs borne by employees in these fast-paced environments.

title: Exclusive: Tesla puts India entry plan on hold after deadlock on tariffs
summary: Tesla Inc. has temporarily halted its plans to sell electric cars in India due to a persistent disagreement with the Indian government over import tariffs. The company had failed to secure lower import taxes for its vehicles, prompting it to abandon its search for showroom space and reassign some of its India team members. The Indian government insists on local manufacturing commitment before it will reduce tariffs.

title: Electric Tractors Tackle Off-Highway Jobs
summary: The agricultural and construction industries are seeing a shift from traditional diesel engines to electric drivetrains for tractors and other off-highway equipment. This transition is driven by changing emission standards, the benefits of quieter operation, and instant torque. Major manufacturers like John Deere, CNH Industrial, and Volvo Construction Equipment, alongside startups like Monarch Tractor and Solectrac, are investing heavily in developing battery-powered machinery, leveraging EV technologies from the automotive industry.

title: Bill Gates Sells $940 Million of CN Rail Stock
summary: Bill Gates' investment firm, Cascade Investment, sold approximately $940 million worth of Canadian National Railway Co. shares between April 27 and May 12, reducing its stake in the company to about 9%. This sale is part of an ongoing reduction in ownership since May 2021. Gates' former wife, Melinda French Gates, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation also sold significant portions of their Canadian National shares.

title: Tesla targets Silver Spring for new service center
summary: Tesla Inc. is planning to open a new service center in Silver Spring, Maryland, expanding its presence in the Greater Washington area. The electric automaker will lease a single-story office building for this new facility. This move signifies Tesla's continued growth and investment in its service infrastructure.

title: 10 Things You Need To Know About XPeng Motors
summary: XPeng Motors, an EV startup founded in 2014, has rapidly grown, delivering 98,000 cars in 2021 with 263% year-on-year growth. Originally focusing on the Chinese market, the company is now expanding into Europe and potentially the US, offering a range of electric vehicles from SUVs like the G9 to sedans like the P7, many equipped with advanced self-driving technology. Despite facing significant competition, XPeng aims to become a major player in the global EV market.

title: Here's How GM Plans to Knock Tesla Off Its Pedestal
summary: General Motors (GM) aims to surpass Tesla in EV sales by mid-decade, with CEO Mary Barra stating GM will sell more EVs than any other manufacturer in the U.S. The strategy focuses on offering more affordable EV options, including the upcoming Equinox EV priced around $30,000, to compete with Tesla's higher price points. While Tesla currently dominates the market, GM and other legacy automakers are ramping up EV production to challenge its lead, especially with affordable trucks and SUVs.

title: 꿈을 먹고 자란 주식 '하락'에 베팅했더니…연초 대비 96% 수익률
summary: 미국 성장주에 집중 투자하는 '아크 이노베이션 ETF(ARKK)'의 올해 수익률이 연초 대비 57% 하락하면서, 이들 성장주의 하락에 베팅하는 상장지수펀드(ETF)들이 주목받고 있다. 특히, ARKK의 일일 등락폭을 기준으로 -1배 수익을 내도록 설계된 '터틀캐피탈 숏 이노베이션 ETF(SARK)'는 연초 대비 89% 상승했다. 스팩(SPAC) 합병을 통해 상장한 기업들을 추종하는 ETF의 하락에 베팅하는 '더 숏 디-스팩 ETF(SOGU)'도 연초 대비 96%의 수익률을 기록했다.

title: Tesla delays plan to restore Shanghai output to pre-lockdown levels
summary: Tesla has postponed its plan to restore production at its Shanghai plant to pre-lockdown levels by at least a week due to ongoing COVID-19 restrictions. The company now aims to increase daily output to 2,600 units from May 23, having maintained a single shift producing around 1,200 units daily for the current week. Challenges include difficulties doubling the workforce for "closed-loop" operations and uncertainties in supplier and logistics restoration.

title: China regulator says Tesla recalling 107,293 China-made Model 3, Model Y vehicles
summary: China's market regulatory agency has announced that Tesla is recalling 107,293 China-made Model 3 and Model Y vehicles. The recall is due to a potential overheating issue that can cause the center touchscreen display to malfunction. This overheating could also lead to other problems, including issues with windshield settings and gear displays.

title: GM is betting its Ultium batteries will lead the automaker to EV dominance
summary: General Motors is making a significant investment in electric vehicle technology, specifically with its new Ultium platform, to become a leader in the EV market. The Ultium platform, centered around uniquely designed batteries developed with LG Energy Solutions, aims to reduce cobalt usage by 70% and lower battery pack costs, making EVs more competitive. GM believes these innovations will enable them to dominate the North American EV market by 2025, challenging current leader Tesla.

title: Why S&P booted Tesla from its ESG index
summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices removed Tesla from its S&P 500 ESG Index due to a decline in its ESG rank compared to global peers. Despite Tesla's role in the transition to electric vehicles, the decision was influenced by claims of racial discrimination, poor working conditions at its factory, and its handling of a federal investigation into autopilot-related deaths. Elon Musk called ESG an "outrageous scam" in response to the decision.

title: Tesla dumped by S&P ESG index as Musk calls label a ‘scam’
summary: Tesla has been removed from the S&P 500 ESG Index due to concerns regarding working conditions, its handling of investigations into driver-assistance system deaths, and a lack of low-carbon strategy and business conduct codes. While S&P Dow Jones Indices noted Tesla's ESG score remained "fairly stable," it slipped against improving global peers. CEO Elon Musk subsequently criticized ESG as a "scam" and "fundamentally flawed," stating it has been "weaponized by phony social justice warriors."

title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as Target and growth stocks sink
summary: Wall Street closed sharply lower on Wednesday after Target's stock plummeted by about a quarter of its value, exposing concerns about the U.S. economy due to surging prices. This marked the worst one-day loss for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average since June 2020, as inflation continued to erode consumer purchasing power, impacting retailers and prompting a market sell-off. Megacap growth stocks also contributed to the decline, with the Nasdaq falling significantly, amidst broader economic worries including rising inflation, supply chain issues, and central bank tightening.

title: Innovation Meets Productivity at AGCO Jackson Campus
summary: The article highlights the AGCO Jackson campus as a world-class manufacturing facility for agricultural machinery, emphasizing its focus on innovation, productivity, and a strong employee culture. It details why Jackson, Minnesota, was chosen for the plant, the importance of its workforce in agricultural production, and how the company is adapting to new challenges like supply chain issues and evolving market trends by prioritizing "farmer first" solutions and behavioral hiring.

title: AC Hotels by Marriott developer buys land in St. Johns Town Center
summary: OTO Development LLC, the developer behind the AC Hotels by Marriott project in St. Johns Town Center, has purchased 2.725 acres of land for $1.18 million. The four-story, 118-room hotel, costing an estimated $18 million, is scheduled to start construction in the first quarter of 2022 and be completed in the second quarter of 2023. This project is a joint venture between OTO and Simon Property Group, with OTO serving as the managing partner.

title: Musk's ESG attack spotlights $35 trillion industry confusion
summary: Elon Musk's criticism of ESG scores, particularly after Tesla was removed from S&P's ESG index, highlights growing confusion and disagreement within the $35 trillion sustainable investing industry. While some believe ESG should reward companies actively doing good for the environment and society, others, including rating agencies, view it as a tool to assess a company's risk exposure to ESG factors. This divergence in understanding means that companies contributing to climate change can still be included if they show efforts to mitigate ESG risks, contrasting with Musk's perspective that Tesla, despite its environmental contributions, was penalized for other issues like working conditions.

title: 10 Most Valuable Car Companies On The Planet
summary: This article lists the 10 most valuable car companies globally as of December 2022, highlighting the significant market shifts caused by companies like Tesla and Rivian. It details each company's origins, key brands, and market valuation, emphasizing the automotive industry's evolving landscape with the rise of electric vehicles. Tesla leads the list, underscoring the dramatic growth of innovative new entrants compared to traditional automakers.

title: A superstar investor with the Midas touch or just lucky? The puzzle of Cathie Wood
summary: Cathie Wood, CEO of ARK Invest, became a superstar investor during the pandemic with her ARK Innovation ETF returning 150% in 2020. However, her funds are struggling significantly in 2022, leading to questions about her investment strategy and whether her past success was due to skill or luck. Despite criticism and poor performance, Wood remains confident, advocating for a five-year investment horizon and continuing to attract new investor money.

title: Rosenbluth Discusses ESG, Tesla, and More on Bloomberg
summary: Todd Rosenbluth recently appeared on Bloomberg to discuss various ETF-related topics, including the growing appeal of low-cost bond ETFs over mutual funds, defensive and factor investing strategies, and specific ETF rebalances. He also addressed why Tesla was dropped from the S&P 500 ESG index, emphasizing the differentiation between environmental, social, and governance factors. Rosenbluth highlighted the importance of looking beyond labels for ESG ETFs, as they can differ significantly.

title: Todd Rosenbluth Talks ESG, Tesla, and More on Bloomberg
summary: Todd Rosenbluth discussed the shifts in bond fund flows, the rise of defensive and value investment strategies, and the complexities surrounding Tesla's exclusion from the S&P 500 ESG index during his appearance on Bloomberg. He highlighted the importance of understanding the different components ("e," "s," and "g") of ESG and how momentum ETFs rebalance. Rosenbluth also emphasized that investors need to look beyond labels, as not all ESG or factor-based ETFs are the same.

title: Lithium Miner Albemarle Lifts Outlook as EV Battery Demand Surges
summary: Albemarle Corp., the world’s largest lithium producer, has raised its financial outlook for the second time this month. This adjustment is due to strong demand for electric vehicle batteries and tight lithium supply, leading battery makers to pay higher prices for the metal. The company now projects sales between $5.8 billion and $6.2 billion for the current year.

title: Airbnb Pulling Out of China Thanks to Stiff Competition From Super-Apps
summary: Airbnb is discontinuing its short-term rental operations in China starting July 30, 2022, due to intense local competition from "super-apps" and strict COVID-19 lockdowns. While Chinese customers can still use Airbnb for international travel, the company will remove approximately 150,000 listings from its platform in China. This move follows other American companies like LinkedIn, Yahoo, Urban Outfitters, and Everlane that have also recently exited the Chinese market.

title: Tesla plans a drive-in movie restaurant in Hollywood
summary: Tesla has submitted documents to the city of Los Angeles for a 24-hour drive-in movie restaurant with a 28-stall Supercharger station in Hollywood, a concept Elon Musk has been teasing for four years. The plans detail a two-story diner with indoor and outdoor seating, two LED movie screens for drive-in viewing, and food delivery to cars. This futuristic establishment would replace a Shakey's Pizza and requires city approval before proceeding.

title: Texas Is Now Home to More Fortune 500 Companies Than Any Other State, and I’m Not Surprised
summary: Texas has become the leading state for Fortune 500 company headquarters, surpassing New York and California, with 53 businesses currently located there. This migration, including major companies like Tesla and Hewlett Packard Enterprise, is attributed to Texas's business-friendly policies, lower cost of living, attractive tax environment (no income tax), educated workforce, and robust infrastructure. The author, whose company U.S. Global Investors operates in Texas, expresses no surprise at this trend, highlighting the state's economic appeal.

title: How a Sustainability Index Can Keep Exxon but Drop Tesla – And 3 Ways to Fix ESG Ratings to Meet Investors’ Expectations
summary: A major stock index recently dropped Tesla but kept ExxonMobil, sparking debate over ESG ratings. Professor Tom Lyon explains that ESG ratings often compare companies within their industry, leading to situations where an oil giant ranks better than an EV manufacturer due to different criteria and internal factors like social and governance issues. He suggests improving ESG ratings by allowing investors to target specific objectives, breaking down ESG into individual "E," "S," and "G" metrics, and enhancing disclosure requirements.
source: University of Michigan's Ross School of Business
source_domain: University of Michigan's Ross School of Business

title: Hyperion looks to slower growth for a helping hand
summary: Australia's largest growth manager, Hyperion, is betting on a counterintuitive outcome—an economic downturn and anemic growth—to revive its performance. Despite a 36% year-to-date loss, Hyperion's CIO Mark Arnold believes that high inflation and high interest rates are temporary and will retreat as the economy cools, providing a tailwind for growth stocks. The firm argues that its disruptive holdings, like Tesla and Amazon, will outperform in a cooler economy where growth is scarce, forcing capital allocators to invest in companies with double-digit earnings growth.

title: Pony.ai's permit to test autonomous vehicles revoked in California
summary: The California Department of Motor Vehicles has revoked Pony.ai's permit to test autonomous vehicles with safety drivers due to the company's failure to monitor the driving records of its safety drivers. The DMV found numerous violations on the driving records of active Pony.ai safety drivers, emphasizing the critical role of clean driving records for safety drivers. Pony.ai, while stating pride in its safety record of over 6.8 million accident-free autonomous miles, had previously lost a permit for driverless testing after a collision and subsequently recalled vehicles due to software issues.

title: Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions, BYU–Hawaii complete campuswide renewable energy system
summary: Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions and Brigham Young University–Hawaii have completed a campuswide renewable energy system, including solar and battery storage. This system is expected to meet 39% of the university's energy needs annually and save over $20 million in utility costs. The project aims to reduce the university's environmental impact and dependence on Hawaii's energy grid, utilizing a 20-year power purchase agreement to finance the initiative.

title: 5 lessons I learned from helping to launch Tesla’s Model S
summary: The article shares five business lessons learned by Sukemasa Kabayama, the former President of Tesla Japan, during the challenging five-week launch of the Model S in Japan in 2014. These lessons emphasize creativity, holistic customer experience, laser focus on outcomes, the principle of "less is more," and clarity in problem-solving. Kabayama also draws parallels to his current startup, Uplift Labs.

title: Putting Recent Market Volatility in Perspective
summary: This article provides perspective on recent market volatility, noting that while 2022 has been a bumpy ride for investors with significant downturns in growth stocks and technology, such fluctuations are not historically uncommon. It examines the CBOE VIX Index and standard deviation data to show increased volatility, driven by inflation fears and rising interest rates, but emphasizes that market losses are a normal part of investing. The piece concludes by advising long-term investors to maintain their asset mix and avoid drastic changes unless retirement or significant near-term expenses necessitate a re-evaluation of their portfolio.

title: Laying the Groundwork for EV Charging Capability
summary: The article discusses the growing importance of electric vehicles (EVs) in the energy transition and the challenges associated with developing a robust EV charging infrastructure. It proposes various business models for oil and gas companies to adopt, such as franchise, charging host, and operator/full-service provider models, to meet the increasing demand for EV charging. The piece also outlines key design considerations for an effective charge point monitoring system (CPMS) to ensure reliability, scalability, and efficient monetization of charge points.

title: Elon Musk blasts ESG after DWS office raids over greenwashing allegations
summary: Elon Musk criticized the ESG industry once more after DWS's Frankfurt offices were raided due to greenwashing allegations. The Tesla CEO tweeted on June 1st that he had "yet to see an ESG list that *isn’t* fraudulent." This follows his previous strong remarks calling ESG "a scam" after Tesla was removed from the S&P ESG Index.

title: Tesla Inc. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Tesla Inc. stock (TSLA) fell 0.18% to $758.26 on Tuesday, May 31, 2022, despite an overall poor trading session for the stock market. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high but outperformed some competitors, such as Toyota Motor Corp. ADR (TM) and Honda Motor Co. Ltd. ADR (HMC), although it lagged behind General Motors Co. (GM). Trading volume for Tesla exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Jupiter Wagons Ltd. launches ‘Jupiter Electric Mobility’, enters the EV segment
summary: Jupiter Wagons Ltd. has launched 'Jupiter Electric Mobility' (JEM) to enter the electric commercial vehicle market. This initiative involves a joint venture with EA GreenPower Private Limited, a subsidiary of GreenPower Motor Company Inc., aiming to produce LCV, MCV, and HCV categories in India and establish it as a manufacturing hub for global exports. The company plans to invest Rs 200 crores in the next three years, focusing on B2B distribution for logistics, e-commerce, and FMCG businesses.

title: GM slashes prices of Chevy Bolt electric vehicles despite rising commodity costs
summary: General Motors has significantly cut the prices of its 2023 Chevrolet Bolt EV and Bolt EUV models, making the Bolt EV potentially the most affordable electric vehicle in the U.S. This price reduction, enacted despite rising commodity costs and amidst price hikes from competitors like Tesla and Rivian, is an effort to improve competitiveness and align with customer purchase prices. The Bolt models, which use older battery technology, are expected to see a boost in sales, with production of the 2023 models resuming after a recall-related shutdown.

title: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Station Market Size to grow by USD 15.81 billion from 2021 to 2026|Driven by the Increasing Number of M & A and Strategic Partnerships to Drive Market | Technavio
summary: The Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Station Market is projected to grow by USD 15.81 billion between 2021 and 2026, accelerating at a CAGR of 20.65%. This growth is primarily driven by an increasing number of mergers, acquisitions, and strategic partnerships within the industry. However, market expansion could be hindered by a lack of standardization in EV charging infrastructure.

title: Self-driving car companies' first step to making money isn't robotaxis
summary: Self-driving car companies are finding their initial path to profitability not through robotaxis, but through sales of driver-assistance software. Investment analysts from Goldman Sachs and Nomura highlight significant opportunities in auto software, with companies like WeRide partnering with Bosch to develop mass-production assisted driving systems. This L2/L3 market, particularly strong in China, offers clearer commercial value and a quicker revenue stream compared to fully autonomous robotaxi services.

title: Electric vehicle maker Stellantis will buy lithium produced at Salton Sea
summary: Stellantis, a major electric vehicle manufacturer, has signed a 10-year agreement with Controlled Thermal Resources (CTR) to purchase battery-grade lithium hydroxide from CTR's Hell's Kitchen project at the Salton Sea. This deal aims to secure a low-carbon lithium supply for Stellantis' North American electrified vehicle production, supporting its ambitious goal of 5 million annual battery electric vehicle sales by 2030. CTR plans to produce lithium from geothermal brines using an environmentally friendly, closed-loop process.

title: Who’ll be Europe’s next green billionaire?
summary: This article examines the current "green billionaires" in European climate tech and identifies potential future candidates. It highlights founders like Denis Sverdlov (Arrival), Stephen Fitzpatrick (Ovo Group), and Peter Carlsson (Northvolt), detailing their net worths based on company valuations and ownership stakes. The piece notes the dominance of fintech and software in creating wealth so far, but points to the rapid growth of the climate tech sector as a new frontier for high-value entrepreneurs.

title: Chip shortage is easing, says world's biggest truck-maker Daimler Truck Holding AG
summary: Daimler Truck Holding AG, the world's largest truck-maker, is observing positive signs of the global chip shortage easing. Despite the improving situation, the company is still closely monitoring the supply chain, as stated by Karin Radstrom, CEO of the Mercedes-Benz truck brand. While demand remains high and production backlogs are keeping factories busy, the company is also focusing on its zero-emissions plan, developing battery-powered and hydrogen fuel-cell trucks.

title: Tesla Fair Fund distributions established to pay 'harmed' investors
summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission announced the establishment of the Tesla Fair Fund to distribute payments to investors harmed by Elon Musk's "funding secured" tweet. Investors who bought Tesla Inc. shares between August 7 and August 8, 2018, may be eligible for distributions. This fund was created after Tesla and CEO Elon Musk agreed to pay $40 million to settle an SEC lawsuit alleging the tweet was false and misleading.

title: What Does Amazon's Stock Split Mean for Investors?
summary: Amazon is executing a 20-1 stock split, its first in over two decades, effective June 3. The split will adjust Morningstar's fair value estimate for Amazon to $192 per share from $3,850, but senior analyst Dan Romanoff's long-term view remains unchanged, anticipating continued growth in e-commerce, AWS, and advertising. Other major tech companies like Alphabet and Tesla are also planning stock splits.

title: U.S. safety regulators receive over 750 complaints of Teslas braking for no reason
summary: U.S. safety regulators have received over 750 complaints from Tesla owners reporting that their vehicles, operating on partially automated driving systems, suddenly stopped on roadways for no apparent reason. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is investigating these "phantom braking" incidents in Models 3 and Y from 2021 and 2022, covering an estimated 416,000 vehicles. This is one of several ongoing investigations and recalls for Tesla by safety regulators.

title: Premarket Movers: Okta Cl A, HashiCorp Cl A, Kohl's Corp
summary: This article details pre-market stock movements for several companies. Okta Cl A and Kohl's Corp saw significant gains, up 16.2% and 7.3% respectively. Other companies like BRP, PagSeguro Digital, and Nutex Health also recorded gains, while HashiCorp Cl A and Tesla experienced declines.

title: Musk wants to cut 10 percent of Tesla jobs: Report
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk reportedly has a "super bad feeling" about the economy and plans to cut about 10 percent of jobs at the electric carmaker, according to an email sent to executives. This message, titled "pause all hiring worldwide," follows his demand for staff to return to the workplace or leave, and comes amidst growing warnings from business leaders about a potential recession. The move has impacted Tesla's stock performance and is a more direct statement on the economic outlook than previous warnings from Musk.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Gains as Stock Split Lowers Price Tag for Retail Buyers
summary: Amazon's stock surged after a 20-for-1 split, making shares more accessible to retail investors. This marks the company's first split in over two decades, leading to increased trading volume and outperforming the Nasdaq 100 Index. The move is expected to attract greater retail interest, potentially acting as a sentiment catalyst.

title: WalMart expands transportation partnerships with electric, hydrogen vehicle pilots
summary: Walmart is expanding its transportation pilot programs to include electric, hydrogen, and natural gas-powered vehicles, partnering with companies like Cummins, Daimler Truck's Freightliner, and Nikola. These initiatives support Walmart's 2040 goal of achieving zero emissions across its global operations, which include a large fleet of tractors and trailers. The retailer emphasized that it is still in the testing phase, exploring multiple solutions, as no single technology currently provides a comprehensive path to decarbonization at scale.

title: Enable Better Performance, Fuel Economy with Garrett’s Electric Compressor for Hybrid Vehicles
summary: Garrett Motion has developed a new generation electric compressor (E-Compressor) for hybrid vehicles, designed to improve performance, enhance fuel economy, and reduce exhaust emissions. This technology can be integrated with 48-volt mild hybrids and 300-400-volt full and plug-in hybrids, expanding Garrett's presence in the growing hybrid market. When paired with a turbocharger, the E-Compressor provides "boost on demand," offering benefits like increased power density, torque density, and significant reductions in NOx and soot emissions, while also enabling fuel savings.

title: ‘World Champion’ WM Motor Joins China EV Race to Market With Hong Kong Listing Plan
summary: WM Motor, a Chinese electric vehicle maker, is seeking to raise up to $1 billion through a Hong Kong IPO, making it the fifth such company to list in the city. Despite aiming for a less crowded Shanghai market initially, WM Motor saw significant revenue growth, doubling unit sales in 2021, but also experienced increased losses. The company, which builds its own manufacturing facilities and focuses on mid-range EVs, faces stiff competition from established players and other startups in China's burgeoning EV market.

title: Baidu's electric vehicle firm Jidu unveils first 'robot' car
summary: Baidu's EV arm Jidu Auto has unveiled its first "robot" concept car, aiming for mass production in 2023. This vehicle, co-funded by Chinese automaker Geely, features Level 4 autonomous capabilities and voice recognition, and is designed to attract tech-savvy users. The move positions Baidu among global tech companies developing smart cars following Tesla's success.

title: Tesla goes ahead with China hiring event after Musk job warning
summary: Despite Elon Musk's recent warnings about job cuts and being "overstaffed," Tesla proceeded with a China hiring event on Thursday, adding two dozen new job postings. The event aimed to recruit staff for "smart manufacturing" roles, including managers and engineers for its Giga Press machines. This comes as Tesla's Shanghai plant, a significant contributor to its global production and revenue, plans to expand, even after being impacted by recent COVID-19 lockdowns.

title: Stellantis Stock Is Undervalued, Even as It Catches Up in the Electric Vehicle Market
summary: Stellantis, formed from the 2021 merger of Fiat Chrysler and Peugeot, is making an aggressive push into the electric vehicle market after being a laggard. Despite its efforts to catch up, Morningstar analysts consider Stellantis stock undervalued, trading at a significant discount to its peers. The company plans an all-electric lineup for its luxury brands by 2024 and aims for 50% EV sales in North America by 2030, alongside ambitious carbon reduction and revenue growth targets.

title: U.S. agency upgrades Tesla Autopilot safety probe, step before possible recall
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has upgraded its probe into 830,000 Tesla vehicles equipped with Autopilot, moving closer to a potential recall. The agency is investigating the system's performance after numerous crashes involving emergency vehicles and is focusing on whether Tesla adequately ensures drivers pay attention while using the assistance feature. This upgrade to an engineering analysis is a crucial step before NHTSA can demand a recall.

title: Renewable energy bill threatens to stall solar in Hawaii
summary: Solar workers and clean energy advocates in Hawaii are urging Governor Ige to veto SB 2510, a bill that mandates one-third of renewable energy to come from “firm” sources, rather than intermittent ones like solar and wind. Opponents argue this bill would harm the solar industry, raise consumer costs, and favor expensive biomass or biofuel projects. Supporters of the bill express concern about over-reliance on intermittent energy, while critics believe it jeopardizes the state's clean energy goals and might be influenced by special interests.

title: ST continues to grow in Morocco – opens new clean room
summary: STMicroelectronics has opened a new clean room at its Bouskoura, Morocco location, dedicated to silicon carbide products. The company invested USD 240 million between 2020 and 2022 to expand capacity for the electric vehicle (EV) and industrial markets, creating 700 new jobs since July 2021. This expansion significantly increases the production capabilities for STPOWER Silicon Carbide products, which are crucial for EV applications.

title: Trudeau meets Google boss Sundar Pichai, but no word on whether the tech CEO chewed out the PM over Bill C-18
summary: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau met with Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet (Google's parent company), but it's unclear if Bill C-18, a controversial Canadian media compensation bill, was discussed. The bill, criticized by experts like Michael Geist as a "shakedown," aims to make platforms like Google pay for linking to news content, giving the CRTC greater oversight. Google's Canadian head of public policy, Colin McKay, has stated that while Google supports journalism funding, Bill C-18 "would fundamentally and negatively impact millions of Canadians."

title: Royal Caribbean wants to add Elon Musk's Starlink high-speed internet to its cruise ships
summary: Royal Caribbean is seeking FCC approval to implement Elon Musk's Starlink high-speed internet on its cruise ships to significantly enhance onboard connectivity. This move aims to address current internet limitations and improve guest experience and business operations at sea. The adoption hinges on SpaceX receiving regulatory approval to operate Starlink on moving vehicles.

title: Apple’s New CarPlay Is the Foreshock to Releasing Its Own Vehicle
summary: Apple's redesigned CarPlay interface, unveiled at WWDC 2022, is seen as a precursor to the company eventually releasing its own vehicle. The article also touches on other Apple developments from WWDC 2022, including its new multitasking system, the absence of tvOS, and hints about an upcoming AR/VR headset. This reflects a broader expectation that Apple is laying the groundwork for a future in automotive technology.

title: Roku, Tesla, and Other Cathie Wood Favorites Are Falling
summary: Cathie Wood's $12 billion flagship exchange-traded fund experienced a decline in Monday trading, signaling continued pressure on "innovation stocks" like Roku and Tesla. This event highlights the ongoing challenges faced by popular growth-oriented investments favored by the Ark Invest CEO.

title: Enovix 3D Silicon Lithium-ion Batteries for EVs Can Achieve 98% Charge Capacity in Under 10-Minutes
summary: Enovix has developed 3D Silicon Lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles (EVs) that can charge from 0-80% in 5.2 minutes and reach over 98% capacity in under 10 minutes. This technology not only offers rapid charging but also maintains a high cycle life, potentially accelerating the mass adoption of EVs by meeting and exceeding OEM roadmaps for faster charging capabilities. Co-founder and CEO Harrold Rust emphasized that this innovation addresses the demand for longer-range batteries and increased access to fast chargers for EV drivers.

title: 7 Founder-Led Stocks to Buy and Hold Forever
summary: This article highlights seven founder-led stocks, including Tesla, Nvidia, Salesforce, Blackstone, Steel Dynamics, Block, and Apollo Global Management, that are considered strong long-term buys due to their history of outperformance. The author emphasizes the sustained engagement of founders in their companies and provides a brief overview of each company's financial health, leadership, and recent performance. The piece suggests that founder-led companies tend to outperform those without a founder in the CEO role.

title: Caterpillar headquarters leaving Illinois after nearly 100 years
summary: Caterpillar Inc. is moving its global headquarters from Deerfield, Illinois, to Irving, Texas, after nearly 100 years in its home state. The construction equipment manufacturer previously moved its base from Peoria, Illinois, to Deerfield in 2017. This move follows a trend of major corporations, including Boeing and several tech companies, relocating headquarters to Texas.

title: Royal Caribbean may add Elon Musk's Starlink internet service to its cruise ships
summary: Royal Caribbean Group is exploring a partnership with Elon Musk's SpaceX to bring Starlink internet service to its cruise ships. The cruise line operator believes Starlink could significantly improve guest experience and business operations at sea, addressing current bandwidth constraints. This potential collaboration, if approved by the FCC, would be a first for the cruise industry and could set a new standard for internet connectivity on vessels.

title: Caterpillar to move global headquarters from Illinois to Texas
summary: Caterpillar Inc. announced it is moving its global headquarters from Deerfield, Illinois, to Irving, Texas. The company declined to state the reason for the move or if it received incentives, though Texas is known for lower labor costs and less stringent regulation. This relocation follows a trend of other major manufacturers, like Boeing and Tesla, moving headquarters to Texas from other states.

title: Caterpillar Moving Its Headquarters to Texas from Illinois
summary: Caterpillar Inc., the construction equipment manufacturer, announced its decision to move its global headquarters from Deerfield, Illinois, to Irving, a suburb of Dallas, Texas. This marks another major corporate relocation from the Chicago area, following Boeing's recent move. CEO Jim Umpleby stated that the move is in the company's best strategic interest, and the transition will begin this year.

title: 2023 Genesis GV60 Quick Spin: Electrifying Performance
summary: The 2023 Genesis GV60 is a new all-electric luxury SUV combining hatchback and four-door-coupe styling with impressive performance. The Performance trim boasts 429 hp, an adaptive suspension, and unique features like a Boost Mode for increased power. While offering quiet sportiness and a user-friendly interior, it has minor drawbacks such as restricted rear visibility and potentially difficult-to-decipher backlit buttons.

title: New EV Battery Reaches 98 Percent Capacity in Less Than Ten Minutes
summary: Enovix has developed a new silicon-anode lithium-ion battery for electric vehicles that can charge to 80% in 5.2 minutes and 98% in 10 minutes. This technology, called 3D Silicon, uses silicon anodes which offer higher storage capacity than traditional graphite while mitigating swelling issues with a proprietary constraint system. The company estimates these batteries will last at least 10 years, even after 1,000 charge cycles, addressing key concerns for EV adoption.

title: Caterpillar to relocate global headquarters from Illinois to Irving, Texas
summary: Caterpillar Inc. announced it will move its global headquarters from Illinois to its existing office in Irving, Texas, starting in 2022. This relocation adds Caterpillar to the growing list of Fortune 500 companies moving to Texas, bringing the total number of corporate headquarters in the state to 54. Despite the move, Illinois will continue to have the largest concentration of Caterpillar employees worldwide.

title: Standard Mileage Rates for Business, Medical, and Moving Expense Purposes Will Increase in July
summary: The IRS has announced a midyear increase in standard mileage rates for business, medical, and moving expenses, effective July 1, 2022. The business rate increases to 62.5 cents per mile, while medical and moving expense rates rise to 22 cents per mile. This adjustment, unusual for a midyear change, reflects recent increases in gasoline prices.

title: Tesla to charge more for cars in United States as inflation bites
summary: Tesla Inc. has once again increased prices for all its car models in the United States, with some models seeing prices rise by as much as $3,000, in response to persistent global supply-chain problems and soaring raw material costs. This marks the fourth price hike for some models in the US in 2022 due to rising costs of materials like aluminum and lithium, as well as an industry-wide chip shortage. Rival Rivian Automotive Inc. has also raised prices for new orders, and CEO Elon Musk has expressed concerns about the economy and the need for job cuts.

title: Opportunities in US stock market for investors who want to invest in climate change theme
summary: This article explores investment opportunities in the US stock market for those interested in the climate change theme, emphasizing the role of companies in mitigating climate risks and achieving long-term profitability. It highlights renewable energy, electric vehicles, and climate-focused Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) as key investment avenues. The piece also provides specific company examples and discusses market growth projections for the renewable energy sector.

title: Tesla prices rise by thousands, again: Model Y now starts at $67,190
summary: Tesla has once again raised prices for several of its models in the U.S. market, with hikes ranging from $2,000 to $6,000. The Model Y's base price increased by $3,000 to $67,190, while the Model S and Model X also saw significant price increases. These adjustments are attributed to intense demand outpacing production capabilities and ongoing supply-chain issues.

title: If you can’t beat ‘em, join ‘em? Dominion Energy begins selling residential solar
summary: Dominion Energy, historically resistant to residential solar, has launched BrightSuite, a subsidiary selling solar arrays to consumers. This move follows the expansion of onsite solar opportunities in Virginia and a significant increase in residential solar installations. While Dominion's brand recognition offers a competitive edge, its higher pricing may benefit independent installers as consumers comparison shop, potentially growing the overall distributed solar market.

title: Sony and Honda Join Forces to Launch New EV Company, Targets Sales by 2025
summary: Sony and Honda have officially formed Sony Honda Mobility Inc., a new electric vehicle joint venture, with plans to start selling high-value EVs and mobility services by 2025. This collaboration brings together Honda's vehicle manufacturing and environmental technologies with Sony's expertise in imaging, sensing, telecommunication, network, and entertainment technologies. The initiative aligns with Honda's broader environmental goals, including achieving carbon neutrality and 100% EV sales by 2040.

title: Ariana Grande Debuts Chapter 3 of R.E.M. Beauty with a Bang(s)
summary: Ariana Grande's R.E.M. Beauty launched its third collection, 'Chapter 3: on your collar,' focusing on lip products. This collection, which includes five new formulas like lip oil, balm, liner, and lipsticks, follows the brand's 'drops' model and continues its extraterrestrial aesthetic. R.E.M. Beauty's initial collections, Chapters 1 and 2, are also available at Ulta stores.

title: Elon Musk and Tesla sued over Dogecoin ‘pyramid scheme’
summary: Elon Musk and Tesla are being sued for $258 billion by a Dogecoin investor who alleges they ran a pyramid scheme to inflate the cryptocurrency's value. The plaintiff, Keith Johnson, claims Musk manipulated Dogecoin for "profit, exposure and amusement" despite knowing it had no intrinsic value, and seeks damages for the $86 billion decline in Dogecoin's market value since May 2021. Johnson also wants to prevent Musk and his companies from promoting Dogecoin and to have it declared gambling under federal and New York law.

title: How the massive EV transition is starting in the car rental industry
summary: The car rental industry is undergoing a significant transition to electric vehicles (EVs), led by Hertz's substantial purchase of Teslas, followed by moves from Enterprise and Avis. This shift, however, faces challenges such as limited EV availability, insufficient charging infrastructure, and the need to educate both employees and customers. Despite these hurdles, rental companies are targeting corporate clients who seek to meet ESG goals through EV adoption, and the industry is seen as crucial for broader public exposure to EVs.

title: Mining billionaire Robert Friedland launches IPO for Ivanhoe Electric
summary: Billionaire Robert Friedland is launching an initial public offering (IPO) for Ivanhoe Electric Inc., aiming to raise US$180-million. The Vancouver-based company will focus on supplying copper and other critical minerals for electric cars and clean-energy technology, with properties in Arizona and Utah. This IPO marks a significant event in a quiet market, with shares planned for listing on both the Toronto and New York stock exchanges.

title: Why ESG is Becoming a Bigger Deal for Investors
summary: ESG (environmental, social, and governance) investing is rapidly gaining traction, with a record $649 billion poured into ESG-focused funds in 2021. Major players like BlackRock are emphasizing ESG, believing that companies deliberating on their societal role perform better, leading to long-term value for shareholders. While greenwashing concerns exist, new global standards and regulatory clarifications are emerging as ESG becomes a mainstream method for evaluating businesses and attracting investment.

title: Laid-Off Workers Claim Tesla Violated WARN Act in Suit
summary: Former Tesla employees have filed a lawsuit alleging the company violated the federal WARN Act by failing to provide 60 days' advance notice before mass layoffs. Two workers from Tesla's battery factory near Reno, Nevada, claim they were terminated without notice and are seeking class-action status for others affected by May and June job cuts. The plaintiffs are seeking compensation and benefits for 60 days following their termination.

title: General Motors increases Hummer EV price by $6,250
summary: General Motors has increased the price of its Hummer EV pickup truck by $6,250 due to higher commodity and transportation costs. The price increase will affect new orders, while the 77,500 existing reservations will not be impacted. This move follows similar price adjustments made by other EV manufacturers like Tesla and Rivian to offset rising supply chain costs.

title: 2022 Cars.com American-Made Index: Which Cars Are the Most American?
summary: Cars.com has released its 2022 American-Made Index, ranking vehicles based on assembly location, parts content, engine and transmission origins, and U.S. manufacturing workforce. Tesla dominates the top spots, with its Model Y retaining the #1 position and all four Tesla models in the top 10. The study also highlights increasing interest in electrified vehicles, despite inventory challenges, and details the methodology used to determine the rankings.

title: 2022 Cars.com American-Made Index: What About the Least American Cars?
summary: This article discusses the "least American" cars based on Cars.com's 2022 American-Made Index, highlighting vehicles that didn't qualify due to various factors like assembly location. It notes that many popular models from major automakers, including Ford and GM, are manufactured outside the U.S., and only Tesla currently produces all its U.S.-sold cars domestically. The piece also provides a breakdown of major automakers' share of U.S. light-duty sales from domestic assembly.

title: Why You Might Buy Your Next Car Online (Published 2022)
summary: Tesla's decision in 2019 to sell cars exclusively online, initially met with skepticism, has proven successful, forcing the auto industry to reconsider its traditional dealership model. This approach, adopted by other EV makers, could transform car sales, as consumers appreciate the convenience and service of online purchasing, potentially impacting established automakers and dealers.

title: Tesla sued by former employees over 'mass layoffs"
summary: Tesla is facing a lawsuit from two former employees who claim the company violated federal law by not providing advance notice for "mass layoffs" at its Nevada gigafactory. The lawsuit, filed on behalf of all former US Tesla employees laid off in May or June without notice, alleges that over 500 employees were dismissed. This legal action comes after Elon Musk announced plans to slash 10% of salaried workers due to predictions of an "inevitable" US recession.

title: Tesla sued by former employees over 'mass layoff'
summary: Former Tesla employees have filed a lawsuit against the company, alleging that its recent "mass layoff" violated federal law by not providing advance notice of job cuts. The lawsuit, filed in Texas by two workers terminated from Tesla's Nevada gigafactory, seeks class action status for all affected employees and highlights the company's alleged failure to adhere to the 60-day notification period required by the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act. Tesla CEO Elon Musk has dismissed the lawsuit as "trivial," while the employees' attorney emphasized the impact of these terminations on workers who received minimal severance.

title: ATS Automation lands $90 million contract with EV manufacturer
summary: ATS Automation Tooling Systems Inc. has secured a US$70 million (C$90 million) contract with a global electric vehicle manufacturer to design and build fully automated battery assembly systems. This order, which will be recorded in Q1 fiscal 2023 and delivered over 18 months, is part of a multi-phase program for the EV company's North American operations. ATS CEO Andrew Hider highlighted that this leverages their experience in the EV market and strengthens their position as a leader in the growing sector.

title: It’s time to talk about consolidation in the EV charging industry
summary: The EV charging industry is undergoing significant consolidation, driven by President Biden's $7.5 billion infrastructure bill. Companies like Blink Charging are making strategic acquisitions, such as SemaConnect, to expand their networks and comply with "Buy American" mandates, which will allow them to access federal funding. Foreign companies like Schneider Electric are also increasing their footprint in the U.S. through M&A, indicating a trend toward strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and scaling DC Fast charging solutions.

title: NIO Inc. ADR rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: NIO Inc. ADR (NIO) saw a significant rise of 9.10% on Tuesday, closing at $22.66 and outperforming the broader market, including the NASDAQ Composite and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This marked its second consecutive day of gains, although it remained $32.47 below its 52-week high. The company's performance was mixed compared to competitors like Tesla, Toyota, and Ferrari, which also saw gains.

title: BITI Chart | ProShares Short Bitcoin Strategy ETF
summary: This page provides a live, interactive chart for the ProShares Short Bitcoin Strategy ETF (BITI), allowing users to analyze its performance. The chart offers various customization options and technical indicators to help investors understand price movements. It also includes current market data for BITI, such as its price, daily range, and 52-week range.

title: Tesla worker rejects $15 million payout in race bias lawsuit
summary: A former Black elevator operator at Tesla's Fremont plant, Owen Diaz, has rejected a $15 million award in his racial abuse lawsuit, opting for a new trial. The original jury award of $137 million was significantly reduced by a federal judge, which Diaz's lawyers argue is unjust and insufficient to deter future misconduct by Tesla. This decision comes amidst other lawsuits against Tesla regarding alleged widespread race discrimination and sexual harassment at its factory.

title: Tesla Model Y nabs title of most American-made 2022 model
summary: Tesla's Model Y and Model 3 secured the top two spots on Cars.com's 2022 American-Made Index, with all four Tesla models landing in the top 10. The company's regional manufacturing approach and 100% domestic production for U.S. sales were key factors. General Motors, Honda, Toyota, and Ford also had significant representation in the overall index, and increasing consumer interest in American-made vehicles is noted, especially concerning EVs.

title: SIGMA LITHIUM SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASES TOTAL NI 43-101 MINERAL RESOURCE BY ~50% TO 86 MILLION TONNES, ADDING 27 MILLION TONNES OF HIGH-GRADE 1.49% LITHIUM OXIDE IN PHASE 3
summary: Sigma Lithium announced a 50% increase in its total NI 43-101 mineral resource to 85.7 million tonnes, primarily due to the addition of 26.8 million tonnes of high-grade 1.49% lithium oxide from its Phase 3 NDC deposit. This significantly strengthens the company's Grota do Cirilo Project as a major source of Battery Grade Sustainable Lithium, with Phase 1 construction remaining on schedule for commissioning by December 2022. The increased resource aims to further boost the potential production profile for global electric vehicle markets.

title: How the Tesla Model S Changed the World
summary: The article reflects on the 10th anniversary of the Tesla Model S, highlighting its transformative impact on the automotive industry by redefining electric vehicles and challenging traditional car manufacturing and sales models. It discusses how the Model S pioneered online sales, over-the-air updates, and robust performance for EVs, but also touches on the controversies surrounding Tesla's pursuit of full self-driving technology and its effects on the car's reputation. Despite challenges with reliability and CEO Elon Musk's public image, the Model S is recognized as a historically significant vehicle that fundamentally reshaped consumer expectations and industry practices.

title: Elon Musk Says New Tesla Plants Are Losing Billions
summary: Elon Musk has revealed that Tesla's new Gigafactories in Germany and Texas are currently incurring "billions of dollars" in losses as the company struggles to ramp up production. Supply chain disruptions, including COVID-19 lockdowns in China, have significantly hampered manufacturing efforts, particularly for Model Y SUVs with new battery technology. Musk emphasized the significant effort required to bring these factories to high-volume production.

title: Musk says Tesla's new car factories 'losing billions of dollars'
summary: Elon Musk stated that Tesla's new factories in Texas and Berlin are "losing billions of dollars" due to production struggles. These issues stem from battery shortages and logistical challenges like parts being stuck in Chinese ports, exacerbated by COVID-19 shutdowns. Despite these hurdles, Musk expects these problems to be resolved quickly, with production of the Cybertruck anticipated to begin in mid-2023.

title: Billionaire Larry Ellison, among world’s richest people, bought Florida estate for $173 million
summary: Billionaire Larry Ellison, co-founder of Oracle, has purchased a sprawling 22-acre estate in Manalapan, Florida for $173 million, marking the largest residential sale ever in the state. The property includes a portion of Bird Island and was bought from fellow software billionaire Jim Clark. The article also details Ellison's net worth, his role at Oracle, his ties to Tesla, his charitable contributions, and a controversial call he reportedly participated in regarding the 2020 presidential election.

title: Tesla’s Texas, Berlin factories ‘losing billions of dollars’
summary: Elon Musk has stated that Tesla's new factories in Texas and Berlin are "losing billions of dollars" due to struggles in ramping up production. This challenge is attributed to a shortage of batteries and port issues in China, along with supply chain interruptions exacerbated by COVID-19 shutdowns in Shanghai. Musk highlighted the company's overwhelming concern as keeping factories operational to avoid bankruptcy.

title: Toyota recalls electric car for faulty wheel that may detach
summary: Toyota has issued a global recall for 2,700 bZ4X electric crossover vehicles due to a potentially faulty wheel that could detach. The cause of the issue is still under investigation, and customers are advised not to drive the vehicles until a remedy is available. This recall poses a significant setback for Toyota's ambitious plans to expand its electric vehicle lineup, which includes having 30 EV models by 2030.

title: Tech layoffs up, job offers gone, but much hiring
summary: Despite a rise in tech layoffs and rescinded job offers, the tech job market continues to see significant hiring, driven by high demand for skilled workers and ongoing growth within the sector. While some companies are cautious due to recession prospects, many are still adding staff and retaining knowledge workers, with the tech industry historically outperforming other sectors during economic downturns.

title: JPMorgan Chase Joins Companies Paying Employees Who Travel for Abortions
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it would cover travel expenses for employees needing to travel out of state for abortions, expanding a benefit that covers services unavailable near an employee's home. This decision follows the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade and aligns JPMorgan with other companies like Citigroup, Starbucks, Amazon, Tesla, and Yelp making similar pledges. The move addresses the implications of state-level abortion bans, with many states poised to restrict or ban abortions following the ruling.

title: Nearly 4 in 10 Who Bought a Car in the Past Year Have Regrets
summary: A LendingTree survey reveals that nearly 40% of recent car buyers regret their purchase, with the most common regret being the vehicle's make and model. Younger generations and those who bought cars within the last year express more regrets, while baby boomers and long-term owners report fewer. Many high earners and men have taken action to address their regrets, such as selling or refinancing their vehicles, though a significant portion of consumers also struggle with car payments and being underwater on their loans.

title: 2 killed as NIO electric car plummets 3 stories from building in China
summary: Two people, identified as "digital cabin testers" for the electric car brand NIO, died when a vehicle plunged three stories from a Shanghai parking structure. The company stated the incident, which occurred on Thursday, was an accident and not caused by vehicle malfunction, and an investigation is underway. Photos from Chinese media showed the car on its side with a caved-in roof, surrounded by debris.

title: Every new passenger car sold in the world will be electric by 2040, says Exxon Mobil CEO Darren Woods
summary: Exxon Mobil CEO Darren Woods predicts that by 2040, every new passenger car sold globally will be electric, a significant shift from the 9% electric vehicle sales in 2021. Despite this projection, Woods states that the company, a major petroleum refiner, is adapting by focusing on chemicals, which can be used in EV manufacturing, and believes the transition will not "make or break" their business. Exxon Mobil is evaluating the impact of declining gasoline sales but expects to remain profitable, similar to its position in 2013-2014 even with reduced oil demand.

title: Kroger increases EV charging offer across US stores
summary: Kroger is expanding EV charging options across its US stores, partnering with Blink, Electrify America, EVgo, Tesla, and Volta. The grocery retailer plans to add hundreds more charging stations in various markets, building on the over 350 chargers already installed in ten states. While the company did not specify AC or DC breakdown, charging times are expected to vary, with many sessions averaging around 30 minutes.

title: Wheels Up adds partnership with Hertz
summary: Wheels Up Experience has forged a new strategic partnership with Hertz, offering its members access to Hertz’s electric vehicle fleet, including Tesla and Polestar models, available at private jet airport locations. Members will also receive complimentary President’s Circle top-tier status in the Hertz Gold Plus Rewards program, along with discounts and dedicated ground transportation assistance. This collaboration aims to provide a seamless door-to-door travel experience and expand Wheels Up's product offerings.

title: BP, Shell to cover employee travel for treatment after Roe v. Wade
summary: BP PLC has joined Shell PLC in committing to cover employee travel expenses for healthcare treatment following the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade. Both European oil producers updated their healthcare plans to extend benefits for women needing to travel for services, though neither explicitly named abortion. This move comes as other major companies like Amazon, JPMorgan Chase, Tesla, and Walt Disney also updated their policies to cover travel costs for out-of-state abortion services, while U.S. oil majors have largely remained silent.

title: Trading At A Mere 4x Earnings, Is VALE Stock A Buy?
summary: This article analyzes whether VALE (NYSE: VALE), a major iron ore and nickel producer, is a buy given its current valuation of under 4x consensus 2022 earnings. Despite recent sequential declines in revenue and earnings due to intense rains and falling commodity prices, potential improvements in the Chinese economy and VALE's strategic focus on the EV market with deals like supplying Tesla, suggest an upside to its stock, which is valued at $25 per share. The company also appears to be in a stronger financial position having significantly reduced its net debt.

title: Frito-Lay CHRO: 'Everyone needs mental health support' | Human Resources Director
summary: Frito-Lay, a division of PepsiCo, Inc., is actively addressing the trucking industry's challenges, including high attrition and mental health concerns, by investing in its drivers' well-being. CHRO Patrick McLaughlin highlights the company's comprehensive approach, which includes competitive benefits, work-life balance initiatives, and robust mental health support programs like meQ and Spring Health. This strategy aims to improve retention and ensure Frito-Lay remains an employer of choice in a volatile labor market.

title: Honda shoots for North America EV rollout in 3 phases
summary: Honda plans a three-phase rollout for electric vehicles in North America, with the first EV, the Prologue (co-developed with GM), launching in 2024. The article briefly mentions this key development for Honda's electrification strategy.

title: Will Zoom Stock Hit $1,500 a Share by 2026?
summary: This article examines Ark Invest's bold prediction that Zoom (ZM) stock could reach $1,500 per share by 2026. While Ark Invest's model, driven by factors like increased remote work, expanding unified communications market share, and revenue growth from new AI-driven products, suggests this possibility, the article highlights the significant discrepancy between Ark's projected 76% annual growth and Zoom's actual present growth rate of around 10-12%. Nanalyze questions the sustainability of such aggressive growth projections and advises caution for investors.

title: Chip shortage drives up vehicle prices, cuts sales
summary: The global semiconductor shortage severely impacted U.S. new vehicle sales in the second quarter of 2022, leading to a 21% drop compared to the previous year. Despite high gas prices, inflation, and rising interest rates, demand outstripped supply, pushing average new vehicle prices to a record high of nearly $45,000. Automakers like GM and Toyota experienced significant sales declines, and while some expect gradual improvement, the shortage is anticipated to continue frustrating buyers and limiting inventory for the foreseeable future.

title: 14 Charts on the Market’s Second-Quarter Performance
summary: The second quarter of 2022 was exceptionally tough for investors, with both stocks and bonds posting losses for two consecutive quarters, a rare event not seen since 2008. Rising interest rates, due to persistent inflation, were the primary driver of market downturns, leading to significant declines in growth stocks and cryptocurrencies. Despite the broad market struggles, defensive sectors like healthcare and utilities, and some commodities like oil, showed relative resilience, while value stocks significantly outperformed growth stocks.

title: How Much Worse Can It Get for Growth Stocks?
summary: The second quarter of 2022 saw growth stocks suffer their largest losses since the 2008 financial crisis, with the Morningstar US Growth Index dropping 25.3%. Value stocks significantly outperformed growth, marking the widest margin since the dot-com bubble collapse, as rising interest rates and inflation dampened the appeal of growth companies' future earnings. While many growth stocks are now at their cheapest valuations in years, experts suggest value stocks may continue to outperform in the short term despite growth's long-term lead.

title: Tesla hit by new lawsuit alleging racial abuse against Black workers
summary: Fifteen Black former and current Tesla employees have filed a lawsuit against the company, alleging racial abuse and harassment at its factories, primarily in Fremont, California. The lawsuit details instances of racist comments, slurs, and discriminatory treatment, including being passed over for promotions or assigned to more physically demanding roles. This new legal action adds to at least 10 other lawsuits Tesla is facing related to race discrimination and sexual harassment.

title: Tesla's deliveries fall, hurt by China's COVID shutdown
summary: Tesla's vehicle deliveries dropped by 17.9% in the second quarter compared to the previous quarter, largely due to China's COVID-19 shutdown which disrupted production and supply chains. The company delivered 254,695 vehicles between April and June, ending a nearly two-year streak of record quarterly deliveries. Despite strong demand, CEO Elon Musk cited ongoing supply-chain challenges and referred to new factories in Texas and Berlin as "gigantic money furnaces."

title: Asset managers affirm they'll pay for travel
summary: Following the Supreme Court's abortion ruling, BlackRock and other asset managers have stated they will cover travel expenses for employees seeking abortion services. This decision places firms in a delicate position, balancing employee demands with potential client backlash, as articulated by Marcia S. Wagner of The Wagner Law Group. The article also touches upon other market news, including SEC work on private credit, endowment performance, and pension fund decisions.

title: Tesla Pauses Plants After Ending Shaky Quarter With a Production Milestone
summary: Tesla announced plant pauses in Shanghai and Berlin after a challenging quarter marked by disappointing deliveries but a record production month in June. The Shanghai factory will undergo upgrades to boost output, while the Berlin plant aims to double production rates. CEO Elon Musk acknowledged that the new Berlin and Austin plants are currently losing money, contributing to a significant drop in Tesla's stock last quarter.

title: The electric vehicle revolution: 'All kinds of cool things are happening'
summary: Karl Bloss, an EV education and outreach coordinator for Consumers Energy, discusses the benefits and future of electric vehicles. He highlights their efficiency, lower maintenance costs, and reduced environmental impact compared to traditional internal combustion engines. Bloss also addresses common concerns about charging and range, explaining modern charging solutions and how EV drivers manage their vehicles.

title: Wally Rippel (BS '68), Electrical Engineer
summary: This extensive interview with Wally Rippel, a Caltech alumnus, chronicles his pivotal role in the development of electric vehicles from the 1960s to the present. He discusses his early work on converting a VW Bus into an EV, the Great Electric Car Race against MIT, his contributions to AeroVironment (including the Sunraycer) and the GM Impact/EV1 program, and his experiences co-founding AC Propulsion and working at Tesla. Rippel also shares his insights on battery technology, the evolution of the EV market, and the importance of fundamental physics research in developing next-generation energy solutions.

title: Is the Nissan Altima a Good Car? 3 Pros and 2 Cons
summary: This article evaluates the 2022 Nissan Altima, highlighting its strengths and weaknesses as a mid-size sedan. It praises the Altima's powertrain choices, user-friendly infotainment system, and competitive pricing, particularly compared to rivals like the Honda Accord and Toyota Camry. However, it critiques the car's poor child seat fitment and the lack of a hybrid powertrain option, which is available in many competitors.

title: 4 Best EV Charging Stocks to Buy in July 2022
summary: The article identifies four top EV charging stocks to consider buying in July 2022, citing significant infrastructure investment plans in the U.S. and Europe. It highlights ChargePoint (CHPT), Blink Charging (BLNK), Wallbox (WBX), and EVgo (EVGO) as companies well-positioned to benefit from the accelerating global adoption of electric vehicles. The author provides reasons why each stock is a good investment, including growth strategies, market positions, and financial health, suggesting they present long-term accumulation opportunities despite recent market pullbacks.

title: Tesla China Shipments Soar to Record as Plant Fires Back Up
summary: Tesla's Shanghai plant significantly increased its vehicle shipments in June, delivering a record 78,906 vehicles. This represents a more than double increase from the previous year and a 145% rise from May, following a period of production disruption due to lockdown measures. The majority of these shipments, 77,938 cars, were for the local Chinese market, indicating a strong recovery for the electric car maker in China.

title: 78% of Americans fear losing their job ahead of recession
summary: A recent survey by Insight Global reveals that 78% of American workers fear losing their jobs due to an impending recession. This fear is more prevalent among managers, and over half of all workers would consider taking a pay cut to avoid layoffs, despite high inflation. Several major companies, including JPMorgan Chase, Coinbase, Netflix, and Tesla, have already conducted significant layoffs, with more expected as economic uncertainty continues.

title: XPeng P7 First Drive: China’s (Better-Built) Tesla Model S
summary: The XPeng P7, an EV sedan from China, is positioned as a strong rival to the Tesla Model S, offering impressive refinement, build quality, and software architecture. Developed with Porsche, it boasts competitive range and performance figures, with a starting price significantly lower than its Tesla counterpart in markets like Norway. The article suggests that if launched in the U.S. with tailored software, the P7 could significantly impact the automotive market, including Tesla's dominance.

title: NLRB Reverses Course on Trump-Era Rule Regarding Union Apparel Bans
summary: The National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) has overturned a Trump-era ruling, significantly restricting employers' ability to ban union insignia on clothing. The case, Tesla, Inc., revives the "special circumstances" test, requiring employers to justify such restrictions. This decision indicates a broader interpretation of employees' rights to display union support and advises employers to be cautious with dress code enforcement.

title: Arkansas Steel Takes Shape for Tesla
summary: W&W/AFCO Steel and Lexicon Inc., both based in Arkansas, significantly contributed to the rapid construction of Tesla's Gigafactory Texas. Within 502 days, the factory was built and began producing vehicles, utilizing thousands of tons of steel fabricated by these companies. The Gigafactory, touted by Elon Musk as the world's largest and most advanced car factory, continues to expand with ongoing steelwork from the Arkansas firms.

title: Tesla's German factory is only building black or white Model Y crossovers
summary: Tesla's factory near Berlin is currently only producing Model Y crossovers in black or white. This strategy may be aimed at optimizing production efficiency in the early stages of the factory's operation. The article highlights this specific production limitation at the German plant.

title: PG&E Recharging with Tesla Powerwall in Virtual Power Plant Pilot
summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Co. (PG&E) and Tesla Inc. have partnered on a five-year pilot program that will pay Tesla Powerwall customers to discharge energy to California's grid during peak demand. Approximately 1,500 customers have enrolled, and participants receive $2 per incremental kWh discharged, potentially adding megawatts equivalent to a small power plant. This initiative is part of California's Emergency Load Reduction Program and builds on previous collaborations between PG&E and Tesla, including the Elkhorn Battery System.

title: SEC Warns Investors About Single-Stock ETFs
summary: The SEC has voiced warnings about single-stock ETFs, despite approving the launch of over a dozen leveraged and inverse funds tied to individual equities. SEC officials highlighted the risks associated with these complex products, noting that while they might appeal to aggressive traders, they are prone to significant long-term losses due to their structure and underlying assets. Commissioner Caroline Crenshaw expressed disappointment that the regulatory framework has not been updated to better address the risks of such products, urging the SEC to use its existing tools to evaluate their appropriateness for investors.

title: What Does Google’s Stock Split Mean for Investors?
summary: Google's parent company, Alphabet, is undergoing a 20-for-1 stock split, which will adjust Morningstar's fair value estimate per share to $180, though its competitive advantage and 4-star "undervalued" rating remain unchanged. Analyst Ali Mogharabi identifies YouTube monetization, Maps monetization, and the cloud business as key growth drivers, with strong confidence in Google's continued dominance in the online search market. The article also notes other companies like Amazon, Shopify, and Tesla undertaking similar stock splits.

title: Electric Vehicle Charging Companies: 5 Questions to Ask
summary: This article identifies five key questions investors should consider when evaluating electric vehicle (EV) charging companies, given the early stage of the industry's development. It examines the evolving competitive landscape, the dichotomy between AC and DC charging, the impact of public policy, cost reduction strategies, and the competitive "fleet game." The piece also provides specific analyses of ChargePoint and EVgo, highlighting their market positions, growth prospects, and competitive challenges.

title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Adobe Next?
summary: Adobe could be the next high-profile company to announce a stock split, following a trend set by others like Alphabet and Amazon in 2022. While stock splits don't alter a company's fundamental valuation, they can make shares more accessible to retail investors and help companies attract/retain talent. Adobe has a history of 2-for-1 splits, with its last one occurring 17 years ago, and its strong financial performance in Q2 2022 suggests a healthy business that could support such a move.

title: Tesla alumni behind all-electric RV startup Lightship raise $23M
summary: Lightship Energy, an all-electric RV startup founded by former Tesla employees Ben Parker and Toby Kraus, has raised $23 million in Series A funding. The company aims to revolutionize the RV industry by developing an electric travel trailer that eliminates propane tanks and generators, and, crucially, addresses the significant range reduction experienced by electric towing vehicles. Their design includes an underlying EV skateboard architecture and a battery pack capable of propelling the trailer, effectively making it a 300-mile trailer for a 300-mile truck.

title: How to Buy Google Stock After the Split: GOOG vs. GOOGL
summary: Alphabet (Google's parent company) completed a 20-for-one stock split on July 15, 2022, making its shares more accessible to retail investors by lowering the per-share price. The article explains that Alphabet trades under two ticker symbols, GOOG (Class C, non-voting) and GOOGL (Class A, voting rights), both of which were affected by the split. Existing shareholders did not need to take any action as their accounts were automatically updated to reflect the new share quantity and price.

title: First US Single-Stock ETFs Debut
summary: AXS Investments has become the first company to launch single-stock ETFs in the U.S. market, providing leveraged exposure to the daily performance of actively traded stocks like NVIDIA and Tesla. While these funds offer potential for significant short-term gains, AXS explicitly states they are not suitable for long-term investors due to the extreme performance volatility associated with leveraged and inverse products. SEC officials like Caroline Crenshaw have also voiced concerns about the risks these products pose to investors and markets.

title: VinFast receives $1.2 billion in incentives for US manufacturing hub in North Carolina
summary: VinFast has secured a $1.2 billion incentive package from the State of North Carolina for its electric vehicle manufacturing facility. This represents the largest economic incentive package in the state's history and will lead to a $2 billion investment for phase one, creating thousands of jobs and establishing an EV production ecosystem in Chatham County. Construction is set to begin in the second half of 2022, with production expected to start in July 2024.

title: General Motors And Pilot Announce Coast-To-Coast EV Fast Charging Network
summary: General Motors is partnering with Pilot Company to establish a coast-to-coast EV rapid charging network across 500 Pilot Flying J locations. This initiative will include 2,000 charging stalls capable of supplying up to 350 kW, along with amenities, to ease range anxiety and support the adoption of electric vehicles. The project combines private investments with potential government grants to create accessible long-distance EV travel.

summary: The AXS TSLA Bear Daily ETF (TSLQ) has launched, offering investors 1x inverse exposure to Tesla (TSLA) stock. This new leveraged single-stock ETF, which carries a 1.15% expense ratio, is designed for experienced investors seeking to bet against TSLA, which has declined over 40% year-to-date. Both the SEC and Federal Reserve Chair Gary Gensler have warned of the significant risks associated with single-stock ETFs.

summary: AXS Investments has launched single-stock ETFs, including the AXS TSLA Bear Daily ETF (TSLQ), which allows investors to short Tesla. However, the article highlights that these ETFs are a "mind-numbingly dumb" and "very risky" investment due to exorbitant expense ratios (1.15%), daily resets leading to chronic underperformance, and a lack of diversification.
