title: Vimeo is cutting 6% of its jobs
summary: Vimeo is laying off 6% of its workforce, impacting approximately 72 employees. CEO Anjali Sud stated this decision was made to ensure the company remains strong despite challenging market conditions and economic downturn fears. This move follows similar workforce reductions by other tech companies like Tesla, Coinbase, and Meta, as Vimeo shifts its focus from a YouTube alternative to a B2B SaaS solution for corporate clients.

title: What Does GameStop’s Stock Split Mean for Investors?
summary: GameStop (GME) is undergoing a 4-for-1 stock split, its first in 15 years, which will increase the number of shares and decrease the price per share without affecting market capitalization. Morningstar gives GME a 3-star quantitative rating, indicating it is fairly valued, but with extreme uncertainty due to high volatility. This split follows similar actions by other tech and consumer companies like Amazon, Shopify, and Alphabet.

title: Tesla crash victim was 99% to blame for his death, Fla. jury says
summary: A Florida jury found a Tesla crash victim 99% responsible for his own death, assigning only 1% fault to Tesla. This verdict was reached in a court case involving a fatal accident.

title: Expion360 looks to build $450 million facility in Redmond
summary: Expion360, a Redmond-based lithium battery producer, plans to build a $450 million manufacturing facility near its current headquarters. The expansion aims to produce 250,000 to 500,000 lithium cells daily, reduce reliance on overseas production, and create approximately 300 manufacturing jobs in Central Oregon. The company emphasizes vertical integration to control its supply chain and compete with global manufacturers.

title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX, Mattel Team Up on Toys With Space Theme
summary: Mattel Inc. has announced a multiyear agreement with Elon Musk's SpaceX to produce space exploration-themed toys under its Matchbox brand, with products expected to hit the market next year. This collaboration marks the latest partnership between the toy manufacturer, famous for Barbie, and the company founded by the world's richest man. The toys will be inspired by SpaceX's ventures.

title: Tesla Sells 75% of Its Bitcoin Purchases
summary: Tesla announced it sold 75% of its Bitcoin holdings, adding $936 million to its balance sheet in the second quarter. The electric-vehicle maker had invested in Bitcoin little over a year ago, disclosing a $1.5 billion holding when the cryptocurrency was trading above $28,000. The sale comes after a significant slump in cryptocurrency markets, with Bitcoin's price falling below $17,700 in mid-June.

title: Baidu Races Ahead of Tesla With Launch of Robotaxi With Detachable Steering Wheel
summary: Baidu has launched a new autonomous car with a detachable steering wheel, priced at about $37,000, which it intends to use for its robotaxi service by 2023. This move positions Baidu to deploy such vehicles a year ahead of Tesla's plans for mass production of a similar car. The Chinese search giant aims to significantly reduce the cost of autonomous vehicles and expand its robotaxi fleet.

title: The World’s Largest Asset Manager BlackRock Lost $2.46 Trillion In The First Half Of 2022
summary: BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, lost US$1.7 trillion (AU$2.46 trillion) in the first half of 2022 due to tumultuous financial markets, high inflation, and rising interest rates. Assets under management fell 11% to US$8.49 trillion, and adjusted profit decreased significantly compared to 2021. Despite these losses and retail investor withdrawals, the firm still attracted US$89.6 billion in new investments.

title: BHP signs MOU for nickel supply with Ford Motor Company
summary: BHP has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Ford Motor Company for the potential multi-year supply of nickel, set to begin as early as 2025. The agreement focuses on providing sustainable, low-carbon intensity nickel from BHP's Nickel West asset in Western Australia and explores ways to enhance the sustainability and efficiency of battery supply chains. This collaboration aims to meet the growing demand for electric vehicle batteries while prioritizing environmental and ethical considerations.

title: Ford Releases New Battery Capacity Plan, Raw Materials Details to Scale EVs; On Track to Ramp to 600K Run Rate by ’23 and 2M+ by ’26, Leveraging Global Relationships | Great Britain
summary: Ford announced a comprehensive plan to secure battery capacity and raw materials, aiming for an annual run rate of 600,000 electric vehicles by late 2023 and over 2 million by the end of 2026. The strategy includes incorporating lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery chemistry, partnering with CATL, LG Energy Solution, and SK On, and direct-sourcing key raw materials like nickel and lithium from global collaborators. This initiative supports Ford's goal to achieve over 90% compound annual growth for EVs through 2026 and reach carbon neutrality by 2050, with a significant focus on localizing production in North America and expanding in Europe.

title: Ford details battery, raw materials sourcing strategies to support looming EV targets
summary: Ford Motor Co. has outlined its strategies to secure battery capacity and raw materials to meet its ambitious electric vehicle production targets, aiming for 600,000 EVs annually by the end of next year and 2 million by the end of 2026. The company is adding lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells to its portfolio and has signed deals for nickel and lithium supply. These efforts are crucial for Ford to compete in the growing EV market and secure its supply chain.

title: Ford inks deal to get lithium from Nevada’s controversial Rhyolite Ridge mine for its EVs
summary: Ford Motor Company has signed an agreement with Ioneer Ltd. to acquire 7,000 tons of lithium carbonate annually for five years from the Rhyolite Ridge mine in Nevada. This deal aims to support localized battery cell production for Ford's electric vehicles, though it faces opposition from environmental groups due to concerns about the potential impact on the endangered Tiehm’s buckwheat wildflower. Ford is also investing significantly in its EV segment, aiming for 2 million EV production by 2026.

title: Lucid Announces Key Leadership to Bolster Operations and Logistics Experience Ahead of Global Expansion
summary: Lucid Group, Inc. has appointed Evelyn Chiang as VP of Process Transformation and Walter Ludwig as VP of Global Logistics to strengthen its operational and logistical capabilities. These strategic hires bring extensive global expertise from companies like Mercedes, Tesla, and SAP, positioning Lucid for its planned worldwide expansion. Both new VPs will report directly to Lucid's CEO and CTO, Peter Rawlinson, and will lead initiatives to optimize business processes and automotive logistics.

title: USPS to increase size of electric vehicle fleet
summary: The USPS is expanding its electric vehicle fleet by raising the minimum percentage of battery electric vehicles in its next-generation delivery vehicles to at least 50% and buying an additional 34,500 commercial off-the-shelf vehicles. The updated plan increases the electric vehicle commitment from an earlier criticized proposal that included only 10% BEVs. The new vehicles will replace aging models and offer improved fuel efficiency and safety features.

title: 7 Reasons Why People Are Moving to Texas
summary: Texas has become a popular relocation destination, drawing nearly 4 million new residents between 2010 and 2020. This article explores the key factors attracting people to the Lone Star State, including a lower cost of living, more affordable housing, no state income tax, and a thriving job market. Additionally, Texas boasts great schools, a warm climate, and rich cultural diversity, making it an appealing option for many.

title: Baidu unveils autonomous vehicle without steering wheel
summary: Baidu Inc. has unveiled a new autonomous vehicle (AV) with a detachable steering wheel, planning to deploy it for its robotaxi service in China next year. The new model will significantly reduce costs to 250,000 yuan per unit, enabling a larger deployment across China and aiming to make robotaxi rides half the cost of traditional taxis. This Level 4 autonomous vehicle features advanced sensors, and Baidu is awaiting regulatory approval to operate it without a steering wheel.

title: Ford to buy cheaper CATL EV batteries to catch Tesla
summary: Ford Motor Co. announced its plan to import lower-cost lithium iron (LFP) batteries from China's CATL for its North American electric trucks and SUVs to reduce material costs by 10-15% and catch up with Tesla. This move is part of Ford's broader strategy to secure battery capacity and raw materials into the next decade, with aims to build over 2 million EVs worldwide by late 2026 and achieve 8% pretax profit margins on its EVs. Ford also revealed plans to explore strategic alliances with CATL for other global markets and secured agreements for lithium and nickel from various mining companies.

title: 2022 Automotive Hall of Fame Inducts Taiichi Ohno, ‘Father of TPS’
summary: Taiichi Ohno, known as the "Father of TPS" (Toyota Production System), was inducted into the 2022 Automotive Hall of Fame on July 21. His revolutionary manufacturing methods, detailed in several books, transformed the automotive industry globally and continue to impact various societal sectors. Toyota Motor Corporation President Akio Toyoda and Toyota Motor North America executive Chris Nielsen highlighted Ohno's enduring legacy as a pioneer in manufacturing and a key figure in Toyota's history.

title: Elon Musk Promotes Lithium: Here are Four Lithium Stocks to Watch
summary: Elon Musk has encouraged entrepreneurs to enter the lithium refining business, highlighting the massive demand and high margins. This article identifies four lithium stocks—Ioneer Limited, Lithium Americas, Sociedad Quimica, and Piedmont Lithium—that are poised to benefit from the surging demand for this critical element. These companies are involved in various stages of lithium production and have significant projects underway to meet future battery needs.

title: Why This PayPal Investor Avoids PayPal Leveraged ETFs
summary: The author, a long-term PayPal shareholder, explains why he avoids newly launched leveraged single-stock ETFs focusing on PayPal. He argues that despite their potential for amplified gains, the daily resets inherent in leveraged ETFs mean they often underperform the underlying stock over time, especially during volatile periods or extended downturns. The article advises investors seeking returns in PayPal to buy the actual stock instead of these short-term, high-risk leveraged products.

title: Tesla Is Set for Settlement Talks Over Musk Tweets About Taking Company Private
summary: Tesla Inc. is scheduled for court-ordered settlement talks in a shareholder lawsuit concerning CEO Elon Musk's 2018 tweets about taking the company private. This adds to a busy October for Musk, who also faces a trial related to his Twitter acquisition and a trial over his Tesla compensation package. Tesla investors are seeking billions in damages from the disruption caused by the 2018 tweets.

title: GM trails far behind Tesla in EV sales — CEO Mary Barra bet the company that will change
summary: GM CEO Mary Barra is betting the company's future on electric vehicles, despite currently trailing far behind Tesla in sales. GM plans to invest $30 billion in EVs by 2025, launch 30 electric models globally, and believes its Ultium platform will enable it to surpass Tesla by mid-decade or 2029. Barra's legacy is tied to transforming GM into an electric leader, building on past efforts to make the company leaner and more agile.

title: Bitcoin Could Hit 10% Adoption Rate by End of the Decade
summary: Frank Holmes discusses Tesla's sale of Bitcoin and the broader implications for Bitcoin adoption. He refutes claims about Bitcoin mining's environmental impact, highlighting the high percentage of sustainable energy used by miners. The article concludes by citing research predicting Bitcoin could reach 10% global adoption by 2030, leading to parabolic growth and significant wealth generation for long-term holders.

title: Apple's earnings will give a peek into the mindset of the high-end consumer
summary: Apple is set to report its third-quarter earnings, which analysts and investors will closely scrutinize for insights into the impact of macroeconomic trends like inflation and rising interest rates on high-end consumer spending. While Apple's sales have historically been robust due to its affluent customer base, any indication of slowing demand for iPhones and Macs could signal broader economic concerns. The company's performance will also reflect its ability to manage supply chain issues and COVID-19 lockdowns in China, as well as the growth trajectory of its services business.

title: GM and Livent enter long-term lithium hydroxide supply agreement
summary: General Motors (GM) and Livent have announced a multi-year sourcing agreement for battery-grade lithium hydroxide, crucial for GM's Ultium battery cathodes. This partnership aims to secure a sustainable supply chain for GM's electric vehicles, with a goal to transition 100% of Livent's downstream lithium hydroxide processing for GM to North America over the six-year agreement. The agreement supports GM's objective of 1 million units of EV capacity in North America by the end of 2025.

title: GM hit by supply chain issues, remains optimistic for vehicle demand, pricing
summary: General Motors' second-quarter net income dropped 40% due to supply chain issues, particularly semiconductor chip shortages, leaving over 90,000 vehicles unfinished. Despite this, the company maintained its full-year forecast and expressed optimism about strong vehicle demand and pricing. GM is also advancing its electric vehicle plans, aiming for significant EV production capacity by 2025 and securing key raw material agreements.

title: Has the Crypto Winter Come and Gone?
summary: The crypto market is showing signs of recovery after a significant downturn, with positive price action in Bitcoin and Ethereum. Edward Moya suggests a "positive risk-on mood" is benefiting cryptos, aligning with easing expectations for Fed tightening. However, some analysts caution that despite recent gains, the market is still in a "full-blown bear market."

title: Auto Advertising: What’s Ahead for Marketers
summary: The article explores the evolving landscape of auto advertising, highlighting the shift in car-buying habits towards digital-first experiences and the increasing importance of online research. It emphasizes the role of native advertising on the open web as a critical strategy for auto brands to reach consumers, focusing on data-driven insights and case studies showing successful campaigns by Volvo, Peugeot, and Honda.

title: WSJ stands by Elon Musk affair report: “We are confident in our sourcing”
summary: The Wall Street Journal is standing by its report alleging an affair between Elon Musk and Nicole Shanahan, Sergey Brin's former wife, despite Musk's denials and Shanahan's lawyer calling the report false and defamatory. Musk has publicly refuted the claims, stating that he spoke to both Brin and Shanahan, who denied being sources for the story, and that he does not plan legal action against the Journal. The WSJ maintains confidence in its sourcing and reporting.

title: Aspen Aerogels posts $24M loss in Q2
summary: Aspen Aerogels Inc. reported a significant loss of $24.1 million in the second quarter of 2022, a substantial increase from the $6.7 million loss in the same period last year. Despite the financial loss, the company saw a rise in revenue, reaching $45.6 million. CEO Donald R. Young highlighted increasing market adoption of their thermal and EV safety solutions and ongoing investments in manufacturing facilities and teams to support future growth and profitability goals.

title: 2023 Chevrolet Colorado Comes in 3 Off-Road Flavors
summary: The 2023 Chevrolet Colorado undergoes a full redesign, featuring a more aggressive exterior, a single four-door crew cab/short box configuration, and a turbocharged 2.7-liter four-cylinder engine with three power output levels. The new model offers three distinct off-road trims (Z71, Trail Boss, ZR2) and significantly upgraded interior technology, including an 11.3-inch touchscreen and an 8-inch digital instrument panel. While fuel economy and pricing are yet to be released, the redesign aims to make the Colorado more competitive in the mid-size pickup segment.

title: GC/CLO hiring roundup: Opendoor names Syndey Schaub its chief legal officer
summary: Opendoor has appointed Sydney Schaub as its new chief legal officer, bringing her experience from Gemini, Rent the Runway, and Square to the residential real estate platform. J.Crew Group, FreeWire, Kepler Group, and Aledade also announced significant legal leadership appointments, showcasing a trend of companies bringing in experienced legal professionals to navigate complex business environments and drive strategic growth. These hires emphasize the increasing importance of legal expertise in corporate decision-making across various industries.

title: Cybersecurity in spotlight with participant's suit against Colgate-Palmolive
summary: A lawsuit filed against Colgate-Palmolive has brought cybersecurity for defined contribution plans into the spotlight. The article highlights this development along with other financial news, including delays in SEC work on private credit for retirement plans and a CIO's strategy for portfolio overhaul.

title: Risk Parity Explained (2023): Complete Investor's Guide ✅
summary: This guide explains risk parity as an investment strategy that equalizes risk levels across all portfolio components, utilizing tools like leverage and short selling. It details how risk parity differs from modern portfolio theory by focusing on risk allocation rather than capital allocation, aiming for lower volatility and improved returns. The article also covers the practical aspects of building and managing a risk parity portfolio, including its pros and cons, and its performance in various market conditions.

title: From Boeing Starliner to Goodyear Tesla tire, 3-D printing is becoming manufacturing reality
summary: 3-D printing, or additive manufacturing, is increasingly being adopted by major industrial companies like Goodyear, Boeing, GE, Caterpillar, and Cummins, despite still representing a small fraction of the overall manufacturing market. Goodyear has opened a $77 million plant focusing on 3-D printing for high-performance tires and is testing airless 3-D printed tires on Teslas and delivery robots. Boeing is also extensively using 3-D printing for satellite components, aircraft parts, and tooling, leading to reduced lead times and costs, though the technology still faces adoption challenges like high investment costs and a need for cultural shifts in engineering.

title: Shenzhen accelerates China's driverless car dreams
summary: Shenzhen has introduced China's clearest regulations for autonomous vehicles, allowing registered AVs to operate without a driver in the driving seat across a broad area, but a human driver must still be present in the vehicle. This regulatory framework is critical for the mass deployment of robotaxis and addresses liability in case of accidents. While the U.S. has led in AV trials, China, particularly Shenzhen, is rapidly accelerating its own autonomous driving efforts with significant industry investments and ambitious revenue targets.

title: NIO, XPeng, and Li Auto Deliveries Cool Off in July. The Stocks Jump Anyway.
summary: Deliveries for Chinese electric vehicle makers NIO, XPeng, and Li Auto saw a cooling off in July compared to June, despite year-over-year growth for NIO. Despite this dip in sales, which could be concerning for the broader EV market including Tesla, investors reacted positively to the initial delivery numbers. This suggests that the market may have anticipated typical summer seasonal selling patterns.

title: The Neocolonial Game Behind Musk-Bolsonaro Rendezvous
summary: This article criticizes Elon Musk's meeting with Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, framing it as a neocolonial act driven by resource acquisition and political manipulation. It highlights concerns about Musk's Starlink project in the Amazon, linking it to Brazil's nickel and lithium reserves, and questions the integrity of Bolsonaro's government in its dealings with foreign interests given its past dismantling of environmental monitoring bodies. The author suggests the collaboration serves to undermine Brazil's democratic processes and exploit its natural wealth for corporate gain.

title: Musk’s antics turn Tesla owners, new buyers against it
summary: Elon Musk’s controversial behavior and public statements are increasingly alienating both current Tesla owners and potential new buyers, despite the company’s previous growth through controversies. While customers generally love their Tesla vehicles, many are becoming put off by Musk's antics, leading some to consider alternative electric vehicle brands despite Tesla's initial market dominance. This shift indicates that as more capable EV options emerge, Tesla may lose its competitive edge among consumers who prioritize a CEO's conduct.

title: Citigroup to launch hiring spree
summary: Citigroup announced plans to hire 500 employees over the next three years for its new "Wealth at Work" division, a move that bucks the recent trend of layoffs and hiring freezes across several industries. This initiative aims to serve junior employees at private equity and accounting firms, with the goal of retaining these clients as their careers advance. The article contrasts Citigroup's expansion with widespread workforce reductions and hiring slowdowns seen in tech, media, and other financial companies.

title: Alibaba and Tesla Rival XPeng Are Teaming Up. Why the Stocks Are Falling.
summary: Chinese tech giant Alibaba and electric-vehicle company XPeng have formed a partnership to develop self-driving car technology. Despite this collaboration, the stock prices of both companies have not seen a positive uplift. XPeng is a notable competitor to Tesla and NIO in the Chinese electric vehicle market.

title: Toyota likely to post lower Q1 profit as production woes cast shadow
summary: Toyota Motor Corp is anticipated to announce a significant decrease in its first-quarter profit due to persistent chip shortages and supply chain disruptions that led to multiple production target cuts. Despite a weaker yen that typically benefits exporters, the company faces substantial challenges including ongoing material shortfalls, rising costs, and longer-term issues like vehicle electrification and automation. Analysts are keen to see if Toyota can maintain its global vehicle production target for the financial year ending March, which largely depends on the resolution of chip shortages and the economic outlook.

title: BorgWarner Acquires Rhombus Energy Solutions
summary: BorgWarner Inc. has acquired Rhombus Energy Solutions for up to $185 million, with an initial payment of $130 million. This acquisition expands BorgWarner's electric vehicle portfolio in North America, complementing its existing European charging business. The strategic move supports BorgWarner's "Charging Forward" strategy by strengthening its position in V2G DC Fast Charging and enabling software, aiming to power the entire propulsion system from grid to wheels.

title: GM to expand its hands-free Super Cruise system to span 400,000 miles, including Route 66 and the Pacific Coast Highway
summary: General Motors is expanding its Super Cruise hands-free driving system in the U.S. and Canada to include non-interstate roadways like Route 66 and the Pacific Coast Highway. This expansion will increase the system's usability to over 400,000 miles of roads, doubling its previous coverage. The update, provided via over-the-air updates for eligible vehicles, aims to reach millions more customers, while GM emphasizes safety measures and its conservative approach compared to competitors like Tesla.

title: Do US Large Cap Equity Index Funds Put Your Clients at Risk?
summary: This article argues that large-cap equity index funds currently pose a significant risk to investors due to an unusually high concentration of overvalued stocks, reminiscent of the dot-com bubble in 1999. The authors, from Kailash Concepts Research, highlight a shift in valuation structures within these funds, with a much larger portion of investments now in stocks with price-to-sales ratios above 10x. They suggest that this trend is driven by market cap-weighted indexing and continuous inflows, creating a self-perpetuating cycle that could lead to substantial losses if flows reverse.

title: U.S. crude oil falls below $90 a barrel, Coinbase stock pops on BlackRock partnership
summary: U.S. crude oil prices dropped below $90 a barrel for the first time since the invasion of Ukraine, erasing all gains made since that event. Meanwhile, Coinbase stock surged over 22% after announcing a partnership with BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, to facilitate institutional investment in Bitcoin. This partnership is seen as a significant boost for Coinbase during the ongoing "crypto winter."

title: Tesla shareholders broadly follow board recommendations at annual meeting
summary: Tesla shareholders largely supported the board's recommendations at the annual meeting, including re-electing directors and approving a three-for-one stock split. However, they rejected most environmental and governance proposals. A proposal to increase investors' ability to nominate directors passed despite board opposition, and CEO Elon Musk stated the company aims for a 2 million vehicle production run rate by the end of 2022 and expects 10-12 gigafactories eventually.

title: Rick Winick Honeywell’s VP of Automotive Refrigerants on EVs
summary: Rick Winick, Honeywell’s VP and General Manager of Automotive Refrigerants, discusses how Honeywell's HFO-1234yf refrigerant can help reduce "range anxiety" in electric vehicles (EVs) by improving thermal management and efficiency. He highlights the challenges facing the EV market, such as extending driving range and lowering MSRPs, and explains how energy-efficient refrigerants can address these issues. Winick notes that HFO-1234yf is a globally available, field-proven solution that can be used in both internal combustion engine and EV heat pump systems to optimize thermal control of the cabin and electronic components.

title: Tesla (TSLA) Shareholders Approve 3-For-1 Stock Split
summary: Tesla (TSLA) shareholders approved a 3-for-1 stock split at the company's annual meeting on August 4, 2022. This decision aims to increase the accessibility of its stock to retail investors and offer employees more flexibility in managing their equity. Additionally, a proposal to increase shareholders' ability to nominate board candidates also appears to have passed.

title: Tesla sets Aug 25 as trading day for three-for-one split shares
summary: Tesla announced that trading for its three-for-one split shares will commence on August 25, following shareholder approval during its annual meeting. Shareholders of record on August 17 will receive two additional shares for each share held, distributed after the close of trading on August 24. This split aims to make the stock more accessible to a wider range of investors, much like its prior five-for-one split in 2020 which bolstered share price accessibility.

title: California regulator claims Tesla falsely advertised Autopilot, Full Self-Driving
summary: A California state transportation regulator has accused Tesla of falsely advertising its Autopilot and Full Self-Driving features, alleging the company misled customers about their autonomous capabilities. The Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) filed complaints stating that Tesla's advertising overstated the systems' functionality, despite the company's disclaimers. The DMV is seeking remedies that could include suspending Tesla's license to sell vehicles in California and mandating restitution to drivers, highlighting concerns about the safety and accuracy of Tesla's self-driving claims.

title: Better Buy: iShares S&P Core 500 Small Cap ETF or Vanguard S&P 500 ETF?
summary: This article compares the iShares S&P Core 500 Small Cap ETF (IJR) and the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO), discussing their features, risks, and benefits for investors. While VOO offers stability with large-cap companies, IJR provides potential for higher upside with small-cap stocks, albeit with increased volatility. The choice between them depends on an investor's strategy, risk tolerance, and investment goals.

title: These Stocks are Buzzing Thanks to the US Senate Passing $430B Climate Bill
summary: The US Senate passed the $430 billion Inflation Reduction Act, allocating about $370 billion to climate and energy programs, causing clean energy stocks and related ETFs to rally. Electric vehicle companies like Tesla, Rivian, and Lucid Group saw gains, while pharmaceutical giants Pfizer, Sanofi, and Eli Lilly experienced slight declines due to Medicare drug price negotiation provisions. The bill's passage into law is expected to benefit the clean energy sector, despite earlier volatility influenced by Senator Manchin's stance.

title: BRP’s famed two-wheeled motorcycles are back — with an electric twist
summary: BRP Inc. has announced its re-entry into the two-wheeled motorcycle market with the introduction of its first all-electric models, the Can-Am Origin and Can-Am Pulse, along with an electric surfboard, the Sea-Doo Rise. These new electric vehicles mark a significant step in the company's electrification strategy and will be available for purchase in mid-2024. BRP aims to become a leader in the electric powersport vehicle market, emphasizing the benefits of a silent, vibration-free, and environmentally friendly riding experience.

title: Tesla hires Hewlett Packard Enterprise lawyer for senior legal post
summary: Tesla has hired Derek Windham, formerly of Hewlett Packard Enterprise, as its new deputy general counsel for corporate and securities. This move comes as the electric carmaker continues to restructure its legal department amidst various high-profile legal disputes involving the company and its CEO Elon Musk. Windham's role will involve leading the company's global corporate, securities, and corporate governance work.

title: BlackRock launches S&P 500 equal weight and ESG ETFs
summary: BlackRock has introduced two new S&P 500 ETFs: the iShares S&P 500 ESG UCITS ETF (ESPX) and the iShares S&P 500 Equal Weight UCITS ETF (EWSP). These launches expand BlackRock's ETF range, offering exposures to ESG and equal-weight methodologies. The S&P 500 ESG index notably overweights information technology and includes a modest extra allocation to energy despite previously ejecting Tesla, while the S&P 500 Equal Weight index overweights cyclical sectors.

title: Groupon lays off hundreds of employees
summary: Groupon, the Chicago-based e-commerce marketplace, has laid off more than 500 employees, approximately 15% of its workforce, across various departments. This decision comes as the company restructures to focus on "self-service merchant acquisition capabilities," reduce cloud infrastructure, and rationalize its real estate footprint, citing that its overall business performance is not meeting anticipated levels and its cost structure is not aligned with its performance. Groupon joins a growing list of companies including Fender, Robinhood, Apple, Google, Vox Media, 7-Eleven, Meta, JPMorgan Chase & Co., Coinbase, Netflix, and Tesla that have recently announced layoffs or slowing hiring efforts ahead of an anticipated economic downturn.

title: With Tesla stock sale Musk cashes up for Twitter
summary: Elon Musk sold nearly $7 billion worth of Tesla shares to secure funds for his potential acquisition of Twitter, aiming to avoid an emergency stock sale if he is compelled to complete the deal. This move comes ahead of a legal battle with Twitter over the $44bn takeover, with Musk indicating he would buy back Tesla stock if the deal does not close. Legal experts suggest he might need to sell more shares if he loses the legal challenge and is forced to acquire Twitter or pay a hefty penalty.

title: Musk Says Tesla Will Begin Shipping Semis Later This Year
summary: Elon Musk announced via Twitter that Tesla plans to start shipping its Semi truck later this year, with the Cybertruck to follow in 2023. This announcement comes as Musk recently sold a significant amount of Tesla stock, totaling $6.9 billion, to prepare for a potential legal battle over his agreement to acquire Twitter. Analysts suggest Musk's stock sale might be a tactical move before a possible market downturn and amid the ongoing Twitter acquisition uncertainty.

title: Elon Musk sells $7 billion in Tesla shares ahead of Twitter court battle
summary: Elon Musk has sold nearly $7 billion worth of Tesla shares to prepare for the possibility of being forced to acquire Twitter or facing a significant settlement. This sale comes as Musk faces a court battle with Twitter over his attempted withdrawal from the $44 billion acquisition deal. Analysts suggest a Twitter deal is more likely, or at least a substantial settlement for Twitter from Musk.

title: TSL Stock Fund Price and Chart — NASDAQ:TSL
summary: This article provides detailed information about the GraniteShares 1.25x Long TSLA Daily ETF (TSL), including its price, chart, key statistics like AUM and expense ratio, and fund structure. It highlights that TSL is a short-term tactical tool designed to deliver 1.25x the daily price return of Tesla stock, emphasizing the need for daily monitoring due to its leveraged nature and the risks involved. The article also includes FAQs about ETFs and TSL's specifics, along with technical analysis and seasonal trends.

title: VinFast SUVs: Reviews, Pricing, and Spec
summary: This article provides an overview of VinFast, a Vietnamese automaker that has expanded into the global market with electric SUVs. It details their plans for a U.S. factory in North Carolina and outlines specifications, estimated pricing, and reviews for their upcoming electric vehicle models, including the VF3, VF6, VF7, VF8, VF9, and VF Wild pickup truck. The article also includes a news section highlighting recent developments for the company.

title: Ford CEO Jim Farley warns EV battery raw material costs will likely stay high
summary: Ford CEO Jim Farley anticipates that the high costs of raw materials for EV batteries, particularly lithium, cobalt, and nickel, will persist due to demand outpacing supply. This has led Ford to increase prices for its electric F-150 Lightning and explore alternative battery technologies, such as lower-cost lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries and solid-state technology. Despite these efforts, consumers can expect continued price increases in the near future for electric vehicles.

title: Aurora delays autonomous truck launch following supplier constraints
summary: Aurora Innovation has delayed the commercial launch of its self-driving truck by a year, pushing its rollout to the first half of 2024, due to difficulties in securing tier 1 suppliers for truck hardware. The company, in partnership with Paccar, faced supply chain constraints that hindered scaling production of its purpose-built autonomous trucks. This delay mirrors similar challenges faced by competitors in the autonomous vehicle sector who are also contending with supply shortages for components.

title: 3 Stock Winners and Losers of Biden’s Inflation Reduction Act
summary: The Inflation Reduction Act, passed by the House on Aug. 12, is expected to generate $739 billion in revenue with significant spending directed towards climate change initiatives and an extension of ACA tax credits. This article identifies the First Trust Nasdaq Clean Edge Green Energy Index Fund (QCLN) as a key winner due to enhanced clean energy tax credits, while the First Trust Dow 30 Equal Weight ETF (EDOW) and Invesco BuyBack Achievers ETF (PKW) are highlighted as potential losers due to new corporate minimum tax and a 1% excise tax on share repurchases, respectively.

title: NIO Rumored To Begin Selling EVs In The US By 2025
summary: Chinese EV automaker NIO is rumored to start selling vehicles in the United States by 2025. The company, known for its battery-swapping technology and luxury EVs, has reportedly posted job openings for its "NIO Houses" (showrooms) and is considering building a factory in the US to circumnavigate tariffs and tax credit restrictions. While not confirmed, the evidence, including existing US offices and frequent sightings of NIO SUVs in California, suggests serious intent for global expansion.

title: Inflation Reduction Act Could Provide Major Boost for Renewable Energy and CleanTech Industries
summary: The Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), representing the U.S. government's largest investment in combating climate change, is expected to significantly boost the renewable energy and CleanTech industries. With nearly $370 billion directed towards climate change mitigation, energy security, and lowering energy costs, the bill aims to put the U.S. on an accelerated path toward achieving its 2030 net greenhouse gas emissions reduction goal. This legislation is anticipated to create substantial investment opportunities across various climate-related themes, including renewable energy, low-carbon hydrogen, and electric vehicles.

title: SCE’s Pre-Owned EV Rebate Has Nationwide Impact
summary: Southern California Edison's (SCE) Pre-Owned EV Rebate Program inspired the $4,000 used-EV federal tax credit included in the Inflation Reduction Act. This federal incentive, similar to SCE's program, aims to make clean energy more accessible nationwide. The article details the credit's specifics and how similar incentives for EV purchase are key to meeting clean energy goals.

title: 2 Long-Term EV Plays Trading Under $20
summary: The article highlights two long-term electric vehicle (EV) investment opportunities trading under $20: Ford Motor Company (NYSE: F) and ChargePoint Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: CHPT). Ford is praised for its aggressive push into EV production and carbon neutrality, with strong growth potential and a low P/E ratio compared to Tesla. ChargePoint is presented as a leading EV charging network operator, poised for growth through its expanding network and subscription-based model, despite not yet being profitable.

title: Tesla denies that legal chief who conducted internal probe has left
summary: Tesla has denied reports that its legal chief, who was involved in an internal probe, has left the company. The article briefly mentions this denial.

title: The Shyft Group debuts a portable EV charging solution
summary: The Shyft Group has introduced the Blue Arc Power Cube, a portable, remote-controlled EV charging station designed to address the lack of EV infrastructure. This unit provides 3MW of onboard power with Level 2 and Fast-DC charging capabilities, and it can be supplemented by wind and solar power, offering a flexible and grid-independent solution for commercial vehicle fleets. Its portability makes it an ideal solution for fleets that lease facilities or need to move charging stations.

title: Sonic Automotive buys Audi store in Maryland from AutoNation
summary: Sonic Automotive has acquired an Audi dealership located in Owings Mills, Maryland, from AutoNation. The transaction was reported in an Automotive News article by Jack Walsworth on August 18, 2022. This move represents a strategic acquisition for Sonic Automotive in the retail automotive sector.

title: Top 13 meme stocks on Reddit right now: Bed Bath & Beyond goes bananas as retail investors return with a vengeance
summary: Meme stocks have seen a resurgence on Reddit, with Bed Bath & Beyond (BBBY) leading the charge with a 360% increase in August, prompting concerns about speculative excesses. The trend, fueled by individual investors coordinating on online forums, targets heavily shorted companies, despite warnings from analysts about the fundamental irrationality of such valuations. HypeEquity identifies current top meme stocks based on social mentions and trending activity, including GameStop and Best Buy, highlighting the challenge for investors to predict the next big mover.

title: Tesla Supercharger network ranks highest in customer satisfaction, finds J.D. Power
summary: A J.D. Power study found that the Tesla Supercharger network leads in customer satisfaction for DC fast-charging with a score of 739, significantly above the industry average. While most EV owners are satisfied with the ease of public charging, reliability remains a major concern, with 20% of respondents unable to charge due to malfunctioning equipment. Tesla plans to triple the size of its Supercharger network and may open it to other EV brands, potentially using federal funding.

title: Time to Buy ARKQ While It’s Still Trading at a Discount
summary: The article suggests now is a good time to invest in the ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ) due to its growth potential and current discounted trading price. ARKQ provides exposure to companies involved in disruptive innovation, autonomous technology, and robotics, and is actively managed by ARK Invest. Despite its 75 basis points management fee, it is considered inexpensive for active management, targeting investors seeking long-term alpha by riding out short-term market fluctuations.

title: 2023 Kia EV6 GT: Performance Soars As Range Sinks
summary: The 2023 Kia EV6 GT offers significantly enhanced performance with 576 hp, AWD, and a 0-60 mph time of 3.4 seconds, thanks to its larger battery and sport-tuned suspension. However, this power comes at the cost of a reduced estimated range of 206 miles, compared to the standard EV6 models and key competitors. The GT model also features unique visual tweaks and customizable drive modes to differentiate it.

title: General Motors reinstates dividend; CEO Mary Barra cites confidence driven by electric vehicle growth
summary: General Motors (GM) has reinstated its dividend, with CEO Mary Barra attributing this decision to confidence driven by the company's growth in electric vehicles. Barra previously stated GM's aim to double its annual revenue by 2030 through a focus on electric and autonomous vehicles, connected services, and new businesses. The reinstatement of dividends signals GM's financial stability and strategic shift towards its EV portfolio.

title: Ex-HP finance manager jailed after going on $5m spending spree using company plastic
summary: A former HP finance manager, Shelbee Szeto, has been sentenced to three years in prison for wire fraud and money laundering after misusing company credit cards for a $4.8 million spending spree on luxury items. Szeto, who created bogus merchant accounts to funnel funds, also failed to report the income to the IRS. She expressed remorse, attributing her actions to addiction and a desire to impress others, and will serve three years of supervised release after her prison term.

title: GM restores quarterly dividend after more than two years
summary: General Motors Co (GM.N) announced the reinstatement of its quarterly dividend payouts, signaling confidence in its recovery from the pandemic's impact and recent economic turbulence. The first dividend of 9 cents per share will be paid on September 15, 2022. GM also increased its share repurchase program capacity to $5.0 billion, highlighting its strengthened financial position and commitment to returning capital to shareholders amidst its electric vehicle expansion.

title: Why the ESG/Tech Combination Is Important
summary: Broad market environmental, social, and governance (ESG) exchange-traded funds (ETFs) frequently have significant allocations to technology stocks. For example, the Invesco ESG Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQMG) has a technology weight of almost 62%. While some critics view this as over-reliance on tech, experts argue that technology companies often embody sustainable development principles, making them suitable for ESG funds despite facing scrutiny on issues like data privacy and energy consumption.

title: Vanilla Total Stock Funds Lag Active Counterparts
summary: This article explores why broad cap-weighted index funds underperformed active counterparts in the first half of 2022, despite the long-held belief that passive investing generally outperforms active after costs. The author attributes this anomaly to imperfect benchmarking methodologies rather than flaws in William Sharpe's arithmetic of active management or superior stock-picking prowess by active managers. The article concludes that low-cost market cap-weighted total index funds remain superior investments both psychologically and mathematically over the long term.

title: Ford is laying off about 3,000 workers
summary: Ford Motor Co. is laying off approximately 3,000 white-collar and contract workers in the U.S. and Canada as part of a restructuring effort to lower costs and accelerate its transition to electric vehicles. The cuts, which represent about 6% of its salaried workforce in the region, come after the company's executive chairman and CEO emphasized the need to reshape operations and improve competitiveness against rivals like General Motors, Stellantis, and Tesla. Ford aims to streamline its business by eliminating redundant work and reorganizing functions across its various units.

title: Musk seeks documents from Jack Dorsey in fight over Twitter deal
summary: Elon Musk is seeking documents from Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey as part of his legal battle to terminate the $44 billion acquisition deal. Musk's subpoena requests communications and documents regarding his April agreement to buy Twitter and information about spam accounts, a key issue in his claim that Twitter violated the contract. Dorsey, who supported Musk's offer and shares views on Twitter's algorithm and subscription model, leads Block Inc.

title: Ex-Apple engineer admits stealing automotive trade secrets
summary: A former Apple engineer named Xiaolang Zhang pleaded guilty to stealing confidential automotive trade secrets from Apple. Zhang was indicted in 2018 for obtaining a 25-page document detailing a circuit board for Apple's autonomous vehicle project, shortly after announcing his departure to work for Chinese EV maker Xpeng. Xpeng has denied involvement in the case, while also being a competitor in the autonomous driving space.

title: These Wide-Moat Stocks Are Gaining Ground
summary: Quality stocks with wide economic moats, including Microsoft and Amazon, have outperformed since the bear market low in June, despite still being undervalued. While narrow-moat stocks have seen stronger recent gains due to market-cap weighting of companies like Apple and Tesla, wide-moat companies are better positioned to handle inflation due to their pricing power. Overall, Morningstar analysts consider wide-moat stocks to be deeply undervalued compared to overpriced narrow-moat stocks.

title: PG&E, Tesla virtual power plant delivers 16.5 MW to California grid amid calls for energy conservation
summary: Nearly 2,500 PG&E customers with Tesla battery systems contributed up to 16.5 MW of solar power to California's grid, marking the first activation of the virtual power plant. This initiative comes as California faces high temperatures and calls for energy conservation, with participating customers receiving $2/kWh for exported electricity. The program aims to bolster grid reliability during peak demand and emergencies.

title: 3 Cathie Wood Stocks That Could Double by 2025
summary: This article identifies three Cathie Wood-backed stocks – Roku (ROKU), Twilio (TWLO), and Shopify (SHOP) – that possess the potential to double their value by 2025 despite facing recent market downturns. The author analyzes each company's current performance, challenges, and growth prospects, highlighting factors that could drive their recovery and significant appreciation within the next few years. The article emphasizes that while these stocks have seen substantial declines, their underlying businesses and long-term forecasts suggest strong rebound potential.

title: Starbox Group (STBX) Stock Price, News & Analysis
summary: This article provides an overview of Starbox Group (STBX), including its stock price, company information, and recent news. Starbox Group engages in cash rebate and digital advertising services in Malaysia through its GETBATS, SEEBATS, and PAYBATS platforms. Recent headlines highlight a share consolidation effective April 15, 2025, a staff determination notice from Nasdaq, and a significant stock price decline.

title: Tesla's former energy head launches startup to compete against Powerwall with key partners
summary: Kunal Girotra, formerly Tesla's head of energy products, has launched a new startup called Lunar Energy to compete with Tesla's Powerwall. Lunar Energy secured $300 million in funding from Sunrun and SK Group and plans to introduce a home battery system and home electrification products. The company also acquired Moixa, a software company specializing in distributed energy resources management, to integrate intelligent software with its hardware offerings.

title: It’s official: California is phasing out gas-powered cars by 2035
summary: California has officially voted to ban the sale of new gas-powered cars by 2035. This move by the California Air Resources Board aims to transition the state to 100 percent zero-emission vehicle sales, building on Governor Gavin Newsom's 2020 executive order. While facing concerns from automakers and environmental justice groups regarding affordability and infrastructure, the rule is projected to deliver significant environmental and public health benefits.

title: Opinion: Touchscreens in cars are a menace
summary: This article argues that touchscreens in modern cars are a dangerous menace, citing a Swedish study by *Vi Bilägare* that found operating common vehicle functions via a touchscreen takes significantly longer and covers more distance than traditional physical buttons. The author, James Mills, contends that while manufacturers claim innovation and cost-saving, these systems increase driver distraction and reduce safety, sparking widespread agreement among commenters who advocate for the return of tactile controls.

title: Tesla shares close lower after 3-1 stock split
summary: Tesla's shares closed 2% lower after its three-for-one stock split took effect, aimed at attracting retail investors. The stock opened at $302 and closed at $296.07 after previously closing at $891.29 before the split. This marks Tesla's second stock split in two years, a strategy adopted by high-growth companies to make shares more affordable for individual investors.

title: Marsh McLennan's Mercer restructures investments and retirement group leadership
summary: Mercer, a Marsh McLennan company, is restructuring the leadership of its investments and retirement group. This move indicates strategic changes within the company regarding how it manages these core areas. The article, published by Pensions & Investments, details this significant organizational change.

title: Legal Alert | A Guide to the Renewable Energy Provisions of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022
summary: This legal alert from Husch Blackwell provides a comprehensive guide to the renewable energy provisions within the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (IRA). The IRA, signed into law on August 16, 2022, is described as the most significant climate change legislation in U.S. history, offering substantial incentives and credits to the renewable energy industry. The guide categorizes and details various provisions related to clean electricity, fuels, individual incentives, clean vehicles, manufacturing investment, Superfund, and credit monetization.

title: S&P Global Mobility US Monthly Light Vehicle Sales Preview, August 2022: US Light Vehicle Sales to mark first YOY gain in 12 months, according to S&P Global Mobility projection
summary: S&P Global Mobility projected the first year-over-year gain in US light vehicle sales in 12 months for August 2022, estimating 1.123 million units. Electric vehicles are becoming a significant market segment, comprising 6.0% of sales in August, a trend expected to continue despite broader industry challenges like constrained inventories and increasing economic uncertainty. The yearly forecast has been downgraded to 14.1 million units due to these persistent supply chain issues and rising vehicle prices impacting consumer demand.

title: Tesla announces 3-for-1 stock split
summary: Tesla Inc. announced a three-for-one stock split, aimed at diversifying its investor base and making shares more accessible to individual investors. This is Tesla's second stock split, following a five-for-one split in August 2020. The move is seen as an acknowledgment of the importance of retail investors, despite the availability of fractional shares through many brokerages.

title: Mirae Asset Global Electric & Autonomous Vehicles ETFs Fund of Fund: Should You Invest?
summary: This article evaluates the Mirae Asset Global Electric & Autonomous Vehicles ETFs Fund of Fund, highlighting the significant growth in the EV/AV sector and government policies supporting it. The fund aims to provide long-term capital appreciation by investing in overseas equity ETFs focused on companies involved in the EV/AV value chain. It discusses the investment strategy, asset allocation, and potential risks, concluding that it is suitable for investors with a decent understanding of the new-age automobile segment and a long-term investment horizon.

title: Elon Musk Says Nuclear Plants Must Remain Open. Uranium Stocks Are Surging.
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has publicly stated his support for keeping nuclear power plants operational, leading to a surge in the stock prices of several uranium mining companies. Musk's comments underscore a growing debate about the role of nuclear energy in global power grids, particularly in the context of energy security and climate change.

title: Honda and LG will jointly build a U.S. battery plant.
summary: Honda and LG Energy Solution announced a joint venture to build a battery plant in the United States, supporting Honda's new electric vehicle lineup. This initiative is part of a broader industry-wide push by automakers to increase EV production and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, with many similar plants being planned or constructed by major manufacturers like GM, Ford, and Toyota. The move comes as regulations, such as California's planned ban on new gasoline-powered vehicle sales by 2035, accelerate the transition to electric vehicles.

title: Uranium Stocks Soar As Elon Musk Applauds the Alternative Energy Source
summary: Uranium stocks are rising amidst increasing global interest in nuclear power as an alternative energy source. This interest is driven by the ongoing global energy crisis and the war in Ukraine. Elon Musk has voiced his approval for the return to nuclear energy and highlighted the need for fossil fuels in the short term to maintain civilization.

title: Hyundai narrows Level 3 self-driving tech gap with Tesla to one year
summary: Hyundai Motor Co. has significantly narrowed its Level 3 self-driving technology gap with Tesla to just one year, with plans to launch Level 3 cars starting with the Genesis G90 later this year. The company aims to surpass Tesla in system computation speeds within a few years and intends to roll out fully autonomous vehicles by 2030. Hyundai also revealed it has cross-checked its technology by disassembling a Tesla Model 3 and plans to reduce integrated controllers in future IONIQ models for better efficiency.

title: U.S. agency: 'unlawful' for Tesla to prevent employees from wearing union shirts
summary: The National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) ruled that it was unlawful for Tesla Inc. to prohibit employees from wearing shirts with union insignia, reaffirming the right to display union clothing. This decision stems from a 2017 dispute with the United Automobile Workers (UAW) union and reverses a prior 2019 NLRB ruling involving Walmart Inc. The NLRB ordered Tesla to rescind its policy against union shirts, noting this is not the first clash between Tesla and the agency.

title: Honda Motor, LG Energy to build $4.4 bln U.S. EV battery plant
summary: Honda Motor and LG Energy Solution announced a joint venture to build a $4.4 billion lithium-ion battery plant for electric vehicles in the U.S., with a target annual production capacity of 40 GWh. The batteries will exclusively supply Honda facilities in North America for Honda and Acura EV models, with construction planned for early 2023 and mass production by the end of 2025. This move aligns with U.S. government policies pushing for domestic battery and EV manufacturing and comes as the country implements stricter regulations and tax credit eligibility for EVs.

title: Which Charging Networks Can your EV Access?
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to electric vehicle (EV) charging networks in the U.S., detailing which networks are compatible with various 2022 and 2023 EV models. It explains that most EVs use standard Level 2 and DC fast-charging connectors, with exceptions like Tesla's Supercharger and Rivian's Adventure Network. The article also lists incentives offered by automakers for specific charging networks.

title: 10 features from the ’80s and ’90s that either hit hard or missed big
summary: This article looks back at ten automotive innovations from the 1980s and 1990s, categorizing them as either a "hit" or a "miss." It examines features like four-wheel steering, digital dashboards, pop-up headlamps, keyless entry, electronic stability control, and satellite navigation, discussing their initial reception and long-term impact on car design and technology. The author highlights how some ideas were ahead of their time, while others were flawed in execution or eventually replaced by better solutions.

title: Lincoln Electric Launches a DC Fast Charge EV Charger Initiative
summary: Lincoln Electric Holdings has announced a new initiative to design and manufacture DC fast charge electric vehicle (EV) chargers for the U.S. market. The company has developed a scalable 50kW DC fast charger power module, with plans for a production model in 2023, leveraging its Cleveland, Ohio, facility. This move aims to address "range anxiety" and accelerate EV adoption by providing reliable and durable fast-charging infrastructure.

title: The electric vehicle boom could bring lithium mines back to North Carolina
summary: Driven by the electric vehicle boom and the Inflation Reduction Act, lithium mining companies are looking to reopen mines in North Carolina, a region with significant lithium deposits and a history of mining. However, these plans face strong opposition from local residents concerned about environmental impacts like water contamination, dust, and increased traffic. While some communities in North Carolina are supportive of the mining developments due to potential economic benefits, others highlight the contentious trade-offs between clean energy goals and localized environmental and social costs of mineral extraction.

title: Portable Charging Solutions for EVs
summary: Running out of power in an EV can leave drivers stranded, as nationwide roadside EV charging services are not yet widely available. While towing to a nearby charging station is the most common solution, several companies offer portable charging devices like SparkCharge's Roadie, Blink's Mobile Emergency Charger, and FreeWire Technologies' Mobi EV Charger, primarily targeting commercial customers and roadside assistance providers. AAA, which once offered a limited EV charging trial, now opts for towing, noting that EV drivers are generally much more range-aware than gasoline vehicle drivers.

title: Gatik, Pitney Bowes Team on Driverless Trucks
summary: Gatik, a California-based autonomous truck technology company, has partnered with Pitney Bowes to integrate its Class 6 autonomous box trucks into Pitney Bowes' e-commerce logistics network. Starting in the first quarter of next year, Gatik's self-driving fleet will operate a continuous loop in Dallas, aiming to enhance delivery speed, efficiency, and potentially reduce transportation costs for Pitney Bowes. This collaboration highlights Gatik's focus on middle-mile logistics and its strategy of using smaller autonomous trucks for frequent, short-haul routes.

title: POSCO builds EV battery recycling plant in Poland
summary: POSCO Holdings has completed the construction of PLSC, a secondary battery recycling plant in Brzeg Dolny, Poland, in partnership with SungEel HiTech. The plant has an annual production capacity of 7,000 tons of black mass, which will be used to extract critical battery materials like lithium, nickel, cobalt, and manganese. This initiative is part of POSCO Group's broader strategy to establish a stable secondary material value chain and achieve significant sales in the sector by 2030, reinforcing their commitment to ESG management and circular economy principles.

title: Cruise lines to begin using Elon Musk's Starlink Wi-Fi
summary: Royal Caribbean Group, including brands Royal Caribbean, Celebrity Cruises, and Silversea Cruises, will implement Elon Musk's Starlink Wi-Fi across its fleet by the end of Q1 2023. This initiative aims to provide significantly faster and more reliable internet connectivity for both passengers and crew, addressing the long-standing issue of slow and expensive internet at sea. The cost structure for Starlink will vary by brand, with Silversea offering it free, Celebrity including basic Wi-Fi with premium upgrade options, and Royal Caribbean yet to announce its pricing model.

title: Formerly Sacred Now Rotting Silicon Valley Dictum of “Growth at All Costs” Crushes Okta: Shares Collapse 80% from Peak
summary: Okta, a company that provides secure access to cloud-based systems, has seen its shares collapse by 80% from their February 2021 peak after reporting a $210 million net loss and lowering its guidance. Despite consistent and growing annual net losses exceeding $2 billion, executives and analysts have ironically reframed these as "profitability," highlighting a prevailing Silicon Valley mantra of "growth at all costs." The company's struggles are attributed to "sales challenges" and "integration challenges" related to its 2021 acquisition of Auth0, signaling the potential end of an era for this business model.

title: With Tesla Decision, NLRB Rules Dress Codes Unlawful That Restrict Pro-Union Apparel
summary: The NLRB has ruled in the Tesla Inc. case that workplace dress codes prohibiting pro-union apparel are presumptively unlawful, overturning a previous standard. Employers must now demonstrate "special circumstances" to justify such restrictions, with the NLRB rejecting Tesla's arguments regarding damage to vehicles. This decision signals a more pro-labor stance from the current NLRB and requires employers to review and potentially revise their dress code policies.

title: General Motors CEO reveals new electric vehicle
summary: General Motors CEO Mary Barra announced a new all-electric Chevrolet Equinox, priced around $30,000, aiming to make EVs more affordable and increase GM's electric product line to 40% by 2025. Barra also addressed supply chain challenges and the company's commitment to environmental goals.

title: Musk says SpaceX discussed iPhone satellite service with Apple
summary: Elon Musk revealed that SpaceX has engaged in discussions with Apple Inc. regarding the integration of Starlink's satellite connectivity into iPhones. This announcement follows Apple's recent partnership with Globalstar Inc. for satellite services on its latest iPhone model, indicating a growing trend in offering satellite-based communication for smartphones. Musk emphasized that dedicated technology is crucial for optimal satellite-to-cell phone service.

title: Meme stocks to watch: top trending Reddit shares in September 2022
summary: This article identifies the top ten trending meme stocks on Reddit for September 2022, explaining what meme stocks are and their inherent benefits and risks, primarily high volatility. It then provides a detailed look into each of the ten companies, including their recent stock performance, significant events, and relevant analyst commentary, noting that all data is from a 30-day period prior to September 8, 2022.

title: TESLA Inc. looking to bring lithium refinery to Coastal Bend
summary: Tesla Inc. is considering building a "battery-grade lithium hydroxide refining facility" in the Coastal Bend area of Texas, near Robstown, or potentially in Louisiana. The company has applied for tax breaks from the state of Texas, which could lead to significant job creation and economic growth for the chosen location. However, the proposal faces concerns regarding water usage and environmental impact from some local residents.

title: Lucid Group Is Now Reportedly Manufacturing 40 to 50 Cars per Day After a Broad-based Logistics Overhaul and Management Reshuffle
summary: Lucid Group has reportedly increased its daily car production to 40-50 units following significant logistics overhauls and management changes. This improvement comes after repeated downward revisions of its 2022 production targets, which were initially over 20,000 units but later dropped to 6,000-7,000 units. The company aims to meet its revised annual guidance by further increasing production and benefiting from a new Saudi Arabian facility and purchase agreement.

title: The New Vision of General Motors: Zero Accidents, Zero Emissions and Zero Congestion
summary: General Motors is shifting its focus to a new vision centered on zero accidents, zero emissions, and zero congestion, driven by electromobility and technological development. This transformation involves connecting vehicles, developing solutions for diverse consumer needs, and pioneering new technologies like the Ultium battery platform and autonomous driving. The company emphasizes its readiness to lead the change towards a sustainable future in mobility.

title: Under the Hood of RCD
summary: The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF (RCD) saw significant inflows in August, making it the most popular Invesco equal-weight sector ETF for the month. RCD offers investors exposure to the consumer discretionary sector with an equal-weighted approach, diversifying away from large-cap bias and providing a tilt towards smaller, potentially undervalued companies. This strategy aims to reduce concentration risk by ensuring each of its 60 holdings, including companies like Etsy, Tesla, and Amazon, receives approximately equal allocation during quarterly rebalances.

title: The best ways to buy strategic metals
summary: This article discusses investment opportunities in strategic metals, particularly in the alternative-energy sector, despite recent price weaknesses. The author highlights companies and ETFs related to battery technology and nuclear energy, explaining that short-term price fluctuations may obscure long-term structural drivers like increased demand for EVs and the need for new mining and refining capacity. Investors are advised to consider these niches as a potential opportunity if they believe in a structural transformation away from hydrocarbons.

title: Auto parts supplier Aptiv to acquire 85% of Intercable unit in EV tech push
summary: Aptiv Plc announced its acquisition of an 85% stake in Intercable Automotive Solutions for 595 million euros. This strategic move grants Aptiv access to high-voltage busbar technology crucial for electric vehicles and aligns with its broader investments in EV and battery technology. The deal, expected to close by the end of the year, aims to bolster Aptiv's earnings next year and diversify its revenue stream.

title: Tesla wants to mine Lithium in Nigeria: What are the hidden costs?
summary: Nigeria rejected Tesla's request to mine lithium unless the company establishes a battery-making factory within the West African nation to add value to the mineral. The Nigerian minister of mines is seeking other lithium miners who align with the country's industrial policy. This decision aligns with Nigeria's goal of retaining value along the global processing chain of lithium, a mineral whose demand is projected to triple by 2040.

title: South Star Battery Metals announces test drilling at Alabama graphite project
summary: South Star Battery Metals is commencing test drilling this month at its Ceylon Graphite Project in Coosa County, Alabama, to assess the extent of mineralization. The project is strategically located in the Alabama Graphite Belt, an area significant for rare earth minerals essential for EV batteries. This initiative aims to generate data for a preliminary economic assessment by late 2023, bolstering U.S. critical minerals supply in a market currently dominated by China.

title: Palo Alto Networks 3-for-1 stock split: What to Know
summary: Palo Alto Networks completed a 3-for-1 stock split, with shares gaining slightly on the first day of trading post-split before moving into negative territory. Shareholders of record as of September 6 received two additional shares for each one held, distributed after the close of trading on September 13. The company stated the split aims to make shares more accessible to employees and a broader base of investors, following significant stock price increases since its IPO.

title: PANW Stock Falls After Palo Alto Stock Split. What to Know.
summary: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock experienced a slight decline despite a 3-for-1 stock split on September 14, 2022. This performance was unexpected by some investors given a broader market rebound and the company's strong financial results and outlook. While stock splits don't add inherent value, studies suggest they can benefit stock prices over a 12-month period.

title: Tesla struggles with Elon Musk’s strict return-to-office policy
summary: Three months after Elon Musk's strict return-to-office mandate, Tesla faces challenges with insufficient office space and resources to accommodate all employees. The policy has led to a decline in morale, increased absenteeism tracking, and the dismissal of some remote workers who could not relocate, impacting the company's ability to retain talent.

title: Tesla (TSLA) Keeps Duping Consumers About Self-Driving Cars, Suit Says
summary: Tesla Inc. is facing a class-action lawsuit for allegedly misleading consumers about the capabilities of its self-driving cars. A California man claims the company deceptively marketed its driver-assistance systems, continuously promising advancements that have not materialized. This suit follows similar accusations from California's Department of Motor Vehicles regarding false advertising.

title: Tesla is sued by drivers over alleged false Autopilot, Full Self-Driving claims
summary: Tesla is facing a proposed class-action lawsuit from drivers who allege that the company and Elon Musk falsely advertised its Autopilot and Full Self-Driving features. The lawsuit claims Tesla misled the public into believing these technologies were fully functional or imminent since 2016, despite known deficiencies, to boost sales and stock price. This legal action follows similar complaints from California's Department of Motor Vehicles regarding the overstatement of Tesla's advanced driver assistance systems.

title: NIU zooms into Brickell with new flagship store
summary: NIU, a Beijing-based and Nasdaq-traded company, has opened a new flagship store in Brickell, Miami, expanding its South Florida presence. The company sells electric-powered mobility devices like kick scooters, ebikes, and mopeds, aiming to offer sustainable and efficient transportation options. NIU's head of North America, Benjamin McGill, stated that the store's location in Brickell is strategic for building brand presence in the US and challenging the perception that alternative mobility solutions don't fit American transportation needs.

title: Chevron is starting to talk to retail investors in a brand new way
summary: Chevron is engaging with retail investors for the first time through a digital Q&A, signaling a broader trend where traditional companies like U.S. Steel and Howard Hughes Corporation are also increasing outreach to individual shareholders. This shift is driven by new digital communication platforms that make it easier and more cost-effective to identify and engage a growing and highly engaged retail investor base. These platforms enable discussions on broader business issues like ESG, company culture, and long-term strategy, demonstrating that retail investors are more informed and seek meaningful engagement beyond quarterly earnings.

title: Asset Allocation, International Stocks, Bonds, and Small and Mid Cap Value Factors
summary: This article discusses various aspects of asset allocation, including whether it should change in retirement, the rationale for international stock investing despite recent US outperformance, and concerns about bonds in a bear market. It also covers the pros and cons of small-cap vs. mid-cap value funds, considerations for taxable accounts, and the balance between saving and spending money after achieving financial independence.

title: TSLQ Stock Fund Price and Chart — NASDAQ:TSLQ
summary: This article provides detailed information on the Tradr 2X Short TSLA Daily ETF (TSLQ), including its current price, chart data, key statistics like AUM and expense ratio, and its investment strategy. It highlights that TSLQ is a short-term tactical tool designed to deliver -2x the daily price return of Tesla stock and discusses its recent name changes and risks. The article also includes various trading ideas and technical analyses from different contributors regarding TSLQ.

title: Off to the (24) races: F1 is capitalizing on its growing audience
summary: Formula 1 announced a record-breaking 24-race calendar for 2023, showcasing its growing global audience, particularly in the US. This expansion follows Liberty Media's acquisition in 2017 and strategic moves like the Netflix series "Drive To Survive," which significantly boosted viewership and interest. The new schedule includes an inaugural Las Vegas Grand Prix, marking a substantial push into the American market.

title: How much does it really cost to charge an electric vehicle?
summary: This article provides a cost comparison between charging an electric vehicle and fueling a gasoline-powered car, focusing on Entergy's service area. It calculates the daily cost of charging an EV at home, considers the investment in Level 2 home chargers, and discusses public charging options. The analysis concludes that electric vehicles offer significant fuel cost savings and overall ownership benefits over time.

title: Ford stock sinks on inflation, supply constraints warning
summary: Ford Motor Co.'s stock dropped 12% after the automaker warned that inflation and supply constraints would negatively impact its third-quarter earnings, leading to a projected $1 billion increase in supplier costs. Ford expects Q3 adjusted earnings before interest and taxes to be significantly lower than previous quarters, ranging from $1.4 billion to $1.7 billion, and anticipates 40,000 to 45,000 vehicles will be assembled but awaiting parts. Despite these issues, Ford reaffirmed its full-year guidance, while analysts expressed concerns about management's handling of the situation and the slow recovery from supply chain problems.

title: GM to sell up to 175,000 electric vehicles to Hertz through 2027
summary: General Motors has agreed to sell up to 175,000 electric vehicles to Hertz Global over the next five years, starting early next year with Chevy Bolt EV and EUV models. This deal is GM's largest vehicle sale agreement with Hertz, following similar agreements between Hertz and Tesla and Polestar, and aims to significantly increase EV adoption and Hertz's electric fleet. Despite a broader market decline, the companies decided not to release financial details of the deal, but GM plans to sell the EVs at "retail margin" rather than at discounted fleet sales.

title: 7 Things to Know About the NANC ETF Aiming to Track Nancy Pelosi Stocks
summary: Unusual Whales has proposed two new ETFs, NANC and KRUZ, designed to track the trading activities of Democratic and Republican lawmakers, respectively. The NANC ETF is inspired by Speaker Nancy Pelosi's successful trades, while KRUZ would follow Republican activity, including Senator Ted Cruz. These ETFs aim to allow investors to mirror the investment decisions of politicians, leveraging their perceived stock-picking skills.

title: NVIDIA Unveils DRIVE Thor — Centralized Car Computer Unifying Cluster, Infotainment, Automated Driving, and Parking in a Single, Cost-Saving System
summary: NVIDIA announced DRIVE Thor, its next-generation centralized computer for autonomous vehicles, delivering up to 2,000 teraflops of performance. This superchip unifies intelligent functions like automated driving, parking, and infotainment into a single architecture, significantly reducing system cost and complexity. ZEEKR, a Geely-owned automaker, is the first customer, planning to integrate DRIVE Thor into its intelligent electric vehicles starting in early 2025.

title: GM backs setting tough U.S. emissions targets for 2030
summary: General Motors (GM) announced its support for stricter federal emissions standards, aiming for at least 50% of new vehicles sold by 2030 to be zero-emission. This stance, articulated with the Environmental Defense Fund (EDF), comes as the EPA develops new requirements and aligns with GM's goal to eliminate tailpipe emissions from new light-duty vehicles by 2035. The move also highlights ongoing discussions and differing approaches between the federal government, California, and various environmental groups regarding the pace and scope of EV adoption.

title: China's Xpeng says CATL is no longer its largest battery supplier
summary: Xpeng, a Chinese electric car maker, has diversified its battery suppliers and no longer considers CATL its largest. This move reflects a broader trend among Chinese EV automakers to seek alternative suppliers to better control costs, especially after CATL raised prices. Xpeng is now working with multiple battery makers, including Sunwoda for fast-charging technology and EVE and CALB for its vehicles.

title: 7 Meme Stocks to Buy During a Stock Market Crash
summary: This article identifies seven meme stocks that aggressive investors might consider buying during a stock market crash for long-term potential. The selection includes companies like Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), FedEx (FDX), GameStop (GME), NVIDIA (NVDA), Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT), and Tesla (TSLA). Each stock is discussed with reasons for its meme stock appeal and potential for recovery despite current market downturns.

title: SolarEdge Home Battery Review: 3 Months In
