summary: The author reviews his new SolarEdge Home Battery after three months of use, detailing the installation process, initial impressions, and challenges encountered. He highlights the benefits of the battery, including a free inverter upgrade and compatibility with Amber Electric's "SmartShift" for increased savings, despite minor issues like a 3-second switchover delay during outages and initial battery failure. The article also addresses common user questions and concerns regarding battery management and performance.

title: XPeng Diversifies Battery Sources, Reducing Reliance on CATL
summary: XPeng Inc. is diversifying its battery suppliers, reducing its primary reliance on CATL. The electric-vehicle maker has added Sunwoda Electronic Co. Ltd., CALB Co. Ltd., and Eve Energy Co. Ltd. to its supplier list, partly to better control costs after CATL raised prices. XPeng is also collaborating with Sunwoda to develop a fast-charging battery for its G9 SUV.

title: Weekly Recalls: Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz (2), Nissan (2), Tesla
summary: This article details the weekly vehicle recalls issued for Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz (two separate recalls), Nissan (two separate recalls), and Tesla. The recalls address issues ranging from fuel system defects and improperly tightened lug nuts to electrical system faults, detaching window trim, transmission park pawl problems, faulty seat belts, and malfunctioning automatic window reversal systems. Each recall specifies the affected models, potential number of units, the nature of the defect, the manufacturer's proposed remedy, and owner notification timelines.

title: Tesla Recalls Almost 1.1 Million Vehicles Over Window Glitch
summary: Tesla has recalled nearly 1.1 million vehicles across all four of its models due to a power window glitch where windows may close too quickly, posing a pinching risk to occupants. The electric car manufacturer plans to resolve this issue with an over-the-air software update, eliminating the need for vehicle owners to bring their cars in for service. The recall impacts Model S, X, 3, and Y vehicles manufactured between 2017 and 2022.

title: Hertz is buying up to 175,000 electric vehicles from GM
summary: Hertz has announced a major purchase of up to 175,000 electric vehicles from General Motors over the next five years, expanding its EV rental fleet. This follows earlier agreements with Tesla and Polestar. The acquisitions will include a variety of GM's North American passenger vehicle brands and types, with GM aiming to significantly ramp up EV production and Hertz targeting a quarter of its fleet to be electric by 2024.

title: GM Is Doubling Down on Self-Driving Cars With LiDAR
summary: General Motors is heavily investing in LiDAR technology for self-driving cars, catching the attention of institutional investors like Cathie Wood's ARK Invest. GM plans to pour $35 billion into EV and AV product development by 2025, with LiDAR being a crucial component for autonomous vehicles to navigate. The global LiDAR market is projected for significant growth, offering investment opportunities through ETFs and specialized tech stock services.

title: GM, Hertz make deal to deploy up to 175,000 EVs
summary: Hertz plans to purchase up to 175,000 electric vehicles from General Motors over the next five years, marking a substantial step towards Hertz's goal of having a quarter of its fleet be electric by the end of 2024. This multi-billion dollar deal could pave the way for similar partnerships between GM and other rental car companies, helping GM achieve its target of producing 1 million EVs annually in North America by 2025. The agreement allows GM to sell EVs at near-retail profit margins to Hertz, deploying them in key cities and helping to reduce carbon emissions.

title: How Hertz and the EV could remake your car rental
summary: Hertz and BP are collaborating to transform the car rental experience with electric vehicles, including building charging infrastructure and exploring services for ride-hailing drivers. Hertz plans for a quarter of its U.S. fleet to be electric by 2024, aiming to address the unique challenges of EV charging at scale and potentially using its facilities to serve other EV users. The move is driven by the financial imperative of maintaining residual car values and could introduce many Americans to EVs for the first time.

title: Hertz, bp collaborate to accelerate EV charging in North America
summary: Hertz and bp have signed a memorandum of understanding to develop a national network of EV charging stations in North America, powered by bp pulse. This partnership aims to accelerate EV consumer adoption by establishing fast-charging hubs at Hertz locations, managing Hertz's charging infrastructure, and customizing bp pulse's Omega software for efficient fleet recharging. Hertz plans for one-quarter of its fleet to be electric by the end of 2024, expanding charging options for customers and supporting lower-emission travel.

title: NIO unlocks its potential through standout user operations
summary: This article features an interview with Lihong Qin, cofounder and president of NIO, discussing the company's unique user-centric operating model for electric vehicles. Qin explains the business logic behind user operations, its role in creating a brand premium, and how it unlocks value throughout the vehicle lifecycle. The interview also touches on the economics of user operations, including optimizing sales and service costs, and NIO's expansion into European markets.

title: Pony.ai and SAIC AI Lab to Develop Fully Driverless EV Robotaxi
summary: Pony.ai and SAIC AI Lab have partnered to develop a fully driverless EV robotaxi, based on the SAIC Marvel R model, equipped with Pony.ai's L4-level autonomous driving technology. This collaboration will focus on co-developing vehicle chassis, intelligent cockpits, and remote assistance, aiming to accelerate the commercial adoption of robotaxi services in numerous Chinese cities. The initiative aligns with Shanghai's driverless policy and builds upon Pony.ai's expanding robotaxi services in the region.

title: Qualcomm CFO Focuses on Investing in Budding Automotive Business
summary: Qualcomm's CFO, Akash Palkhiwala, is strategically allocating investments towards the company's expanding automotive-chip business. This move is a diversification strategy to offset slowing consumer demand for smartphones, which traditionally has been a significant revenue driver for the company. Qualcomm, primarily known for mobile-phone chips, has secured $30 billion in commitments from auto-component suppliers to support this growth.

title: How China Is Transforming the Global Lithium Industry
summary: China has become a dominant force in the global lithium industry, controlling around 80% of battery cell manufacturing and holding key positions in both upstream and downstream supply chains. This ascendancy is driven by robust policy support, entrepreneurial breakthroughs from companies like CATL and BYD, and significant investments in lithium mines and energy storage solutions. China's strategic initiatives, including a shift towards LFP batteries and ambitious energy storage targets, position it to continue leading the lithium sector for the foreseeable future, impacting global renewable energy goals and EV adoption.

title: Tesla workers' lawsuit over layoffs likely belongs in arbitration, judge says
summary: A U.S. magistrate judge has recommended that a proposed class-action lawsuit against Tesla Inc, concerning alleged failures to provide advance notice for layoffs, be moved to private arbitration. The judge stated that an arbitrator, not a court, should determine the validity of the arbitration agreements signed by Tesla workers. This decision means former employees will likely pursue their claims individually in arbitration rather than through a class action.

title: Tesla names Airbnb co-founder to board
summary: Tesla Inc. has appointed Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia to its board of directors, bringing the total number of directors back to eight. Gebbia steps into a role previously held by Larry Ellison and continues to serve on Airbnb's board. He had previously stepped back from a daily operational role at Airbnb, which he co-founded in 2007.

title: Elon Musk seeks to end SEC 'muzzle' requiring pre-approval of tweets
summary: Elon Musk's lawyers have petitioned a federal appeals court to dismantle a provision within his 2018 consent decree with the SEC, which necessitates a Tesla lawyer's pre-approval for some of his tweets. They argue this requirement acts as a "government-imposed muzzle" violating free speech principles. The SEC has not yet commented but is expected to file its own brief in response.

title: Ford Rolls Out Gas-Guzzlers To Fund Its Green Energy Ambitions
summary: Ford Motor Co. is releasing new gas-guzzling pickup trucks, including its Super Duty series with powerful engines, to fund its ambitious green energy goals. Despite aiming for carbon neutrality by 2035 and investing $50 billion in electric vehicles, Ford relies heavily on the profitability of its F-series trucks, which generate nearly a third of its global revenues. This strategy highlights the trade-offs companies and even nations, like the E.U., must make during the transition to a greener economy, acknowledging that progress cannot happen overnight and requires sustained business operations.

title: ARK Invest CEO Cathie Wood’s tech bargain hunt
summary: Cathie Wood's ARK Invest continued its strategy of investing in tech stocks in September 2022, acquiring shares in companies like Nvidia and Adobe despite significant market downturns for these firms. The ARK Innovation ETF has seen substantial losses and outflows, but the firm is betting on a rebound in battered tech stocks. Additionally, there has been a management reshuffle within ARK Invest, with William Scherer taking over two ETFs and Brett Winton promoted to chief futurist.

title: Tesla adds billionaire Airbnb co-founder Gebbia to board
summary: Tesla Inc. has appointed Airbnb co-founder Joseph Gebbia to its board, reversing an earlier plan to reduce the number of directors. This move follows criticism from a shareholder group regarding the lack of independent board members and the need to comply with a 2018 SEC consent decree. Gebbia will waive cash and stock compensation for a period, though some experts question whether his appointment truly adds diversity to the board.

title: CATL – The Battery Giant Leading Innovation in China A-Shares
summary: This article highlights Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL), the world's largest EV battery supplier, founded by Yuqun Zeng. Despite its global importance, CATL, trading on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, is often inaccessible to international investors, but the KraneShares Bosera MSCI China A-Share ETF (KBA) includes it as a top holding. The company's success is attributed to its technological innovation, supply chain advantages within China, and efficient manufacturing processes, positioning it as a leader in the rapidly expanding EV battery market.

title: CATL – The Battery Giant Leading Innovation In China A-Shares
summary: Contemporary Amperax Technology Co., Limited (CATL) is a leading innovator and one of the largest EV battery suppliers globally, providing batteries for major companies like Tesla, Ford, and NIO. Due to its listing on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, CATL is often inaccessible to international investors through standard brokerage accounts and ETFs, making the KraneShares Bosera MSCI China A-Share ETF (KBA) a key avenue for investment access. The article highlights CATL's significant role in the EV market and its founder's origin story.

title: The Rivian R1T Is the Best Truck I’ve Ever Driven
summary: The author reviews the Rivian R1T electric pickup truck after taking it on an off-roading, backcountry camping trip. He highlights its impressive off-road capabilities, luxury features, and storage, acknowledging its "game changer" status despite challenges like range anxiety and a high price point. The article concludes that while expensive, the R1T delivers an outstanding driving and outdoor adventure experience.

title: Here are the people who texted Elon Musk to offer advice or money for the Twitter deal
summary: This article details text messages between Elon Musk and various tech and media luminaries concerning his bid to buy Twitter. The exchanges reveal advice, investment offers, and discussions about the platform's future, as shared in court documents related to Musk's attempt to back out of the $44 billion acquisition. Notable texters include Jack Dorsey, Larry Ellison, Joe Lonsdale, and Sam Bankman-Fried.

title: TTAC: Overweight Tech & Energy, Underweight Industrials & Communication
summary: The FCF US Quality ETF (TTAC) focuses on free cash flow to select approximately 150 stocks, aiming to outperform the Russell 3000. As of late August, TTAC was overweight in technology and energy sectors and underweight in industrials and communication services. FCF Advisors prioritizes free cash flow metrics, which they believe are more difficult to manipulate than GAAP earnings, especially in the current challenging investment environment.

title: Tesla Gets a Warning From NIO, Li, XPeng Deliveries
summary: Deliveries from Chinese electric vehicle makers NIO, XPeng, and Li indicate a warning for Tesla as their growth lags behind the overall industry. The article suggests that car buyers are drawn to new models, potentially impacting Tesla's market share. This trend highlights the importance of innovation and new product offerings in the EV market.

title: How John Deere plans to build a world of fully autonomous farming by 2030
summary: John Deere aims to achieve fully autonomous farming by 2030, building on two decades of investment in AI and robotics, including its autonomous 8R farm tractor. Despite current fleet size being under 50 units, the company is making strategic acquisitions and partnerships to advance its technology. Competitors like AGCO and Case IH are also developing autonomous solutions, with AGCO focusing on retrofit kits for existing machinery and Case IH recently unveiling its autonomous Trident 5550 applicator.

title: Tesla's a 'key stock in everyone’s ESG portfolio.' So why is that so controversial?
summary: This article examines the controversy surrounding Tesla's inclusion in ESG portfolios despite its environmental contributions. While Tesla is a leader in EV technology and carbon emission reduction, concerns about its corporate governance, transparency on emissions, and controversies like racial discrimination and Autopilot safety issues have led to scrutiny and even removal from certain ESG indices. This highlights a fundamental debate within the ESG investing world regarding what constitutes true social responsibility and impact.

title: Tesla slides on widening delivery and production gap, demand worries
summary: Tesla Inc. shares dropped 8.6% due to lower-than-expected third-quarter deliveries, attributed to logistical challenges and growing concerns about demand amidst rising prices and economic slowdown. Despite record deliveries, the significant gap between production and deliveries highlighted transport issues, impacting Tesla's market value and raising questions about future sales. Analysts, however, anticipate robust manufacturing margins for Tesla, while rival Rivian reported increased production.

title: Can Vietnam’s VinFast be the Real Contender to Tesla’s EV Throne?
summary: VinFast, a Vietnamese automotive company, is emerging as a potential contender in the electric vehicle (EV) market against established players like Tesla. Despite being a relatively new entrant, VinFast has ambitious goals for production and profitability, offering lower-cost, tech-heavy EVs with comparable ranges to Tesla models. The company is actively expanding its manufacturing capabilities and supply chain, including battery production and semiconductor partnerships, with a focus on penetrating high-wealth Western markets.

title: Cathie Wood bought up Tesla shares after a Monday stock plunge. They quickly rebounded.
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Investment Management LLC purchased 132,213 shares of Tesla on Monday, marking her firm's first buy since mid-June after a significant stock decline. This dip-buying activity led to a quick rebound in Tesla's shares by as much as 4% on Tuesday, contributing to S&P 500 gains. The purchase indicates a renewed strategy of buying the dip after a year of selling down her stake in the EV manufacturer, whose shares had previously lost their "crown jewel" status in her main fund.

title: Micron chooses New York for $100B factory instead of Central Texas
summary: Micron Technology announced its decision to build a new $100 billion semiconductor factory in Central New York, opting against Lockhart, Texas, which had been a finalist for the facility. The move comes with the aid of $5.5 billion in incentives from New York. This investment is part of Micron's larger plan to invest $40 billion in the U.S.

title: Is Tesla seeing a slowdown in demand?
summary: Early signs suggest a potential slowdown in demand for Tesla vehicles, indicated by falling waiting times for deliveries in the US and China and the company building more EVs than it delivered in Q3 2022. Analysts note increasing premium pricing and exposure to a decelerating global economy as key factors, while Tesla maintains it still has more demand than supply. The issue of demand and supply balance will be crucial for investors when the company reports quarterly results on October 19.

title: Icahn had Twitter stake worth over $500 mln before Musk's about-face - WSJ
summary: Activist investor Carl Icahn amassed a Twitter stake worth over $500 million in the months leading up to Elon Musk's decision to proceed with the takeover. Icahn, who paid around the mid-$30s per share, made an estimated profit exceeding $250 million after Twitter shares jumped over 22% following Musk's announcement. Other investors like D.E. Shaw Group and Daniel Loeb's Third Point LLC are also expected to see significant gains from their recent bets on Twitter shares.

title: Exclusive: Apollo, Sixth Street no longer in talks to finance Twitter deal
summary: Apollo Global Management and Sixth Street Partners are no longer discussing providing financing for Elon Musk's proposed $44 billion acquisition of Twitter. These talks reportedly ceased months ago when Musk first began to express doubts about the deal. Musk later confirmed that neither entity was part of the announced third-party equity or debt financing.

title: Tesla Stock Gets a Little Good News: S&P Upgrades Tesla Bonds
summary: S&P Global has upgraded the bonds of electric-vehicle maker Tesla, removing their junk status. This development is a piece of good news for Tesla stock investors. The upgrade signifies improved financial health and creditworthiness for the company.

title: Musk says Pepsi to receive Tesla's first Semi trucks in December
summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla is starting production of its Semi electric trucks and PepsiCo Inc will receive the first deliveries on December 1st. The truck, which has a 500-mile range and is expected to cost $180,000, has seen its production timeline pushed back multiple times since its 2017 unveiling. PepsiCo had reserved 100 of these trucks to reduce fuel costs and fleet emissions.

title: Tesla Aims to Deliver First Semitrailer Trucks in December to PepsiCo
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced plans to deliver the first all-electric semitrailer truck to PepsiCo in December, five years after its initial reveal. The truck is expected to have a 500-mile range on a single charge. This delivery marks a significant step for Tesla's long-delayed Semi project.

title: PepsiCo confirms Tesla Semi truck deliveries to start in December
summary: PepsiCo has confirmed it will be the first company to receive Tesla Semi truck deliveries, starting December 1st. The electric trucks will be deployed at PepsiCo's Frito-Lay plant in Modesto, California, and its PepsiCo beverages factory in Sacramento, as part of the company's efforts to reduce fuel costs and emissions. Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced production of the Semi truck, which boasts a 500-mile range, after years of delays.

title: Tesla's China-made sales hit record following Shanghai factory upgrade
summary: Tesla Inc. delivered a record 83,135 China-made electric vehicles in September, following an upgrade to its Shanghai factory. This increase comes despite a challenging economic environment and growing competition from domestic EV makers in China. Globally, Tesla's third-quarter deliveries fell short of analyst expectations, yet still marked a record for the company.

title: PayPal says policy to fine customers for 'misinformation' was an 'error'
summary: PayPal clarified that its earlier policy update, which suggested customers could be fined $2,500 for promoting misinformation, was sent in error and will not be implemented. The company stated that it does not fine users for misinformation and apologized for the confusion caused by the update, which had gone viral and drawn criticism from former PayPal executives.

title: TVA, VW to Test All-Electric Mobile Drone Response Vehicle
summary: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) and Volkswagen (VW) are collaborating to test an all-electric "Mobile Drone Response Vehicle" based on the VW ID.4. This modified SUV will be used by TVA's drone response team to inspect and maintain over 16,000 miles of transmission lines, supporting TVA's goal to convert its entire passenger car fleet and half of its cargo vehicles to EVs by 2030. The initiative aims to accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles and decarbonize the nation's transportation network.

title: PayPal says policy to fine customers for 'misinformation' was an 'error'
summary: PayPal clarified that a recent policy update suggesting fines for misinformation was an error and never intended to be implemented. The company faced significant backlash on social media, leading its shares to drop, and prominent figures like former president David Marcus and co-founder Elon Musk criticized the policy. PayPal apologized for the confusion caused by the incorrect information.

title: Pepsi first in line for Tesla semi truck deliveries starting in December
summary: Five years after its unveiling, the Tesla semi truck is finally set for delivery, with Pepsico Inc. being the first recipient in December. Pepsico has reserved 100 semi trucks and plans to have 15 on the road by year-end. This development follows Tesla's prioritization of other models due to supply shortages and is boosted by the Inflation Reduction Act's tax incentives for heavy-duty electric trucks.

title: General Motors launches electric grid division
summary: General Motors has launched a new division called GM Energy, signaling the auto industry's strategic goal of fusing electric cars with the electric grid. This new unit will offer a comprehensive suite of energy services, including bi-directional charging, vehicle-to-home capabilities, stationary storage, and microgrid solutions, positioning GM to compete with companies like Tesla in the broader battery and energy market. The initiative aims to address challenges with grid infrastructure, energy storage, and management, with plans for dealerships to promote these new energy products and vehicles to serve as aggregated resources for utilities.

title: Hertz False-Arrest Claimants Can Sue in State Court, Judge Rules
summary: A US Bankruptcy Judge has ruled that over 60 people accusing Hertz of false arrest can join a lawsuit against the company in state court, rather than being confined to bankruptcy court. This decision allows more than 120 individuals to sue Hertz outside of bankruptcy, potentially leading to higher litigation costs and significant jury verdicts for the rental car giant. Hertz, which has appealed an earlier ruling, continues to offer settlements to some alleged victims while fighting other claims.

title: Tesla Plans to Deliver Semis to Pepsi Years After Unveiling
summary: Tesla is set to deliver its first Semi trucks to PepsiCo Inc. on December 1, five years after the electric big rigs were initially unveiled by Elon Musk. PepsiCo confirmed it will take delivery of 15 of the 100 reserved trucks by year-end, which will be deployed at its Frito-Lay and beverage plants in California. The delivery follows production delays due to prioritizing other Tesla models and supply chain issues, with renewed urgency fueled by new federal tax credits for heavy-duty electric trucks.

title: Winter is Coming
summary: S&P Global Mobility warns that the global auto industry faces significant risk from the looming European energy crunch, particularly due to skyrocketing energy prices. This could lead to extensive pressure on OEMs and suppliers with energy-intensive manufacturing processes, potentially reducing European final-assembly plant output by over 1 million units per quarter starting in Q4 2022. The report highlights potential supply chain disruptions, increased energy costs per vehicle, and varying impacts on European countries based on their energy mix, storage, and governmental fiscal positions.

title: GM takes on Tesla in home and commercial energy storage, management
summary: General Motors is launching a new unit, GM Energy, to compete with Tesla in the home and commercial energy storage and management market. GM Energy will offer stationary storage batteries, solar panels, and hydrogen fuel cells, bundling existing public charging services with new residential and commercial offerings. This expansion leverages GM's expertise in batteries, manufacturing, and connectivity, aiming for a significant share in the estimated $120-$150 billion energy management market.

title: General Motors takes on Tesla with new energy division
summary: General Motors is launching a new unit called GM Energy to offer energy storage and management services to residential and commercial customers, directly competing with Tesla's established energy business. GM Energy will provide EV chargers, stationary batteries, solar panels, and hydrogen fuel cells, with Ultium Home services starting in late 2023. summary: Cathie Wood's flagship ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) experienced its best day ever, surging over 14% on Thursday following an easing inflation reading. Major holdings like Zoom Video, Tesla, Roku, and Teladoc saw significant jumps. This rally indicates a potential rebound for growth stocks if reduced price pressures lead the Federal Reserve to scale back its aggressive tightening.

title: California's new solar energy proposal removes hefty grid connection fee
summary: California regulators have revised their proposal for rooftop solar systems, removing a controversial monthly grid connection fee while offering new support for low-income customers. The new plan, which still needs approval, aims to expand renewable energy and has significantly boosted shares of rooftop solar providers, despite concerns from some critics about reduced export rates and equitable distribution of incentives. The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) will vote on the proposal on Dec. 15, with implementation slated for April 15 next year.

title: 3 Stocks That May Be Kicked Out of the Dow Jones Industrial Average (and the 3 Stocks That Could Replace Them)
summary: This article discusses three companies, Walgreens Boots Alliance, Dow Inc., and Verizon Communications, that are at risk of being removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average due to their declining influence or market cap. It also proposes potential replacements: CVS Health for Walgreens, Tesla for Dow Inc., and Alphabet for Verizon, highlighting how these changes could update the index to better reflect the current economic landscape. The Dow's share price-weighted methodology means that lower-priced stocks have less influence, making these companies vulnerable.

title: Fake account posing as pharmaceutical giant says 'insulin is free', causes stocks to plummet
summary: Pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly & Co apologized after a fake "verified" Twitter account announced that insulin was free, causing the company's stock to drop. This incident highlights issues with Twitter's new verification policy under Elon Musk, which has led to a wave of impersonations of major brands and significant reputational risk for advertisers. The controversy led Twitter to temporarily roll back its premium service and revive "official" labels for some accounts.

title: Truck stops will soon need the same amount of power as a small town if electrified rigs continue, study shows
summary: A new study by National Grid Plc. indicates that the widespread adoption of electric semi-trucks will dramatically increase power demands at truck stops, requiring as much electricity as a small town by 2035. The main challenge isn't the total electricity supply, but rather the infrastructure needed to deliver high-speed charging quickly and efficiently, a process that currently takes years to build out. This infrastructure gap is a significant concern for fleets considering electrification, potentially hindering the transition to electric trucks without proactive investment and policy changes.

title: Can GM electric vehicles turn a profit by 2025? Mary Barra is betting on it [Update]
summary: General Motors (GM) CEO Mary Barra is confident the company's electric vehicle (EV) segment will become profitable by 2025, a goal she highlighted during an investor update. This forecast comes as GM scales its EV production and invests heavily in battery technology and manufacturing, aiming to mirror the profitability seen in pure EV companies like Tesla. The company's strategy includes launching new EV models, building battery plants, and improving margins through initiatives like a new digital platform for dealers.

title: How Sysco Corp. plans to deploy 800 battery electric Class 8 trucks (and that’s just the beginning)
summary: Sysco Corp. plans to deploy 800 battery electric Freightliner eCascadia Class 8 tractors by 2026, aiming to electrify 35% of its U.S. broadline fleet, totaling around 2,500 electric trucks, by 2030. The company proactively partnered with Daimler Truck North America on eCascadia development and is now focused on solving charging infrastructure challenges, including using mobile charging solutions. Sysco prioritizes states friendly to electric charger installation and is looking to secure clean, sustainable energy for these operations.

title: Trial over Tesla boss Musk’s $56bn pay package starts
summary: A trial has begun over allegations that Elon Musk's $56bn pay package from Tesla was based on easily achievable performance targets and that investors were misled into approving it. A shareholder is attempting to prove that Musk used his influence over Tesla’s board to dictate the terms of the 2018 package, which did not require him to work full-time at the company. Musk and Tesla's directors deny the allegations, arguing that the pay package incentivized him to guide Tesla through a critical growth period.

title: Court told Musk's $56 billion pay wasn't for punching a clock
summary: A Delaware court heard arguments regarding Elon Musk's $56 billion Tesla pay package, with a director and former executive defending it against a shareholder's claim that Musk dictated terms. The shareholder alleges Musk used his dominance to craft the 2018 package and duped investors, while defendants argue the package incentivized Musk during a critical growth period for Tesla. The trial examines the board's latitude in setting executive compensation, especially for a controlling shareholder, and will impact the future of Musk's compensation from Tesla.

title: Ford must bring more work in-house to preserve jobs - CEO
summary: Ford CEO Jim Farley stated that the company needs to bring more electric vehicle component manufacturing in-house to preserve jobs, as EV production requires 40% less labor than combustion vehicles. This strategy aims to ensure "everyone has a role" in the future and improve competitiveness, similar to Tesla's integrated production approach. Farley also noted that upcoming contract talks with the United Auto Workers will focus heavily on the shift to electrification.

title: Musk's all-nighters at Twitter raise concern for Tesla investors
summary: Elon Musk's intense focus on Twitter, including working all-nighters at its San Francisco headquarters, is causing concern among Tesla investors about his capacity to lead the electric carmaker. Tesla's stock has dropped 50% since Musk disclosed his stake in Twitter in April, and his recent tweets have shown a significant shift in attention towards Twitter. While some supporters remain confident, others in the financial community fear Twitter has become a major distraction for Musk, negatively impacting Tesla's brand and stock performance.

title: Tim Draper turns attention from China to Taiwan
summary: US venture capitalist Tim Draper, an early investor in Tesla and SpaceX, has shifted his investment focus from China to Taiwan. He stated that he stopped investing in China due to early signs that it was moving away from a free market under President Xi Jinping, and he now sees Taiwan as a natural place for investment, particularly in its booming tech and semiconductor sector. Draper also expressed concerns about a potential Chinese attack on Taiwan and praised Elon Musk's ability to get things done.

title: Vietnamese electric vehicle maker VinFast launches first showroom in Canada
summary: VinFast, a Vietnamese electric vehicle manufacturer, has opened its first Canadian showroom in Toronto's Yorkdale Shopping Centre, with plans for seven more by year-end across Canada. The company, a subsidiary of the Vingroup conglomerate, began taking online reservations for its VF8 and VF9 models in March and expects first deliveries by late 2022 or early 2023. These vehicles range from $64,990 to $103,790, with options for battery subscriptions and potential eligibility for federal and provincial EV subsidies.

title: Elon Musk says in court that he doesn't want to be CEO of any company and tries to walk back SEC insults
summary: In a Delaware court testimony regarding a lawsuit over his 2018 Tesla compensation, Elon Musk stated he does not want to be CEO of any company, including Tesla, and confirmed his role at Twitter is temporary. He also attempted to clarify past insults directed at the SEC, suggesting his notorious "SEC, three letter acronym, middle word is Elon's" tweet was misunderstood and meant "Save Elon's Company." Musk also defended using Tesla employees for Twitter work as voluntary, after-hours assistance.

title: Ford fighting electric vehicle bottlenecks with industrial automation giant
summary: Ford has partnered with industrial automation giant Rockwell to address electric vehicle (EV) manufacturing bottlenecks and accelerate its EV rollout to meet overwhelming demand. This collaboration aims to enhance Ford's production capabilities and supply chain efficiency for its next three EV assembly lines, including the Blue Oval City campus. Ford wants to become the number one EV brand, trailing only Tesla in US sales, and believes this partnership will help strengthen its manufacturing prowess.

title: Tesla board member says Elon Musk identified potential successor as CEO
summary: A Tesla director, James Murdoch, testified that Elon Musk has identified a potential successor as CEO in recent months, though the individual was not named. This revelation comes amid investor concerns about Musk's divided attention following his acquisition of Twitter. Previous discussions within the board also explored finding an "administrative CEO" to allow Musk to focus on product development.

title: GM expects EV profits to be comparable to gas vehicles by 2025, years ahead of schedule
summary: General Motors anticipates its electric vehicle profits will align with those of its traditional gasoline-powered cars and trucks by 2025, significantly earlier than projected. This acceleration is largely attributed to federal incentives from the Biden administration's Inflation Reduction Act, which provides financial benefits for North American EV production and purchases. The company also boosted its 2022 cash flow guidance and expects strong growth from new businesses like its BrightDrop electric commercial vehicle unit and a new digital retail platform.

title: Vale and GM Sign Long-Term Nickel Supply Agreement in Canada Critical to North American EV Supply Chain
summary: Vale Canada Limited and General Motors Co. have signed a long-term agreement for Vale to supply battery-grade nickel sulfate to GM. This nickel sulfate, equivalent to 25,000 metric tons of contained nickel annually, will support GM's growing EV production in North America, powering approximately 350,000 electric vehicles per year starting in the second half of 2026. The agreement highlights Canada's role in the EV supply chain and aims to secure a sustainable, low-carbon source for GM's Ultium battery cathodes.

title: Musk says he made some Tesla decisions without board nod, defends $56 bln pay
summary: Elon Musk testified in court, defending his $56 billion Tesla pay package against claims he dictated terms to the board. He acknowledged making some decisions without board approval, including ending Bitcoin acceptance and discussing stock buybacks, but denied that his pay package goals were easy to achieve. The trial centers on whether Musk exerted undue influence to secure his compensation.

title: Ford tackles electric vehicle supply bottlenecks with new partner’s support
summary: Ford is partnering with Rockwell, an industrial automation startup, to address electric vehicle manufacturing bottlenecks and meet the high demand for zero-emission cars. This collaboration aims to help Ford achieve its production targets for EVs, including its goal of a 600,000 unit run rate by the end of the year and 2 million units by 2026. Rockwell will serve as a key controls and solutions source for Ford's new EV assembly lines, promising increased responsiveness, shorter lead times, lower prices, and higher quality throughout the supply chain.

title: Musk's pay trial asks if Tesla's growth justifies $56 bln compensation
summary: A Delaware judge is set to rule on whether Elon Musk's $56 billion pay package from Tesla was justified by the company's significant growth or if the process was flawed. The trial heard testimony from Musk and Tesla directors, who argued the package incentivized extraordinary growth and enriched shareholders. Shareholders challenging the package claim it was dictated by Musk to subservient directors and approved based on misleading information.

title: 2016 S&P Global Mobility Loyalty Awards
summary: The S&P Global Mobility Loyalty Awards recognize automakers for their ability to retain customers, based on actual consumer transactions and vehicle registration data. The 2016 awards, based on an analysis of over 17.5 million new vehicle registrations, recognized 34 winners across various categories. General Motors won for Overall Loyalty to Manufacturer and Ford for Overall Loyalty to Make, among other key industry players.

title: Vale, GM sign long-term Nickel supply agreement in Canada
summary: Vale S.A.'s Canadian division and General Motors have signed a long-term agreement for the supply of battery-grade nickel sulfate from Vale's proposed plant in Bécancour, Québec. This deal will secure a significant supply of nickel for GM's growing EV production in North America, with deliveries expected to begin in the second half of 2026. The agreement is crucial for GM to meet its goal of 1 million units of annual EV capacity in North America by 2025 and supports EV eligibility for consumer incentives under new U.S. clean energy tax credits.

title: Tesla recalls 321,000 U.S. vehicles over rear light issue
summary: Tesla has issued a recall for over 321,000 vehicles in the U.S. due to an issue where tail lights may intermittently fail to illuminate. The recall affects certain 2023 Model 3 and 2020-2023 Model Y vehicles, and Tesla plans to address the problem with an over-the-air software update. The company has reported no crashes or injuries related to this defect.

title: Weekly Recalls: Ford, Kia, Tesla (2)
summary: This article details recent recalls announced by Kia, Ford, and Tesla. Kia is recalling certain 2017-2018 Niro hybrid electric vehicles due to a potential issue with the Power Relay Assembly overheating rear seats. Ford is recalling 2021-2022 F-150 vehicles for a front windshield wiper motor failure. Tesla has two recalls: one for 2021-2023 Model X vehicles due to an incorrect front passenger airbag deployment calibration and another for 2023 Model 3 and 2020-2023 Model Y vehicles concerning intermittent taillight illumination.

title: Toyota-backed Pony.ai granted permit to offer driverless robotaxi services in Beijing
summary: Toyota-backed Pony.ai and Baidu have been granted permits to operate driverless robotaxi services in Beijing, allowing the removal of safety operators from the driver's seat to the back. This move, which accelerates the commercialization of autonomous driving in China, permits each company to deploy up to 10 autonomous vehicles in a 60-square-kilometer designated area. Other major Chinese cities like Shanghai and Guangzhou are expected to follow Beijing's lead in allowing similar advanced autonomous driving tests.

title: Former Twitter Employees Sue Company Alleging WARN Act Violations
summary: Former Twitter employees have filed a lawsuit against the company, alleging violations of both California's and the federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Acts. The lawsuit claims that Twitter failed to provide the legally required 60 days' notice before mass layoffs, impacting approximately 3,700 employees. This action seeks to prevent further unlawful layoffs and secure back pay and benefits for affected workers, though potential arbitration clauses similar to those in a Tesla case could complicate the class action.

title: EVgo Opens New Fast Charging Station in East Bay to Support Local EV Adoption
summary: EVgo Inc. has opened a new public fast charging station at Marina Square Shopping Center in San Leandro, California, featuring 100kW and 350kW chargers for up to four vehicles. This station, supported by the California Energy Commission and Uber, aims to enhance EV adoption, particularly for rideshare drivers, near Oakland International Airport and I-880. The initiative is part of the Northern California Charging Access for Reliable On-Demand Transportation Services (CARTs) grant program, providing critical charging infrastructure in a high-demand area.

title: Tesla Confirmed the Cybertruck Is Made of Starship Material Supplied by Steel Dynamics
summary: Tesla has officially confirmed that its Cybertruck is made of steel supplied by Steel Dynamics Inc. (SDI), the same company that provides material for SpaceX's Starship. This information was revealed during the "Inside Tesla: Supercharging the Electric Revolution" exhibition at the Petersen Automotive Museum, corroborating long-standing rumors. Franz von Holzhausen, Senior Design Executive at Tesla, also confirmed the accuracy of the information presented at the exhibit.

title: Lithium market update: Elevated prices are creating favourable dynamics for miners
summary: Driven by the rapid increase in electric vehicle (EV) adoption, battery-grade lithium carbonate prices reached an all-time high in October 2022. This surge in demand has outpaced lithium supply upgrades, leading to a projected supply deficit for several years and creating significant opportunities for mining companies. Major lithium producers like Albemarle, SQM, and Ganfeng are responding by announcing ambitious plans to expand their capacity, often supported by government incentives to build out EV supply chains.

summary: This article provides detailed information about the YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY), an exchange-traded fund launched in October 2022 that uses a synthetic covered call strategy on Tesla stock to generate income. It includes current pricing, key statistics such as dividend yield and expense ratio, and a list of recent news headlines regarding its weekly distributions. The article also offers insights into its holdings, major shareholders, and FAQs about its performance and how to purchase shares.

title: YieldMax Innovation Option Income Strategy ETF (OARK) Price, Holdings, & News
summary: This article provides detailed information on the YieldMax Innovation Option Income Strategy ETF (OARK), including its current price ($30.49), holdings, and recent news. OARK is an actively managed ETF that uses a synthetic covered call strategy on the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) to generate income and capped gains, collateralized by cash and US Treasuries. The fund has an expense ratio of 1.00% and a dividend yield of 64.55%, with its stock having decreased by 16.1% since the beginning of 2026.

title: TSLY Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:TSLY
summary: The YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY) aims to generate monthly income and provide exposure to Tesla (TSLA) stock price returns, subject to a cap on potential gains. Launched on November 22, 2022, TSLY uses a synthetic covered call strategy involving options and US Treasuries for collateral, but does not directly invest in TSLA stocks. The fund currently has $966.97 million in assets under management and an indicated dividend yield of 97.69%.
