summary: This article provides trade ideas and an in-depth analysis of the YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY). It details how TSLY generates income by selling TSLA options for premium, aiming for high dividend yields, and explains the mechanics of synthetic stock leverage. The article also outlines the risks and advantages of investing in TSLY, including its high yield, capital gain limitations, and sensitivity to TSLA's performance and volatility.

title: Technical Analysis of YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (AMEX:TSLY)
summary: This article provides a technical analysis of the YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY) based on various indicators. It details the summary of oscillators, moving averages, and pivots, categorizing them into buy, sell, or neutral signals. The overall technical rating for TSLY is currently a strong sell, emphasizing that this information is not investment advice and market conditions can change.

title: Tesla's Full Self-Driving Beta now available to all in N. America, Musk says
summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla's Full Self-Driving Beta software is now available to all North American customers who have purchased the option. This release comes as the automaker seeks regulatory approval for vehicles to operate without human oversight, with Musk hoping an FSD update in 2023 will demonstrate its safety advantage over human drivers. The $15,000 FSD add-on allows autonomous lane changes and parking, supplementing the standard Autopilot feature, while the company faces a U.S. Department of Justice investigation regarding claims its EVs can drive themselves.

title: Tesla owners are keeping GM service techs busy
summary: Tesla owners are reportedly bringing their vehicles to General Motors service centers for maintenance and repairs, keeping GM technicians busy. This article, published by Automotive News, highlights a surprising trend in the auto service industry.

title: TLT ETF Stock Price Today, News, Stock Analysis, Trading Ideas
summary: This article provides current stock information for the TLT ETF (iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF), including its price, recent performance, and trading volume. It also compiles news headlines related to TLT and broader market trends, particularly focusing on the impact of a US-Iran peace deal on oil prices, stocks, and Fed monetary policy. The content includes comparisons between TLT and other long-term bond ETFs, discussing factors like expense ratios and dividend yields.

title: Power to the People: How a single tweet could reignite a movement
summary: A fake tweet from an impersonating account claiming Eli Lilly was making insulin free went viral, significantly impacting the company's stock value and highlighting the potential for social media activism. This incident, enabled by changes to Twitter's verification system, sparked renewed debate on corporate greed, particularly regarding pharmaceutical pricing, and demonstrated how "internet trolls" could force corporations to address public concerns. The article suggests this event could reignite movements for social and corporate accountability.

title: Special Report: Electric Vehicles – Electric Energy
summary: This report details the growing electric vehicle market in the Los Angeles area, highlighting manufacturers like Xos Inc., Faraday Future, Karrior Electric Vehicles TransLectric, and BYD Motors. It discusses the challenges and opportunities in the EV sector, including operational cost savings for fleets, the need for more charging infrastructure, and anticipated industry consolidation. The article also touches on the unique products and strategies of these companies, from electric step vans to luxury EVs and industrial vehicles.

title: Tesla is still dominant, but its U.S. market share is eroding as cheaper EVs arrive
summary: Tesla remains the top-selling electric vehicle brand in the U.S., but its market share is declining as more affordable EV models from competitors enter the market. S&P Global Mobility reports Tesla's U.S. market share of new registered EVs was 65% through Q3, down from 71% last year, and forecasts it will drop to under 20% by 2025. This shift is attributed to the proliferation of cheaper alternatives with comparable technology.

title: No, you can’t buy a self-driving car yet, but a lot of people seem to think you can
summary: Despite widespread misconceptions, fully self-driving cars (Level 3-5 autonomy) are not yet available for purchase in Canada or the U.S. Many consumers mistakenly believe that current driver-assist technologies, like Tesla's Autopilot or GM's Super Cruise (which are Level 2), provide full self-driving capabilities, leading to dangerous misuse. Experts emphasize that drivers must remain attentive as these systems are only aids and not replacements for human operators, and more advanced systems are still in limited testing or decades away.

title: Tesla EV battery packs repurposed into energy storage systems in Finland and California
summary: Two companies, Smartville Inc. in California and Cactos in Finland, are repurposing Tesla EV battery packs into energy storage systems. Smartville received a US$6 million grant to commercialize its systems, while Cactos raised €2.5 million to expand production of its behind-the-meter ESS product. Both companies are scaling their operations to meet the growing demand for energy storage, with Smartville focusing on entire battery packs and Cactos using both second-life and new batteries to manage supply and demand.

title: Spotify, Epic Games get ally in Musk in fight against Apple fees
summary: Elon Musk has joined Spotify and Epic Games in criticizing Apple's 30% App Store fees, even suggesting Apple threatened to remove Twitter from its store. This stance strengthens the position of companies previously involved in antitrust complaints and lawsuits against Apple over its in-app purchase policies. Analysts are concerned that Musk's battle with Apple could deter Twitter users, as people are unlikely to abandon their iPhones.

title: Tesla Delivers Semi Trucks to PepsiCo, Expanding Beyond Passenger Vehicles
summary: Tesla Inc. delivered its first all-electric semitrailer trucks to PepsiCo Inc. on Thursday, marking a significant expansion beyond its traditional passenger vehicle market. This delivery comes five years after Elon Musk initially revealed the Semi model, which was originally due out in 2019. The Semi represents the first new model Tesla has put into customer hands since early 2020.

title: ADS-TEC Energy Launches New Ultra-Fast Charging System ChargePost, an Energy Platform With Integrated Battery Storage and Large Digital Displays
summary: ADS-TEC Energy has launched ChargePost, a compact, battery-based, all-in-one system for ultra-fast EV charging. This system integrates battery storage, power electronics, cooling, and charger, requiring minimal ground space and connecting to existing power grids, eliminating the need for extensive grid expansion. ChargePost also features optional large digital displays for advertising and can function as an energy platform, offering bidirectional charging capabilities by the first half of 2023.

title: Alta Equipment Group launches Alta eMobility business to provide fleet electrification solutions
summary: Alta Equipment Group has launched Alta eMobility, a new business dedicated to providing comprehensive fleet electrification solutions. This segment will manage all aspects of converting truck fleets and heavy equipment to electric power, from securing funding to ongoing maintenance. Alta eMobility will also serve as a key dealer and service provider for Nikola tractors in specified regions, handling sales, service, commissioning, and infrastructure installation.

title: Tesla to issue software updates for 435,000 cars in China over marker light issue
summary: Tesla will issue software updates for over 435,000 vehicles in China to fix an issue with side marker lights that could potentially lead to collisions. This fix is considered a recall and will be implemented via an over-the-air update, affecting Model 3 and Model Y cars. This follows a previous recall for over 80,000 vehicles in China for other software and seat belt issues.

title: Honda Unveils Next-generation Technologies of Honda SENSING 360 and Honda SENSING Elite
summary: Honda announced the next-generation technologies for its Honda SENSING 360 and Honda SENSING Elite safety and driver-assistive systems. These advancements aim to further reduce driver burden and prevent collisions by incorporating new functions and utilizing AI technologies for extended applicability, including non-expressways. Honda also outlined targets to equip all new automobile models globally with Honda SENSING (including 360 and Elite with motorcycle detection) by 2030, aiming to halve global traffic collision fatalities involving Honda vehicles and motorcycles by the same year.

title: 2 foreign-owned manufacturing facilities open in northern Mexico
summary: Two foreign-owned manufacturing facilities have opened in northern Mexico: an Irish plastics company, Mergon Group, near Saltillo, Coahuila, and a U.S. medical technology company, BD, in Tijuana, Baja California. Mergon invested 15 million euros to create 150 jobs making plastic components for electric vehicles, while BD's $38.6 million facility will produce medical devices, adding 500 jobs over two years. These openings highlight northern Mexico's appeal to manufacturers due to its proximity to the U.S. and affordable labor.

title: Ford claims No. 2 spot in EVs behind Tesla – but gap remains wide
summary: Ford has claimed the No. 2 spot in U.S. electric vehicle sales, surpassing Hyundai/Kia, though it remains a distant second to market leader Tesla. Despite this achievement, the gap with Tesla is significant, and Ford's overall November sales were down. Tesla's market share in EVs is decreasing as more competitors enter the market, with General Motors also aiming to overtake Tesla in EV sales by mid-decade.

title: Workhorse Group Inc. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: Workhorse Group Inc. (WKHS) stock increased by 4.31% on Friday, closing at $2.42, outperforming both the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the NASDAQ Composite Index. This marked the third consecutive day of gains for the company's stock, though it remained $3.17 below its 52-week high. The stock also outperformed competitors like Tesla Inc. while General Motors Co. declined.

title: Tesla expands with the first electric Semi-truck to PepsiCo
summary: Five years after its prototype reveal, Tesla delivered its first electric Semi-truck to PepsiCo\'s Frito-Lay in Modesto, California. PepsiCo has reserved 100 trucks and plans to deploy 15 by year-end, aiming to reduce fuel costs and emissions. Tesla CEO Elon Musk projects significant cargo transportation cost decreases and safety boosts, with a tentative plan to produce 50,000 Semis for North America in 2024.

title: How suite of dividend growth ETFs brings quality to the fore
summary: In an environment of market volatility and economic uncertainty, CI WisdomTree ETFs offer a quality-focused core portfolio solution that has outperformed benchmarks. These dividend growth ETFs, managed by CI Global Asset Management, employ a unique methodology to identify companies with strong fundamentals, sustainable earnings, and resilient business models, screening for quality and growth metrics. This strategy aims to provide diversified large-cap exposure and long-term stability by avoiding overvalued companies and focusing on profitable dividend payers, proving particularly effective during periods of economic contraction.

title: Polestar 2 Electric Vehicle achieves 5-Star Safety Rating from US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
summary: The Polestar 2 electric vehicle has received a 5-star overall safety rating from the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), the highest possible score. This achievement follows its 5-star EuroNCAP rating and highlights Polestar's commitment to safety, building on Volvo Cars' legacy with advanced protective and preventive technologies. The article also provides an overview of Polestar Automotive Holding UK PLC, its vehicle lineup, and future plans.

title: BorgWarner to spin off fuel systems, aftermarket business in EV pivot
summary: BorgWarner announced its plan to spin off its fuel systems and aftermarket businesses into a new publicly traded company by late 2023. This strategic move aims to allow BorgWarner to focus entirely on electric vehicle propulsion, aligning with its "Charging Forward" strategy and significant investments in EV technology. The new entity, temporarily named "NewCo," will continue to operate in internal combustion engine systems and alternate fuels, boasting substantial projected revenues and operating margins.

title: Janitors set up picket line after being fired by Twitter in latest attack by billionaire owner Musk
summary: Janitors at Twitter's San Francisco headquarters began picketing after being fired without notice due to a terminated contract with their building maintenance contractor, FlagShip. The 48 affected janitorial workers, members of SEIU Local 87, are demanding rehire and compensation, highlighting that San Francisco law often requires existing workers to be hired for 90 days after a contractor switch. This incident is the latest in a series of workforce reductions and changes at Twitter following Elon Musk's acquisition, which has included significant layoffs and a demand for an "extremely hardcore" work environment.

title: Tesla launches EVs in Thailand amid competition from cheaper brands
summary: Tesla Inc. has launched two electric vehicle models in Thailand, marking its first entry into the market previously dominated by Japanese automakers. The move comes as Thailand promotes EV adoption through tax cuts and subsidies, but Tesla faces strong competition from Chinese brands offering more affordable options. Tesla did not disclose sales targets, as Thailand aims for 30% of its vehicle production to be electric by 2030.

title: Lucid Motors Offers Discounts as Demand Shrinks
summary: Lucid Motors is offering significant discounts to attract customers and employees as its order numbers dropped to 34,000 in September and production goals for 2022 were not met. The discounts include 10% for reinstating lapsed orders, an $18,000 employee discount on the Grand Touring model, and a 2.81% in-house financing rate for ready-made units. This strategy aims to boost sales and generate cash flow as the company faces a competitive EV market with high production costs and falling stock prices.

title: ST SiC power modules for Hyundai EV platform ...
summary: STMicroelectronics' SiC-MOSFET based power modules have been chosen by Hyundai Motor Company for its E-GMP electric vehicle platform, specifically powering the Kia EV6. These modules offer flexible power ratings, support common EV traction operating voltages, and feature robust sintering technology for integration. ST's third-generation SiC technology aims to provide high power density, energy efficiency, and improved vehicle performance, range, and charge time.

title: Workers at E.V. Battery Plant in Ohio Vote to Unionize (Published 2022)
summary: Workers at Ultium Cells, a joint venture between General Motors and LG Energy Solution in Ohio, have voted to unionize with the United Automobile Workers (U.A.W.). This 710-to-16 vote marks a significant step for the auto union in organizing electric vehicle manufacturing, especially as the industry transitions away from traditional internal combustion engines. President Biden lauded the outcome, emphasizing his administration's goal for American union workers to lead in E.V. manufacturing.

title: Tesla to suspend Model Y output in Shanghai in last week of Dec-memo
summary: Tesla plans to suspend Model Y production at its Shanghai plant between December 25 and January 1, reducing output by about 30% for the month. This planned suspension is unusual for the factory, which usually operates normally at year-end, and follows earlier reports of production cuts due to elevated inventory levels. Despite record sales in November and recent price cuts, weakening demand and increased inventory in China appear to be factors for the adjustment.

title: Kwang Yang looking to unseat Gogoro by 2024
summary: Kwang Yang Motor Co aims to overtake Gogoro Inc as Taiwan's leading electric scooter vendor by 2024, driven by increasing brand awareness and sales of its new Ionex Air model. The company plans to expand internationally, focusing on India and Europe, while overcoming challenges like chip shortages and establishing brand recognition as a market newcomer.

title: Exclusive: Toyota to outline 3-year EV plan changes to suppliers
summary: Toyota Motor Corp is set to announce adjustments to its electric vehicle strategy to major suppliers early next year, aiming to compete more effectively with industry leaders like Tesla and BYD on price and performance. The changes, which cover the period until early 2026, include accelerating the adoption of performance-enhancing technologies for EVs and potentially delaying some original development programs. Toyota is also reviewing its e-TNGA platform, considering a dedicated EV platform instead, to improve cost performance and technology in the rapidly expanding EV market.

title: Questions arise on whether more is better in PRT market
summary: The article questions the current state of the pension risk transfer (PRT) market, highlighting concerns raised by Sen. Chris Murphy regarding outdated Department of Labor guidance. The sentiment revolves around whether an increased volume in PRT translates to improved outcomes for workers or introduces new risks due to regulatory stagnation.

title: Exclusive: Zeekr, a premium Geely electric car brand, seeks over $1 billion in U.S. IPO - sources
summary: Zeekr, Geely's upmarket electric car brand, has confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering, aiming to raise over $1 billion and seeking a valuation exceeding $10 billion. This would be the first major Chinese IPO in the U.S. in over 18 months, following a landmark auditing deal between Beijing and Washington. Zeekr plans to expand into Europe next year, highlighting Geely's complex EV strategy with seven brands manufacturing electric vehicles.

title: Rivian Scraps Plan to Make Electric Vans in Europe With Mercedes
summary: Rivian Automotive Inc. has scrapped its plans to jointly build electric vans in Europe with Mercedes-Benz AG, just three months after signing a memorandum of understanding. CEO RJ Scaringe stated that focusing on its consumer and existing commercial businesses represents the most attractive near-term opportunities for Rivian. This decision marks another setback for Rivian's global ambitions and follows a previous abandoned partnership with Ford Motor Co.

title: U.S. finalizes $2.5 billion loan to GM, LG battery joint venture
summary: The U.S. Energy Department announced the finalization of a $2.5 billion low-cost loan to Ultium Cells LLC, a joint venture between General Motors Co and LG Energy Solution. This loan will fund three new lithium-ion battery cell manufacturing facilities in Ohio, Tennessee, and Michigan, creating 6,000 construction jobs and 5,100 operations jobs. The initiative supports President Biden's goal for 50% of U.S. auto production to be electric or plug-in hybrid vehicles by 2030 and GM's plan to produce 1 million EVs in North America by 2025.

title: GM, Stellantis rank as worst automakers for fuel efficiency, even amid EV push, EPA says
summary: General Motors and Stellantis were identified by the EPA as having the worst average estimated real-world fuel economy and highest carbon emissions among major automakers for the 2021 model year. Both companies saw a decline in fuel efficiency and an increase in CO2 emissions since 2016. This report comes as the Biden administration pushes for a transition to electric vehicles, with GM aiming for an all-electric consumer fleet by 2035, despite their current fleet's poor efficiency.

title: As GM Installs Thousands of Electric Charges, Watch This ETF
summary: General Motors plans to install 40,000 electric vehicle chargers, primarily in rural areas, to support its goal of selling only zero-emission passenger vehicles by 2035. This significant infrastructure expansion nearly doubles the current number of charging stations in America, highlighting the rapid growth in the EV sector. Investors can capitalize on this trend through ETFs like the Direxion Daily Electric and Autonomous Vehicles Bull 2X Shares (EVAV), which provides leveraged exposure to companies involved in electric and autonomous vehicles and their supporting infrastructure.

title: How Well Do Electric Cars Work in Cold Weather?
summary: Electric vehicles experience a significant drop in driving range in cold weather, primarily due to natural battery capacity loss and increased energy demand for heating the cabin. Drivers can mitigate these effects by preheating the battery and cabin while still plugged in, planning trips with charging stations in mind, and utilizing features like heat pumps and energy-efficient drive modes. Understanding these limitations and taking precautions can help EV owners manage their vehicles effectively during colder seasons.

title: Albemarle Corporation Selects Mecklenburg County for Advanced Lithium Technology Park
summary: Albemarle Corporation is investing $200 million to establish an advanced lithium technology and R&D center in Mecklenburg County, creating 205 jobs. This move reinforces the region's position as a leader in electric vehicle innovation and clean energy, with the new facility focusing on next-generation lithium products and enhancing lithium recovery and production. The project is a collaborative effort involving several local and state entities, contributing significantly to capital investment and job creation in the area.

title: Tesla Investors Voice Concern Over Elon Musk’s Focus on Twitter
summary: Tesla investors are increasingly concerned that Elon Musk's focus on Twitter is negatively impacting the electric-vehicle maker. The company's stock is headed for its worst full-year performance amidst Musk's controversial takeover of Twitter. A major investor even tweeted that "There is no TSLA CEO today," reflecting the growing anxieties.

title: GraniteShares goes live with three leveraged single stock ETFs on NASDAQ
summary: GraniteShares has launched three new leveraged single-stock ETFs on the NASDAQ Stock Exchange, offering sophisticated investors 1.5x to 1.75x long exposure to Meta, Alibaba, and Nvidia. This expansion builds on GraniteShares' existing leveraged ETF offerings for Tesla, Coinbase, and Apple and aims to make leveraged single-company exposure, previously confined to specialists, accessible to a broader range of investors. Having pioneered the single-stock ETF market in Europe, GraniteShares is now bringing its expertise and popular product range to the U.S. market.

title: DI wealth advisor hits Wall Street, launches fund on NYSE
summary: Daniel Island resident Adam Curran, founder of Curran Financial Partners, has launched a new ETF on the NYSE called the "God Bless America ETF" under the ticker "YALL." The fund, valued at over $25 million, invests in American-based companies that prioritize profits over political activism. This achievement marks a lifelong dream for Curran, who plans to ring the NYSE bell in January to celebrate.

title: Elon Musk sold $3.6 billion more in Tesla stock, stoking fear that the carmaker is his ‘ATM’
summary: Elon Musk has sold an additional $3.6 billion in Tesla stock, raising fears among investors that he is using the carmaker as a personal "ATM" to fund his other ventures, particularly Twitter. This latest sale of nearly 22 million shares occurred between December 12 and December 14, causing Tesla shares to drop by 12.4% over three trading sessions. The ongoing stock sales and Musk's involvement with Twitter continue to be concerns for Tesla investors regarding operational and financial distractions.

title: What is Tesla?
summary: This article provides an overview of Tesla, detailing its history, product lines, and key figures. It covers the company's founding, its role as a pioneer in electric vehicles and energy storage, and the current ownership structure with Elon Musk as the largest shareholder. The article also addresses reasons for the recent decline in TSLA stock price, attributing it to investor concerns about Elon Musk's involvement with Twitter and his sale of Tesla shares.

title: G.M. Unit’s Self-Driving Taxis Are Subject of U.S. Safety Investigation (Published 2022)
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has launched a preliminary investigation into General Motors' Cruise division over reports of its self-driving taxis stopping unexpectedly or too quickly. This probe covers 242 vehicles and addresses concerns that such incidents could strand passengers in unsafe locations or create obstacles for other vehicles, increasing accident risks. While no fatalities or serious injuries have been reported with Cruise cars, this investigation marks a significant step in regulatory scrutiny of autonomous vehicle technology.

title: 2023 Kia EV6 GT Review: Affordable All-Electric Performance
summary: The 2023 Kia EV6 GT is reviewed as an affordable, high-performance all-electric SUV that excels in power, handling, and fun. It outperforms competitors like the Ford Mustang Mach-E GT Performance Edition and Tesla Model Y Long Range in acceleration and driving engagement, while also being significantly less expensive. Despite some comfort compromises in the cabin, the EV6 GT offers substantial performance thrills both on the street and track.

title: PepsiCo to roll out 100 Tesla Semis in 2023 for deliveries
summary: PepsiCo plans to deploy 100 heavy-duty Tesla Semis in 2023 for deliveries to major customers like Walmart and Kroger. The company is investing significantly in infrastructure, including charging stalls, supported by state grants and federal subsidies. Initially, the trucks will haul lightweight Frito-Lay products for longer distances and sodas for shorter routes, with plans to expand beverage delivery ranges as well.

title: Elon Musk’s troubling week pushes Tesla investors closer to the edge
summary: Elon Musk's controversial actions and management of Twitter have led to a significant 16 percent drop in Tesla's stock price over the last five sessions, marking its worst week since March 2020. Prominent Wall Street analysts have reduced their expectations for Tesla, and concerns about the economy and potential recession are expected to further impact demand for electric vehicles. This decline has pushed Tesla's market value below $500 billion, and analysts warn of further risks due to valuation and Musk's preoccupation with Twitter.

title: The Intersection 12-18-22
summary: This article, "The Intersection 12-18-22," highlights several key automotive industry stories. It covers a ruling regarding Trump's tariffs on vehicles and parts, the impact of tariffs on new-vehicle prices, dealership buy-sell updates including four Chevrolet stores, and Jeffrey Epstein's interest in Carlos Ghosn's arrest. The piece provides a snapshot of significant news from December 18, 2022.

title: Ford Motor has once again raised prices for the third time this year
summary: Ford Motor Company has increased the price of its F-150 Lightning Pro for the third time this year, raising the base model's MSRP by $16,000 to $55,974. The company attributes these price hikes to rising material costs, similar to other EV manufacturers like Tesla, Lucid, and Rivian. Despite the increases, Ford plans to expand production and anticipates increased demand due to the Inflation Reduction Act's tax benefits for electric commercial vehicles.

title: AJRD Stock Alert: What to Know as L3Harris Technologies Acquires Aerojet Rocketdyne
summary: Aerojet Rocketdyne (AJRD) stock is climbing due to a $4.7 billion acquisition deal by L3Harris Technologies (LHX), which will pay $58 per share in cash. This price represents a 37% premium to the unaffected share price before activist investor involvement. The deal is expected to close in 2023, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals, with Aerojet Rocketdyne continuing to operate as a provider of national security propulsion solutions.

title: Red-Hot Solar Stock Earns 'Top Pick' Status
summary: Goldman Sachs has named SolarEdge Technologies Inc (NASDAQ:SEDG) as a top pick for 2023 in the solar energy industry, alongside First Solar (FSLR). This endorsement comes despite the stock being down 1.1% recently, as SEDG has shown a 37% gain this quarter and boasts strong support from its 20-day moving average. Options traders have also been overwhelmingly bullish on SEDG in the past two months, as indicated by a high call/put volume ratio.

title: Tech short-sellers make $12bn betting against Tesla in 2022
summary: In 2022, short-sellers profited nearly $50 billion from betting against tech stocks, with Tesla being the most profitable target at $11.7 billion. This trend reflects a market shift from bullish to bearish, driven by high inflation and rising interest rates, leading to significant stock price declines for major tech companies like Amazon, Meta, and Apple. Despite the substantial sell-off, some analysts predict continued opportunities for short-sellers as tech valuations remain relatively high compared to historical averages.

title: Tesla (TSLA) Illegally Fired Workers for Criticizing Elon Musk, Complaints Claim
summary: Tesla is accused of illegally firing two California employees for criticizing CEO Elon Musk, according to complaints filed with the National Labor Relations Board. The employees were involved in drafting letters that objected to Musk's return-to-office policy and his tweets, which they claimed violated company policy. The filings suggest that these terminations were in violation of labor laws protecting employees' right to engage in such discussions.

title: Tesla fired workers for criticizing Musk, company policies, say new complaints
summary: Tesla is facing new complaints alleging the company illegally fired two employees for their involvement in drafting letters critical of the company and CEO Elon Musk. The workers claim their firings were intended to discourage other employees from speaking up about working conditions and company policies. Similar claims have been filed against SpaceX, another company owned by Musk.

title: New YieldMax ETFs Seek Covered Call Strategies on Tesla and ARKK
summary: Tidal Financial Group has launched two new actively managed ETFs, YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY) and YieldMax Innovation Option Income Strategy ETF (OARK), which employ a synthetic covered call strategy on Tesla (TSLA) and the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), respectively. These ETFs aim to generate monthly income for investors by capitalizing on the volatility of the underlying assets. This launch marks the first in a series of yield-producing ETFs under the YieldMax brand.

title: As Rhyolite Ridge lithium project advances, environmental activists plan fight
summary: A final environmental review is underway for the Rhyolite Ridge Lithium-Boron Project in Nevada, proposed by Australia-based Ioneer Ltd. This development follows the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service's decision to protect the rare Tiehm's buckwheat wildflower, which grows only on land where the mining operation is planned. Environmental activists are gearing up for a significant fight, claiming the mine poses an existential threat to the endangered plant, while Ioneer maintains its plan avoids direct impacts and is crucial for domestic lithium supply for electric vehicles.

title: Megatrends: Driving Toward Electric Vehicle Mass Adoption
summary: The electric vehicle (EV) market is projected for significant growth, with EVs expected to account for 90% of auto sales by 2050, driven by automaker investment, consumer demand, and supportive public policy. Long-term investors can find opportunities across three tiers: EV auto companies and battery manufacturers, key suppliers, and ancillary service providers, despite potential roadblocks like supply constraints and insufficient infrastructure. Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management division provides insights into investment strategies for this megatrend.

title: Tesla falls on growing angst over Musk's focus on Twitter
summary: Tesla shares fell nearly 6% after several brokerages cut price targets due to concerns over Elon Musk's focus on Twitter. Analysts fear Musk may need to sell more Tesla shares to fund Twitter, and the social media acquisition could harm Tesla's brand. This comes amid weakening demand in China and ahead of Tesla's quarterly deliveries report.

title: Purpose pushes through with yield-focused single-stock ETFs
summary: Purpose Investments has launched its initial suite of Yield Shares ETFs, which are single-stock, yield-focused ETFs. These world-first ETFs allow Canadian investors to gain exposure to individual stocks like Tesla and Apple while receiving enhanced monthly distributions through a covered-call options strategy and moderate leverage. The ETFs also address an advisor pain point by simplifying the process of generating augmented income from individual stocks and offer Canadian dollar-denominated exposure to U.S. stocks with currency hedging.

title: In EV race China leads world in higher sales, lower prices, more selection
summary: China is leading the global electric vehicle (EV) market with higher sales, lower prices, and a wider selection of vehicles, driven by government support and intense domestic competition. This has made EVs in China cheaper than gasoline cars and more affordable than comparable models in Europe and North America. Chinese automakers are increasingly seen as global leaders in the EV revolution, with this trend benefiting climate change efforts and Beijing's industrial planning goals, despite facing challenges like overcapacity and slim profit margins for individual manufacturers.

title: S&P Global Mobility Makes 2023 Light Vehicle Sales Forecast
summary: S&P Global Mobility forecasts global new light vehicle sales to reach nearly 83.6 million units in 2023, a 5.6% increase year-over-year, despite ongoing supply chain challenges, economic deterioration, and fading pent-up demand. The forecast remains cautious due to factors like semiconductor disruption, the Russia-Ukraine war, and an intensifying affordability squeeze. Electrification is expected to grow significantly, with battery electric vehicles projected to hit almost 10 million units in 2023.

title: I drove hundreds of miles 'hands-free' in GM, Ford and Tesla cars – here's how it went
summary: This article details a CNBC reporter's experiences test-driving the "hands-free" advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) from Tesla, General Motors, and Ford. While none of the systems are fully autonomous, the author found GM's Super Cruise to be the most consistent and best-performing on highways, followed by Ford's BlueCruise which still has areas for improvement, especially with curves and construction. Tesla's FSD Beta is noted as the most ambitious but also the most "nerve-wracking" on city streets, with communication issues and challenges in complex driving scenarios.

title: Toyota Boss Could Be Right About Electric Cars — Or Very Wrong
summary: Akio Toyoda, president of Toyota, believes that the auto industry has a "silent majority" who question the sole reliance on electric vehicles (EVs) and that a multi-pronged approach, including hybrids and hydrogen, is necessary. While Toyoda is right that climate solutions need diverse approaches and current EV infrastructure is lacking, his hesitation might cause Toyota to fall behind. Other major automakers are investing tens of billions in EVs, suggesting that despite current challenges, widespread adoption and infrastructure improvements are imminent, potentially leaving Toyota at a disadvantage if they don't fully commit to battery-electric technology.

title: Tesla owners didn’t buy a car: We bought a set of beliefs Elon is trashing
summary: The author, a Tesla owner, argues that buying a Tesla was an investment in a set of beliefs and a brand dedicated to doing good in the world, not just a car. However, Elon Musk's recent behavior, particularly since his acquisition of Twitter, has undermined these beliefs, causing disillusionment and embarrassment among many loyal customers and investors. The article details how Musk's erratic actions and political pandering are jeopardizing the strong brand loyalty Tesla had cultivated and leading to financial and emotional divestment from the company and its mission.

title: Micron To Reduce Workforce By Almost 5,000 Due to Plunging Demand
summary: Micron Technology Inc. announced it will cut 10% of its workforce, impacting nearly 4,800 positions, and suspend 2023 bonuses due to a significant downturn in demand for semiconductors and soaring inventories. The company reported a $195 million net loss in the first quarter of its 2023 fiscal year and expects rebalancing of customer inventory levels by mid-2023. This move follows similar workforce reductions by other tech giants like Meta and Snap amid a slowing global economy and inflation-related concerns.

title: New EV entrants disrupt Europe’s automotive market
summary: New Asian electric-vehicle (EV) manufacturers are rapidly entering the European market, employing diverse go-to-market strategies, and attracting significant consumer interest. These strategies range from fully-owned retail channels to various partnership models with importers and non-automotive retailers, driven by goals like customer experience control or speed to market. The article also provides nine key takeaways for these new entrants to succeed, emphasizing direct control over customer experience, strong online channels, data-driven targeting, community building, robust aftersales, flexible ownership models, fleet strategies, used car management, and critical partnerships.

title: Tesla Dangles $7,500 Discount in Rare Move to Boost Deliveries
summary: Tesla is offering a rare $7,500 discount on its Model 3 and Model Y vehicles for deliveries taken before year-end, signaling potential struggles with demand. This discount is double what was offered earlier in the month and aligns with anticipated changes in US tax credit eligibility for consumers. The move represents a departure from Elon Musk's previous stance against discounts and advertising.

title: The Tesla struggle is so real that the company is offering a $7,500 discount on cars—with one big catch
summary: Tesla is offering a rare $7,500 discount on its Model 3 and Model Y vehicles for customers taking delivery before the end of the year. This unusual move, departing from Elon Musk's long-standing no-discounts policy, suggests the automaker is facing demand challenges. The discount coincides with new federal EV tax credit guidance, which is expected to make many EVs eligible for the full $7,500 credit in early 2023, effectively accelerating a tax credit that buyers would likely receive next year.

title: Electric cars are taking off, but when will battery recycling follow?
summary: The article explores the nascent but critical industry of electric vehicle battery recycling, highlighting the challenges and opportunities for companies like Redwood Materials and Li-Cycle. Despite significant investment and the environmental necessity, the industry faces a shortage of used batteries for recycling for at least a decade, as most EVs on the road are new and batteries have long lifespans. The focus for now is on recycling manufacturing scrap, with a future shift towards end-of-life vehicle batteries.

title: Will XPeng's $140,000 Electric Flying Car Become the 'Tesla of the Flying Vehicle Industry'?
summary: XPeng's urban air mobility (UAM) business, AeroHT, demonstrated its gull-winged electric flying car, which could enter commercial production by 2025 with an estimated cost of $140,000. Unlike many eVTOLs, AeroHT's sixth-generation model is also a drivable car intended for road use over 90% of the time, flying only when necessary. The company aims to overcome regulatory hurdles and capture a share of the trillion-dollar urban air mobility market, with investors hoping it becomes the "Tesla of the flying car industry."

title: Elon Musk says he will not sell more Tesla stock for about two years
summary: Elon Musk has stated he will not sell any more Tesla (TSLA.O) stock for approximately two years, anticipating a "serious recession" in 2023. This announcement comes amid a significant sell-off of Tesla shares due to concerns about softening demand and Musk's focus on Twitter. Tesla shares rose in after-hours trading following his comments despite previous instances where Musk sold stock after similar pledges.

title: Tesla ups its discount on Model 3 and Model Y to $7,500
summary: Tesla has increased its discount on the Model 3 and Model Y to $7,500, following an earlier $3,750 discount, and is also offering 10,000 miles of free Supercharging. This move comes after significant price hikes earlier in the year and may be influenced by lagging demand and high inventory despite record vehicle deliveries. The $7,500 figure is notably the potential maximum federal EV tax credit amount for next year, though its applicability to Tesla vehicles after January is uncertain as new guidelines are expected.

title: Elon Musk's vow to not sell more Tesla stock fails to calm investors
summary: Elon Musk's pledge not to sell more Tesla stock for two years failed to reassure investors, as shares hit a new two-year low. This comes after Musk previously sold $40 billion worth of shares, partly to fund his acquisition of Twitter, despite similar past pledges. Investors are concerned about Musk's focus on Twitter and his history of issues with the SEC.

title: Nio unveils 500-kW ultra-fast charger that can charge EVs from 10% to 80% in 12 minutes
summary: Nio has introduced a new 500-kW ultra-fast charging pile capable of charging electric vehicles from 10% to 80% in as little as 12 minutes for 800V models and 20 minutes for 400V models. This charging technology is open to all EV brands and features a maximum charging current of 660A. The company specified that the new chargers, like its third-generation battery swap stations, will be operational by March 2023.

title: Tesla stopped reporting its Autopilot safety numbers online. Why?
summary: Tesla ceased reporting its Autopilot safety statistics online in 2021, around the same time the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) began collecting and releasing its own data. Critics suggest Tesla stopped reporting because its safety record, based on NHTSA numbers, appears to have worsened significantly compared to its sales growth and rivals like Ford and GM. The article also highlights the controversial nature of Tesla's past safety reports and the distinction between Autopilot and the more advanced, aspirational Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature, emphasizing that even FSD requires full human attention.

title: Cox Automotive Forecast: U.S. Auto Sales Expected to Finish 2022 Down 8% Year Over Year, as General Motors Reclaims Top Spot, Honda and Nissan Fall Significantly
summary: Cox Automotive forecasts that U.S. new-vehicle sales for 2022 will end at 13.9 million units, an 8% decrease from 2021, marking the lowest sales volume in a decade. While December sales saw a slight increase due to improved inventory, the full-year decline reflects challenges in both supply and, increasingly, demand, particularly exacerbated by rising interest rates and affordability concerns. General Motors is expected to reclaim the top sales spot from Toyota, while Honda and Nissan experienced significant declines, and Hyundai, Kia, and Tesla gained market share.

title: Better Buy: Rivian Stock or Lucid Stock?
summary: This article compares Rivian Automotive (RIVN) and Lucid Group (LCID) as long-term investment opportunities in the electric vehicle (EV) market. While both companies have seen significant stock price drops since their IPOs, the analysis concludes that Rivian appears to be the better buy due to higher production, increasing reservations, a stronger cash position, and a lower price-to-sales ratio compared to Lucid. However, the author cautions that the entire EV industry remains volatile due to rising material costs, supply chain issues, and potential recession impacts.

title: Tesla shares extend losses on demand worries in China
summary: Tesla shares fell sharply after a Reuters report indicated the company plans a reduced production schedule in January at its Shanghai plant due to demand concerns in China. Investors are also worried about CEO Elon Musk's time commitment to Twitter and his recent share sales, contributing to the stock's significant decline.

title: GlobalFoundries is cutting 50 workers at its former HQ in Santa Clara
summary: Chipmaking giant GlobalFoundries is laying off 50 staff members at its former headquarters in Santa Clara. This decision comes despite the company experiencing burgeoning sales and profits. GlobalFoundries had previously moved its headquarters out of California.

title: ERTH: Holding Up Well Despite Tesla Tanking (NYSEARCA:ERTH)
summary: The Invesco MSCI Sustainable Future ETF (ERTH) is a sustainability-focused fund with global holdings, which has demonstrated resilience despite a high concentration in electric vehicle stocks like Tesla. The article suggests that the ETF's diversification strategy has been effective in mitigating downside risks for investors interested in higher-risk asset classes. The author highlights the fund's broad range of holdings focused on sustainable operations and technologies, including unexpected top-10 holdings in net-zero focused data centers.

title: Musk tells Tesla workers not to be 'bothered by stock market craziness'
summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla Inc., urged employees not to be concerned by the company's significant stock decline, which saw shares fall nearly 70% this year amidst demand jitters and his involvement with Twitter. In an email, Musk expressed his belief that Tesla will ultimately be the most valuable company globally and pushed staff to prioritize deliveries to close out the quarter. This appeal came as analysts cut price targets for Tesla, forecasting a shift from supply exceeding demand to demand exceeding supply in 2023.

title: 2022, Year of Face-Ripping Bear-Market Rallies that Got Crushed
summary: The article describes 2022 as a year of "face-ripping bear-market rallies that got crushed," affecting indices like the Nasdaq and S&P 500. It highlights significant plunges in major tech stocks and compares the current market downturn to the Dotcom Bust, noting that the Nasdaq is not yet halfway to the 78% decline seen then. The author uses terms like "consensual hallucination" to describe the over-hyped market environment fueled by "free-money."

title: Cathie Wood's grim 2022 is almost over, but 2023 also looks bad
summary: Wall Street analysts are slashing earnings forecasts for major holdings in Cathie Wood's ARK Innovation ETF, portending continued challenges for the fund in 2023 after a difficult 2022. Despite a 67% year-to-date drop, ARKK still attracted $1.3 billion in inflows this year, though significantly less than previous years, indicating a dedicated base of long-term investors. The pessimistic outlook for tech stocks is part of a broader trend of trimmed S&P 500 earnings forecasts, driven by sustained high interest rates.

title: Occidental and Enphase Were Top Performing Stocks in 2022. Tesla Wasn't Last.
summary: The article identifies Occidental Petroleum as the top-performing stock in the S&P 500 for 2022, marking the end of a volatile year for the stock market. It suggests that while the year was challenging, there were still companies that saw significant gains, with Occidental leading the pack. This highlights the divergent performances within the market despite overall volatility.

title: Tesla Poised for Delivery Record Despite Demand Concerns
summary: Tesla is expected to announce record quarterly deliveries despite investor concerns over inflation, rising interest rates, and softening demand. The company offered a $7,500 discount and free Supercharging to U.S. customers at year-end, coinciding with the upcoming restoration of federal tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act. Analysts estimate fourth-quarter deliveries to be around 421,000 units.

title: Warren Buffett Surpassed Jeff Bezos in Wealth, May Overtake Bill Gates
summary: Warren Buffett has surpassed Jeff Bezos in wealth this year and is nearing Bill Gates' net worth, potentially making him the second-richest American after Elon Musk. This shift is attributed to the strong performance of Berkshire Hathaway stock compared to the declines seen in tech giants like Amazon, Microsoft, and Tesla. Despite significant charitable donations, Buffett's conservative investment strategy has proven resilient in the current economic climate, attracting investors away from growth stocks.

title: Could Cummins New B6.7H Hydrogen Powerplant Be The Future Of Ram Heavy Duty?
summary: This article explores the potential of Cummins' new B6.7H hydrogen internal combustion engine (H2-ICE) as a future powerplant for Ram Heavy Duty trucks. It highlights hydrogen as an alternative to battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) for towing and commercial use, addressing limitations like range anxiety and charging infrastructure. The piece details the B6.7H's capabilities, its seamless integration with existing diesel components, and its environmental benefits as a zero-carbon solution.

title: Baidu, Pony.ai start driverless robotaxi tests in Beijing
summary: Baidu and Pony.ai have secured the first licenses to test fully autonomous vehicles without safety operators in Beijing. Both companies will deploy 10 driverless vehicles each in a Beijing technology park, moving closer to commercial robotaxi services. Baidu, focusing on self-driving for diversification, aims for robotaxi rides to be half the cost of traditional commercial car rides and plans to expand its robotaxi network.
